summary: Seer setup check loading/error states not handled: orgHasAcknowledged defaults to false, indistinguishable from 'not acknowledged', causing misleading CTA during loading and deadlocked feature on API error
failure_scenario: User visits replay detail page. The seer setup check API is loading or returns an error (network failure, 503). setupAcknowledgement.orgHasAcknowledged stays false. The component shows the 'View Seer Settings' CTA instead of a loading/error indicator, and the summary query (useFetchReplaySummary) stays permanently disabled because its enabled condition requires orgHasAcknowledged===true. Even though the org already acknowledged Seer, the feature appears broken with a misleading CTA. The component should destructure and check isPending/isError from useOrganizationSeerSetup to differentiate 'still loading' and 'API errored' from 'genuinely not acknowledged'.

summary: useOrganizationSeerSetup() fires an unnecessary API request to /organizations/{slug}/seer/setup-check/ when only the synchronously-computed areAiFeaturesAllowed value is used
failure_scenario: FocusTabs component mounts and calls useOrganizationSeerSetup(), which triggers an API query with staleTime:0. The component only destructures areAiFeaturesAllowed (computed synchronously as !organization.hideAiFeatures && organization.features.includes('gen-ai-features')). The API response (billing, setupAcknowledgement) is never read. This causes an unnecessary network request on every mount and window refocus, and triggers an unnecessary re-render when the API resolves. The value could be computed locally: areAiFeaturesAllowed = !organization.hideAiFeatures && organization.features.includes('gen-ai-features'). If the API call is intentionally desired (e.g., to warm the cache for ai.tsx), pass {enabled: false} to useOrganizationSeerSetup to make intent explicit and avoid the wasted fetch.

summary: Missing try/finally in CancelCodingAgentButton.cancel: if cancelCodingAgent rejects, setBusy(false) is never called and the button spinner runs forever
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Cancel Coding Agent'. setBusy(true) fires, showing the spinner. The underlying cancelCodingAgent message-passing promise rejects (e.g., network fault, extension deactivation, timeout). The rejected promise unwinds without running setBusy(false). The button remains disabled with a spinning icon permanently until the webview is reloaded. The CheckoutButton.onClick in the same file (line 248) correctly wraps the async body in try/finally for exactly this reason.

summary: onHideAction is recreated every render; removeEventListener in the else branch passes a fresh function reference that never matches the one added, leaking click+keydown listeners on document with every open/close cycle
failure_scenario: User opens the dropdown (split-right click). Two listeners (click, keydown) are added to document via addEventListener wrapping the current render's onHideAction. User clicks outside to dismiss. The effect re-runs with expanded=false and calls removeEventListener with a newly-created function wrapping a newly-created onHideAction -- a different reference from the one that was added. The old listeners remain permanently. Repeat 50 open/close cycles: 100 leaked listeners fire on every document click/keydown (all no-ops, but waste memory and add per-event overhead). The effect also has no cleanup function returned, so listeners from the final expanded=true state survive component unmount.

summary: Class-level @persist checks for __is_flow_method__ but flow methods decorated only with @start()/@listen()/@router() lack this attribute, so class-level @persist silently wraps zero methods and never persists state
failure_scenario: User applies @persist at class level with @start()-decorated methods as documented — the loop at line 164 finds no matching methods because __is_flow_method__ is only set by method-level @persist, not by @start() which sets __is_start_method__. Result: flow state is never persisted despite the decorator being present. This is a pre-existing defect in code touched by the PR's refactoring of _persist_state to PersistenceDecorator.persist_state.

summary: Python closure captures loop variable 'method' by reference; all class_async_wrapper/class_sync_wrapper closures created in the for loop at line 164 would call the last iterated method instead of their intended method
failure_scenario: If class-level @persist matched multiple flow methods (e.g., after fixing the attribute-check bug), the for loop iterates methods A then B. Both wrappers capture `method` from the closure; when either wrapper is called, `method` resolves to B (the last value). Method A's wrapper erroneously calls method B. Pre-existing but the PR touches the code inside these closures (replacing _persist_state with PersistenceDecorator.persist_state at lines 175 and 182).

summary: Except (TypeError, ValueError) at line 124 catches ValueError('Flow instance has no state') raised at line 93 and replaces it with the generic 'id_missing' error message, masking the true cause
failure_scenario: A flow method decorated with @persist is called but the flow instance has no state attribute. At line 92 state is None, line 93 raises ValueError('Flow instance has no state'). This is caught by the broad except (TypeError, ValueError) at line 124 which substitutes LOG_MESSAGES['id_missing'] ('Flow state must have an id field for persistence'). The user sees a misleading error about a missing id when the real problem is that there is no state at all. This is a regression from the old _persist_state function which preserved the original message via str(e) in the RuntimeError.

summary: flow_id property returns 'None' (the literal string) when state's id key exists but holds None, because dict.get('id', '') returns the actual value (None) when the key exists, and str(None) produces the string 'None'
failure_scenario: A flow's state dict contains {'id': None, ...} (possible via _initialize_state with kwargs id=None or a persisted state that stored a null ID). Accessing flow.flow_id returns the string 'None' instead of an empty string, violating the documented contract that an empty string is returned when the id is not found. Downstream code checking for a truthy flow_id would be misled — 'None' is truthy unlike ''.

summary: paapiReplacer missing return in else branch causes TypeError crash when paapiDef is truthy but not an array or function
failure_scenario: A bid interception rule with paapi: 'invalid' (truthy string) passes through the array/func checks, logs an error, but returns undefined. When intercept() later calls match.rule.paapi(match.bid, bidRequest), it throws 'TypeError: match.rule.paapi is not a function'.

summary: intercept() calls addPaapiConfig unconditionally via forEach but JSDoc marks it optional -- throws TypeError if not provided and mockPaapi is non-empty
failure_scenario: Call intercept({bids: [...], bidRequest: {...}, addBid: fn, done: fn}) without addPaapiConfig when a matching rule has a non-empty PAAPI config array. mockPaapi.forEach(cfg => addPaapiConfig(...)) throws 'TypeError: addPaapiConfig is not a function'.

summary: normalizer inner function accesses cd[field] without null guard -- TypeError when consent data is null or undefined
failure_scenario: When no GPP section data exists for a state, getConsentData()?.parsedSections?.[api] evaluates to undefined, flatSection(undefined) returns undefined, and the normalizer's inner function executes cd[field] on undefined consent data, throwing 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined' at the Array.isArray(cd[field]) check.

summary: JSDoc return type changed from {knssoId} to {string|undefined} but getId returns an object {id: string}, not a string
failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc expect getId() to return a plain string or undefined; it actually returns {id: string} on success. Callers checking typeof result === 'string' would incorrectly treat a valid result as invalid.

summary: JSDoc @param {BidderRequest} bidderRequest added to getOpenRTBExtObject which takes zero parameters
failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc believe they must pass a bidderRequest argument; the function signature accepts none, so any passed argument is silently ignored. This is a documentation regression introduced by the PR.

summary: JSDoc says @param {Object} bid but the actual onTimeout function parameter is named timeoutData, not bid
failure_scenario: Developers reading the JSDoc reference the parameter as 'bid' in their mental model; the actual parameter name available at runtime is timeoutData. The previous JSDoc had the correct parameter name timeoutData; this is a regression introduced by the PR.

summary: Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls uses $MyInvocation.PSCommandPath to locate the script, which resolves to the caller's path under dot-sourcing, causing $packageRoot (and all derived paths: $sourceDir, solution path) to point to the wrong location silently
failure_scenario: Script is dot-sourced from <HOME>/helper.ps1 (a common pattern for reusing script functions) -> $MyInvocation.PSCommandPath inside Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls returns <HOME>/helper.ps1 -> $scriptDir = <HOME> -> $packageRoot = /home -> $sourceDir = <HOME>/generator (does not exist) -> all three DLL copy operations fail with 'Source DLL not found' warnings -> script continues and creates a debug profile pointing to empty/missing DLLs -> user tries to debug and dotnet fails with 'Cannot find assembly'

summary: DLL path constructed via string interpolation with hardcoded forward slashes produces mixed-separator paths on Windows when $resolvedSdkPath from Resolve-Path uses backslashes
failure_scenario: On Windows, Resolve-Path returns '<WINDOWS_USER_PATH>' -> $dllPath becomes '"<WINDOWS_USER_PATH>/TempTypeSpecFiles/node_modules/@azure-typespec/http-client-csharp/dist/generator/Microsoft.TypeSpec.Generator.dll"' -> the mixed-slash path embedded in the JSON launchSettings.json profile -> some path-consuming tools or scripts that post-process the launchSettings.json may fail to parse the non-canonical path

summary: Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls and Get-LaunchSettingsPath duplicate the same package-root computation from the script location using different approaches ($MyInvocation.PSCommandPath chain vs $PSScriptRoot + Resolve-Path), creating a maintenance hazard if the script moves or directory layout changes
failure_scenario: If the script is relocated from eng/scripts/ to a different depth (e.g., tools/), the Split-Path parent-chain logic on line 197 must be updated to match the new depth, but a developer might only notice and update one of the two locations (line 124 vs line 197) -> one function produces a wrong $packageRoot -> either launchSettings.json is written to the wrong file OR DLLs are copied from/to the wrong directory

summary: Missing test file (react-router.spec.tsx) -- violates CLAUDE.md rule requiring tests alongside components
failure_scenario: All 13 other JS framework docs in this directory have collocated .spec.tsx files. Without tests, regressions in the full onboarding flow (client setup, server setup, replay, feedback, profiling configs) for the React Router platform will not be caught by the test suite. CLAUDE.md lines 312-313 state: '5. ALWAYS colocate tests'.

summary: Missing featureFlagOnboarding in Docs export -- all 14 other JS framework docs include it
failure_scenario: javascript-react-router is included in featureFlagOnboardingPlatforms (derived filter) so the sidebar will open for this platform, but the loaded docs module lacks featureFlagOnboarding. The FeatureFlagOnboardingLayout falls back to docsConfig.onboarding (line 41 of featureFlagOnboardingLayout.tsx), so users get generic onboarding instead of platform-specific feature flag setup instructions. Every other JS framework doc (react, nextjs, remix, vue, angular, astro, ember, gatsby, nuxt, solid, solidstart, svelte, sveltekit, tanstackstart-react) includes this config.

summary: Unused import: 'Route' type imported but never referenced in getVerifySnippet
failure_scenario: The verify snippet imports 'import type { Route } from "./+types/error-page"' but the Route type is never used in the loader or component body. This dead import appears in the rendered documentation, potentially confusing users about whether Route is needed. Low severity but unnecessary code in a user-facing snippet.

summary: Hash fragment silently stripped from URLs that contain query parameters, while URLs without query parameters preserve their hash
failure_scenario: A user submits `https://example.com/page?ref=search#section-anchor` -- the preprocess returns `https://example.com/page?ref=search` with the hash fragment dropped. But `https://example.com/page#section-anchor` (no query params) falls through to `return x` on line 39 and keeps its hash. For SPAs using hash routing (React Router hash history) or pages where the hash anchors to a specific element, the scraper navigates to the wrong content.

summary: Embedded authentication credentials (user:password@) silently stripped because urlObj.origin excludes username and password
failure_scenario: A user submits `http://protected.example.com/data?format=json` to access a basic-auth-protected endpoint via URL credentials. The preprocess returns `http://protected.example.com/data?format=json` -- the credentials are dropped. The downstream HTTP request fails with 401 Unauthorized.

summary: URLSearchParams adds '=' to query parameters that have no explicit value, changing semantics for some server-side parsers
failure_scenario: A user submits `https://api.example.com/endpoint?debug&compact` where the target server treats bare keys as boolean flags (presence = true). After the preprocess, the URL becomes `https://api.example.com/endpoint?debug=&compact=`. Server frameworks like Express parse `?debug` as `undefined` (key present, no value) but `?debug=` as `""` (empty string). The scraped response differs because the server interprets the normalized parameters differently.

summary: Empty catch block swallows all exceptions from the try block, hiding errors from new URL() parsing failures and any programming mistakes
failure_scenario: A future code change introduces a typo or type error inside the try block (e.g., a mistyped property access on urlObj). The error is silently discarded by `catch (e) {}` with no logging, and the original `x` is returned. The bug goes undetected -- zod validation may or may not catch it downstream, and there is no error trace for debugging.

summary: Search query is silently dropped when credentials contain gmail.metadata scope alongside full-access scopes (e.g., gmail.readonly). The check uses membership (`in`) instead of verifying metadata is the exclusive scope.
failure_scenario: GmailReadBlock with query='is:unread', max_results=5; credentials.scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly','https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata'] -> query is not added to list() kwargs, the API returns all messages unfiltered instead of only unread.

summary: Message/thread format forced to 'metadata' (stripping email bodies) when gmail.metadata scope is present alongside full-access scopes. Same membership-check flaw: user has full read permission but gets empty bodies.
failure_scenario: credentials.scopes=['gmail.readonly','gmail.metadata']; GmailReadBlock or GmailGetThreadBlock calls messages.get() with format='metadata' -> all message bodies return 'This email does not contain a text body.' despite the user having full gmail.readonly access that supports format='full'. Same defect exists in _get_thread at line 592.

summary: _get_attachments crashes with KeyError on metadata-format messages because part['body']['attachmentId'] is absent in metadata-format API responses. The PR introduces metadata-format responses but does not guard attachment processing.
failure_scenario: Message with attachments fetched with format='metadata' (triggered by the scope-check defect above); _get_attachments iterates parts, finds a part with filename=True, then accesses part['body']['attachmentId'] -> KeyError because metadata-format body dicts only contain 'size', not 'attachmentId'. Same defect in GmailGetThreadBlock._get_attachments at line 658.

summary: No pagination on comment listing: listComments with only per_page=100 silently truncates at 100 comments, missing the existing marker comment on busy PRs and creating duplicate preview comments on every subsequent run.
failure_scenario: A PR accumulates more than 100 comments. The existing <!-- documentation preview --> marker comment falls beyond the first 100 fetched by listComments({ per_page: 100 }). The script finds no existing comment, so it creates a new one. Each subsequent workflow run repeats this, accumulating duplicate preview comments. The codebase standard pattern (used in cancel.js, labeling.js, protect.js, etc.) wraps the REST call with github.paginate() to exhaust all pages; this code does not.

summary: jq returns the literal string 'null' when netlify-cli --json output lacks a deploy_url field; the truthy string passes JS validation and produces a broken preview link in the comment.
failure_scenario: The netlify-cli deploy --json command succeeds but its JSON output lacks a deploy_url field (e.g., a version change in the CLI). jq -r '.deploy_url' outputs the literal string 'null'. DEPLOY_URL='null' is written as a step output. The deploy step outcome is 'success', so STAGE='completed'. In the JS code, the check !netlifyUrl evaluates to false (the string 'null' is truthy), so validation passes. The resulting PR comment contains 'Documentation preview is available at: - null' -- a broken, non-functional link.

summary: Record accepts only 2 type parameters, but 3 are provided (string, SearchResult['url'], QueryResult['query']), causing a TypeScript compilation error that prevents tsc from succeeding.
failure_scenario: Running `npm run build` (which invokes `tsc`) on this codebase fails with error TS2558: Expected 2 type arguments, but got 3. The return type annotation `Record<string, SearchResult['url'], QueryResult['query']>` should be `Record<string, string>` (the original type before this refactoring) — passing 3 generic arguments to the built-in `Record<K, V>` utility type is invalid TypeScript.

summary: Falsy-zero data loss: tier output mapping uses `|| undefined` which converts `unit_amount: 0` (meaningful free tier) to `undefined`
failure_scenario: User creates a tiered price with a free tier (`unitAmount: 0`). Stripe returns `unit_amount: 0` on the tier. The output mapping on line 483 evaluates `0 || undefined` as `undefined`, so the returned Price object shows no `unitAmount` for that tier. Downstream code (e.g., billing calculations, UI display of tier rates) treats the tier as having no unit price, billing customers incorrectly or displaying incomplete pricing information. The same `||` pattern on line 481 affects `flat_amount: 0` -- a tier capped at $0 charge (e.g., 'no further charges beyond this tier') would silently lose that information.

summary: Validation gap: `props.unitAmount || props.unitAmountDecimal` uses truthiness check, bypassing the 'cannot set both tiers and unitAmount' validation when `unitAmount` is `0`
failure_scenario: User specifies `tiers: [{ upTo: 100, unitAmount: 500 }]` and also `unitAmount: 0`. The validation on line 351 evaluates `0 || undefined` (falsy), so no error is thrown. The code proceeds to send both `tiers` and `unit_amount: 0` to Stripe (line 391: `if (props.unitAmount !== undefined)` sets `unit_amount: 0`). Stripe rejects the request with a cryptic API error like 'You cannot set both unit_amount and tiers' instead of the helpful `Cannot set both tiers and unitAmount/unitAmountDecimal` message the validation was intended to provide.

summary: Compilation error: parameter renamed from 'object' to 'target' but body still references undeclared 'object' in UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetDouble() call
failure_scenario: `javac` rejects the file -- method signature says `getDouble(Object target)` but line 48 uses `UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetDouble(object, getOffset())` where `object` is no longer declared. Compilation fails.

summary: Compilation error: parameter renamed from 'object' to 'target' but body still references undeclared 'object' in UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetInt() call
failure_scenario: Same pattern as DoubleFieldInfo -- `javac` rejects the file. `getInt(Object target)` tries to use `UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetInt(object, ...)` with an undeclared symbol.

summary: Compilation error: parameter renamed from 'object' to 'target' but body still references undeclared 'object' in UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetLong() call
failure_scenario: Same pattern -- `javac` rejects the file. `getLong(Object target)` tries to use `UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetLong(object, ...)` with an undeclared symbol.

summary: Compilation error: parameter renamed from 'object' to 'target' but body still references undeclared 'object' in UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetChar() call
failure_scenario: Same pattern -- `javac` rejects the file. `getChar(Object target)` tries to use `UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetChar(object, ...)` with an undeclared symbol.

summary: Compilation error: parameter renamed from 'object' to 'target' but body still references undeclared 'object' in UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetObject() call
failure_scenario: Same pattern -- `javac` rejects the file. `get(Object target)` tries to use `UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetObject(object, ...)` with an undeclared symbol.

summary: TupleFieldInfo.set() primitive overloads (char/int/long/double) call set(name, ...) instead of set(target, ...), dropping the target object and using the String field name as the target -- causes Proxy.getInvocationHandler() to throw on every primitive set
failure_scenario: Calling `TupleFieldInfo.set(someProxy, 42)` on an int field enters `set(Object target, int value)` which calls `set(name, (Object) value)`. The inherited `set(Object, Object)` then calls `getMap(name)` which invokes `Proxy.getInvocationHandler("someFieldName")` on a plain String -- throws `IllegalArgumentException` because String is not a proxy. All primitive set operations on TupleFieldInfo crash at runtime. (This is a pre-existing bug that the diff touches but does not fix.)

summary: Javadoc corruption from over-aggressive search-and-replace: 'write field newValues' should be 'write field values'; 'FieldInfo targets/FieldInfo target' should be 'FieldInfo objects/FieldInfo object'; 'Returns the newValue of the field' should be 'Returns the value of the field'; 'source target to the destination target' should be 'source object to the destination object'
failure_scenario: Javadoc generation produces nonsensical documentation (e.g., 'and write field newValues' at line 35, 'FieldInfo targets' at line 71, 'Returns the newValue of the field' at line 137, 'source target to the destination target... targets will be copied' at lines 237-238, 'in two targets' at line 283). Readers are confused by documentation that reads like a failed find-and-replace.

summary: Javadoc `@param o` does not match the renamed parameter `target` in getMap(Object target) -- produces Javadoc warnings and misleading documentation
failure_scenario: The method signature is `getMap(Object target)` but the Javadoc says `@param o The object whose fields map needs to be fetched.` Javadoc toolchain (javadoc -Xdoclint) emits a warning about unmatched @param tag. The documentation references a parameter name `o` that no longer exists.

summary: totalCount uses count(*) (all result rows) but filteredCount uses COUNT(DISTINCT test_idx) — mismatched units displayed as 'X of Y results' in the UI
failure_scenario: An eval with 10 test cases and 3 prompts per case produces totalCount=30 (result rows) but filteredCount=10 (distinct test indices). The UI shows '10 of 30 results' even though there are only 10 test cases.

summary: numTests defined as testPassCount + testFailCount, excluding testErrorCount — inflates pass rate, per-test cost, avg tokens, and avg latency in the header
failure_scenario: An eval with 80 pass / 10 fail / 10 error results displays '88.89% passing (80/90 cases)' instead of '80% passing (80/100 cases)', and per-test cost is inflated by dividing total cost by 90 instead of 100.

summary: When filteredResultsCount is 0, pageCount = 0 and maxPageIndex = -1, allowing safeRowPageIndex = -1 and a negative pagination.pageIndex
failure_scenario: URL contains rowId parameter while filters produce zero results. pagination.pageIndex is set to -1, which React Table's manual pagination does not handle — could cause rendering errors or infinite loops.

summary: setEvalId(id) called before fetchEvalData; on fetch failure, evalId is left pointing to the failed eval while table/config may be stale from a previous successful load
failure_scenario: User navigates to eval A (loads correctly), then to eval B (fails/404). Store keeps evalId=B but table/config from eval A. UI shows eval A's data labeled as eval B, and subsequent operations use the wrong evalId.

summary: testCaseMetadataIdx indexes json_extract(metadata, '$') instead of json_extract(test_case, '$.metadata'), and is duplicated by metadataIdx on line 137 — search on test_case.metadata has no index coverage
failure_scenario: Search queries filtering on test_case metadata ('json_extract(test_case, $.metadata) LIKE %...%') get no index assistance, causing full table scans. The two duplicate indexes on json_extract(metadata, '$') waste storage and write overhead.

summary: Header stats read prompt.metrics from server, which are absent for evals created before this PR — old evals display '0.00% passing (0/0 cases)' with zero token/cost/latency stats
failure_scenario: A user views an eval created before the PR deployment. The eval's saved prompts have no metrics object. All header stats show 0 or empty values — '0.00% passing (0/0 cases)', $0.00 cost, 0 tokens, 0ms latency — despite valid results existing.

summary: BAMModerations interface drops the social_bias field and changes structure from {input: {enabled: boolean}} to {input?: boolean} — breaking existing BAM provider moderation configs
failure_scenario: A user has a promptfoo config with BAM provider and moderations: { social_bias: { input: { enabled: true, threshold: 0.7 } } }. After this change, social_bias is silently dropped from the API request, and the nested enabled boolean is no longer parsed correctly, disabling content moderation.

summary: comparisonEvalIds stored in zustand persist middleware survives page reloads — stale eval IDs from deleted evals cause all table requests to fail with 404
failure_scenario: User adds a comparison eval, closes the browser. Days later, that comparison eval has been deleted. On page reload, the stale comparisonEvalIds are sent to the /eval/:id/table endpoint. The server returns 404 for the entire request, and the main eval table also fails to load.

summary: Search debounce increased from 200ms to 1000ms, making search feel 5x slower with server-side processing on top
failure_scenario: User types a search query. Previously debounced at 200ms (near-instant feedback), now debounced at 1000ms (1-second delay) plus network round-trip. Combined with server-side search, total latency exceeds 1 second, degrading UX significantly.

summary: Grader.getResult now unconditionally passes goal instead of conditionally passing newInjectVar for intent plugin — combined with simplified IntentGrader rubric, this changes the evaluated prompt for intent-based red team tests
failure_scenario: An intent-based red team test with pluginId='intent' previously passed the dynamic newInjectVar (the crafted jailbreak prompt) to the grader. Now it passes goal (the high-level intent). Combined with the IntentGrader rubric change removing multi-turn context, the grader evaluates a different input, potentially producing different pass/fail results.

summary: getattr(target_sa, relation.back_populates) raises TypeError when back_populates is None for unidirectional relationships — a regression from the old code which used session.get() + session.refresh() and did not require back_populates
failure_scenario: SQLAlchemy model defines orders: Mapped[list['Order']] = relationship() without back_populates. The auto-generated list resolver crashes with TypeError: getattr(): attribute name must be string because getattr(target_sa, None) is called.

summary: The pagination query select(target_sa).join(back_attr).where(primary_col == entity_id) has no ORDER BY clause, making paginated results non-deterministic — items can appear on different pages or be missed across requests
failure_scenario: A client calls page 1 (page_size=20) then page 2 on the same relationship resolver. Because the database returns rows in arbitrary order, item X appears on page 1 in the first call but also on page 2 in a subsequent call, or is entirely missed by both pages.

summary: For self-referential one-to-many relationships (e.g. Employee.subordinates), where(primary_col == entity_id) filters by the target table's own PK instead of the FK, returning the wrong entity — the old session.get() + getattr() approach handled this correctly
failure_scenario: Employee model with id, manager_id (FK to self), manager and subordinates relationships. Calling the subordinates resolver with entity_id=1 returns employee with id=1 (if they have a manager) instead of employees where manager_id=1.

summary: The mutable_crud/app.py example was removed from the EXAMPLES smoke-test list, losing automated regression coverage for this example
failure_scenario: A future change to EnrichMCP or EnrichModel breaks the mutable_crud example (e.g., removing a deprecated API it relies on). CI does not detect this because the example is no longer tested.

summary: All six CAT acceptance-test suites (spec, connection, discovery, basic_read, full_refresh, incremental) are now bypassed. Previously, spec, connection, discovery, and incremental ran real tests. This PR introduces a breaking config-schema change (single 'database' string to 'databases' array) with no integration-test validation.
failure_scenario: The spec backward-compatibility test (which validated expected_spec.json against the new multi-database schema) no longer runs. A mismatch between spec.json, expected_spec.json, and the config parsing code would go undetected until a user configures the connector.

summary: Hardcoded string literal "connection_string" used instead of the existing constant MongoDbDebeziumConstants.Configuration.CONNECTION_STRING_CONFIGURATION_KEY.
failure_scenario: If the constant value is ever changed (e.g. renamed to 'conn_string' for consistency), this line would silently break with a MissingNode result while all other code paths remain correct.

summary: New .filter() calls getNamespace().equals(...) without a null-guard; a stream with a null namespace would throw NullPointerException. Old code had no filter and would have processed such a stream.
failure_scenario: If a catalog contains a ConfiguredAirbyteStream whose AirbyteStream.getNamespace() returns null (due to an upstream bug or incomplete stream discovery), the filter throws NPE, crashing the initial snapshot phase. The old code would have skipped the filter and proceeded.

summary: Log message contains typo: 'save_id' should be 'server_id' to match the first half of the sentence which correctly references 'server_id'.
failure_scenario: Confusing log output during offset migration. An operator searching logs for 'server_id' would miss this message, delaying diagnosis of offset-migration issues.

summary: Dead commented-out code left behind: the old single-database pipeline construction. The new code uses Filters.or with ns.db matching, making these commented lines permanently dead.
failure_scenario: No runtime failure. Maintenance cost: a future developer wastes time wondering whether the commented code should be restored or whether it documents an alternative approach.

summary: CancellationToken is unsafely cast to AbortSignal, breaking test-run cancellation entirely
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Cancel' in the VS Code Test Explorer during a test run. The token is a vscode.CancellationToken with `isCancellationRequested` / `onCancellationRequested`, but Node's `child_process.exec()` expects `AbortSignal` with `aborted` / `addEventListener('abort', …)`. The signal mismatch means Node never detects the abort request; the subprocess keeps running and the cancel button has no effect. (The existing code in `sqlmesh.ts:239-240` already shows the correct pattern: create an `AbortController`, bridge via `token.onCancellationRequested(() => abortController.abort())`, and pass `abortController.signal`.)

summary: All tests in a run are marked with the same pass/fail status based on the aggregate exit code, misrepresenting individual test results
failure_scenario: Five tests run: four pass and one fails. The sqlmesh CLI returns exit code 1 (non-zero). The loop at lines 80-83 marks ALL five tests with `run.failed(t, …)`. The user sees every test as failed and cannot determine which single test actually broke. The stderr from the aggregate invocation is also smeared across all five test messages.

summary: setupTestController is called on every LSP restart, creating duplicate run profiles that are never disposed
failure_scenario: The user changes their Python interpreter (triggering a restart), then changes a VS Code setting (another restart), then manually runs 'sqlmesh.restart'. After three restarts, `controller.createRunProfile(…)` has been called four times total (once initially + three restarts) but only the last `resolveHandler` assignment is active. The Test Explorer UI shows four duplicate 'Run' buttons. Clicking any of them triggers multiple overlapping test runs, and the old run profiles are never disposed, leaking resources.

summary: Test name containing '::' breaks ID parsing, producing a malformed pattern that silently skips the test
failure_scenario: A SQLMesh test named `check::integrity` at `/project/models/test.sql` gets the TestItem ID `file:///project/models/test.sql::check::integrity`. Line 69 splits on `::` producing `['file:///project/models/test.sql', 'check', 'integrity']`. Destructuring captures only `uriStr='file:///project/models/test.sql'` and `name='check'`. The pattern passed to sqlmesh CLI becomes `/project/models/test.sql::check` which does not match `check::integrity`. The test is silently omitted from the run.

summary: No try/catch around execAsync; if it rejects (spawn failure), run.end() is never called and the test run remains stuck in 'running' state
failure_scenario: Between `sqlmeshExec()` succeeding and `execAsync()` executing, the sqlmesh binary becomes unreadable (permission change, filesystem race). `execAsyncCore` rejects via `child.once('error', reject)` and `execAsync` re-throws. Without a try/catch at line 74, the `runTests` async function rejects. `run.end()` on line 85 never executes. VS Code's Test Explorer shows the test run as perpetually 'running', and the user cannot start a new run without reloading the window.

summary: CLI crashes on --help and --version when API keys are not configured, because importing getResponse triggers module-level env var checks in config.ts before commander parses arguments
failure_scenario: User runs 'deepresearch --help' without setting JINA_API_KEY env var. Import chain cli.ts -> agent.ts -> config.ts executes line 137 'if (!JINA_API_KEY) throw new Error("JINA_API_KEY not found")' at module load time, crashing before commander outputs help text.

summary: 'main' field 'dist/index.js' points to a file that will never exist: no src/index.ts source file means tsc never creates dist/index.js, making the package unimportable
failure_scenario: User runs 'npm install node-deepresearch' followed by 'require("node-deepresearch")' or 'import ... from "node-deepresearch"'. Node resolves to dist/index.js which does not exist, producing MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The package also has no 'bin' field, so the CLI command cannot be invoked either.

summary: When evaluator deems answer definitive but references are missing and URLs are available, the code still sets isAnswered=true and breaks out of the loop, returning an unreferenced answer (pre-existing bug now exposed through the new CLI)
failure_scenario: Agent produces an answer the evaluator accepts (is_definitive=true) but without references. The condition on line 389 'thisStep.references?.length > 0 || Object.keys(allURLs).length === 0' is false (references.length is 0 and URLs exist). The else branch pushes a diary note about needing references, but execution falls through to line 421 'isAnswered = true; break', exiting the loop and returning the unreferenced answer. The agent should continue searching for references instead.

summary: parseInt(val) validation accepts inputs like '10abc' (returns 10) and '0x10' (returns 16), silently coercing garbage suffixes into numbers
failure_scenario: User runs 'deepresearch -t 50abc "query"' expecting an error for the invalid number. parseInt('50abc') returns 50, so the token budget is silently set to 50 instead of the intended 500000 or producing a validation error. Use Number(val) or val.match(/^\d+$/) for strict validation.

summary: jest.mock('../agent', ...) is dead code: all tests use execAsync which spawns child processes where the mock has no effect, and no test imports the mocked module directly
failure_scenario: A developer adds tests that call getResponse directly (not through execAsync), expecting the mock to intercept them. The mock is silently non-functional for the existing test pattern, and the tests pass only because real environment variables satisfy the module-load checks. If a future test relies on the mock, it will call the real agent with real API costs.

summary: GOOGLE_API_KEY env var is set from secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY (wrong secret name); the codebase never reads GOOGLE_API_KEY and always passes GEMINI_API_KEY explicitly to createGoogleGenerativeAI, making this mapping dead and misleading
failure_scenario: If future code changes rely on GOOGLE_API_KEY env var (e.g., using @ai-sdk/google's default credential resolution), it would silently receive the Gemini API key instead of a dedicated Google API key, potentially causing auth failures for non-Gemini Google services. Currently the mapping is harmless dead config copied from the existing test.yml.

summary: @types/commander ^2.12.0 is installed alongside commander ^13.1.0; commander v13 ships its own TypeScript types, and the v2 type definitions are for a completely different API surface, risking type conflicts
failure_scenario: TypeScript may resolve @types/commander's module declaration for 'commander' instead of commander v13's built-in types. The code currently works around this by typing options as 'any', but if someone adds typed option access, they would get v2-era types that don't match the v13 API (e.g., missing features, different method signatures).

summary: resp.tool_calls[0] unguarded: crashes with TypeError/IndexError when the model returns no tool calls in XAI_TOOLS mode
failure_scenario: An xAI model in XAI_TOOLS mode returns a response where resp.tool_calls is None or empty list (model declined to call a tool or returned text instead). Accessing resp.tool_calls[0] raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable (async path line 97) or IndexError (sync path line 136). The diff now adds _raw_response assignment immediately after this unguarded access, re-exposing the pre-existing crash path.

summary: validation_context is silently discarded in XAI_TOOLS path: None is hardcoded in _validate_model_from_json call
failure_scenario: A user passes validation_context with additional data for model validation (e.g., a dict of reference values for cross-field checks). The xAI create function pops validation_context from call_kwargs at line 75 (async) / line 114 (sync) and discards it. Line 100 / 139 then passes None to _validate_model_from_json(response_model, args, None, strict). A model validator that relies on validation_context will receive None instead of the user-provided data, causing misleading validation failures or silently weakened validation.

summary: create_with_completion is only tested with XAI_JSON mode, not XAI_TOOLS; the XAI_TOOLS path for create_with_completion has no test coverage
failure_scenario: If XAI_TOOLS mode has a bug where create_with_completion returns wrong or missing _raw_response, existing tests won't catch it because test_xai_create_with_completion (line 167) and test_xai_create_with_completion_async (line 200) only use Mode.XAI_JSON. No test exercises the XAI_TOOLS path through create_with_completion.

summary: Cache key in _check_cache omits tool_choice, causing cache collisions across different tool_choice values
failure_scenario: Call create(messages=[...], tools=[t], tool_choice='required') to populate the cache, then call create(messages=[...], tools=[t], tool_choice='none') with identical other inputs. The second call hits the cache and returns the result computed under 'required' (which may contain tool calls), instead of a text-only response as 'none' intends.

summary: Ollama _process_create_args does not validate that a Tool-valued tool_choice is in the provided tools list, and does not raise an error when tools is empty
failure_scenario: Call create(messages=[...], tools=[tool_a, tool_b], tool_choice=tool_c) where tool_c is a Tool not in the tools list. The Ollama client silently sends tool_c to the API without the other tools. The API may return a confusing error or silently use the wrong tool. Other clients (OpenAI, Anthropic) raise a clear ValueError in this case.

summary: Azure AI create and create_stream do not validate that a Tool-valued tool_choice is in the provided tools list
failure_scenario: Call create(messages=[...], tools=[tool_a], tool_choice=tool_b) where tool_b is not in tools. The Azure client sends a ChatCompletionsNamedToolChoice referencing tool_b along with tools=[tool_a]. The Azure API will either reject this as an invalid tool_choice (because tool_b's definition was never sent) or behave unpredictably.

summary: Dead code: convert_tool_choice_anthropic never returns None, so the guard 'if converted_tool_choice is not None' is always True
failure_scenario: No runtime failure, but the misleading guard suggests to future maintainers that None is a possible return value. If the function is later modified to return None for some case, the Anthropic create and create_stream would silently drop tool_choice from the request, causing subtle behavior changes.

summary: Duplicate tool_choice validation logic (~20 lines) copy-pasted between create (lines 611-632) and create_stream (lines 811-832) with only variable-name differences
failure_scenario: A bug fix or enhancement applied to one copy could be missed in the other. For example, a new validation rule added only to create would silently be absent from create_stream, allowing invalid tool_choice values through the stream path.

summary: Navigator-based language fallback detection is dead code -- unconditionally unreachable because the preceding block always writes to localStorage, making the subsequent localStorage read always truthy
failure_scenario: N/A (dead code, not a runtime bug): the first block (lines 63-69) always executes localStorage.setItem for either zh-Hans or en-US on both branches; the localStorage.getItem on line 72 always retrieves that value; the if (lang) branch on line 73 always executes; the else branch (navigator detection) on lines 77-89 never runs. If someone modifies the first block without understanding this dependency, the navigator fallback could silently stop working

summary: Same dead navigator-based language fallback detection as login -- the preceding block's unconditional localStorage write makes the navigator fallback code unreachable
failure_scenario: Same as above: lines 62-68 always write to localStorage; line 71 always reads a truthy value; the else block at lines 76-89 never executes

summary: Debug console.log statements left in production code -- language state and handler values logged to browser console
failure_scenario: Lines 72, 85, and 94 log runtime language state to the browser console in all environments; these debug statements should have been removed before merge. Not a crash or user-facing bug, but indicates incomplete cleanup and leaks internal state

summary: judgeLanguage and handleLanguageChange logic is copy-pasted from the register page with only minor differences -- duplicated code between both authentication pages
failure_scenario: Any fix or enhancement to language detection (e.g., adding support for zh-TW, updating the fallback logic, fixing the dead code) must be applied in both login/page.tsx and register/page.tsx independently, creating a maintenance burden and risk of divergent behavior

summary: Unicode and non-ASCII characters are silently stripped from folder_name and class_name, corrupting valid names like 'café' into 'caf'/'Caf' with no warning.
failure_scenario: User runs 'crewai create crew café' — folder is created as 'caf' with class name 'Caf' instead of the expected 'café'/'Café'. The regex [^a-zA-Z0-9_] strips valid Python identifier characters (accented letters, Cyrillic, CJK, etc.) from names that start with an ASCII letter. Names starting with a non-ASCII character are caught by line 29 and rejected, but names starting with ASCII and containing non-ASCII characters are silently corrupted.

summary: The 'name' argument passed to copy_template is the raw CLI input (unsanitized), leaking trailing slashes and other unvalidated characters into generated README.md and pyproject.toml via the {{name}} placeholder.
failure_scenario: User runs 'crewai create crew my-project/' — create_folder_structure correctly strips the trailing slash from folder_name (my_project) and class_name (MyProject), but create_crew passes the original 'my-project/' string as the 'name' arg to copy_template. The generated pyproject.toml gets 'description = "my-project/ using crewAI"' and README.md gets 'The my-project/ Crew is composed of...'. The {{folder_name}} and {{crew_name}} placeholders are correctly cleaned; only {{name}} is affected.

summary: Premature validation against the raw name (before character stripping) rejects names that would produce valid Python identifiers after cleaning, with a factually incorrect error message.
failure_scenario: User runs 'crewai create crew .myproject' — the name starts with '.' which is not in [a-zA-Z0-9_-], so the check on line 29 matches and raises ValueError('Project name ".myproject" contains no valid characters for a Python module name'). However, after the re.sub cleaning on line 26, folder_name would be 'myproject', which IS a valid Python module name. The error message is factually wrong (the name contains valid characters) and the rejection is inconsistent with the function's own cleaning logic.

summary: Hardcoded test credentials (token and email) are set in localStorage whenever the HomeSidebar mounts without an existing token, bypassing the authentication flow.
failure_scenario: A user navigates directly to /home without authenticating first (no middleware guards the route). The useEffect on mount detects no token and sets token='test-token' and userEmail='test@example.com'. Subsequent API requests from any home sub-page send Authorization: Bearer test-token, which is either rejected as invalid by the backend (causing a delayed 401 redirect loop) or, if the backend were to accept it in a misconfigured deployment, grants unauthenticated access. This is a debug/development artifact accidentally committed to production code — there is no environment check (e.g., process.env.NODE_ENV) gate.

summary: Video placement type lost: adapter deletes canonical `plcmt` field and `placement.placement` is sourced from deprecated `mediaTypes.video.placement` instead of canonical `mediaTypes.video.plcmt`
failure_scenario: Publisher sets `mediaTypes.video.plcmt = 1` (instream) without the deprecated `placement` field. Library sets `placement.placement = undefined` (from deprecated field), adapter deletes `placement.plcmt` (the canonical value). Server receives no placement type, potentially serving wrong ad format or no ad.

summary: `interpretResponse` has no try/catch around `serverResponse.body.length`; old colossusssp adapter caught and logged errors
failure_scenario: Server returns null body, malformed response, or network error produces an unexpected response object. `serverResponse.body` is null/undefined, accessing `.length` throws an uncaught TypeError, crashing the bid response processing instead of returning an empty bid array.

summary: `schain` always included in placement (minimum `{}`); old code only included it when `bid.ortb2.source.ext.schain` was present
failure_scenario: A placement with no supply chain data now sends `schain: {}` in the JSON request. `{}` is invalid ORTB schain (missing required `ver`, `complete`, `nodes` fields), potentially causing server-side validation failure or bid rejection.

summary: `page` field now sends full URL from `bidderRequest.refererInfo.page` instead of just `location.pathname`
failure_scenario: Old code sent `page: '/home'`; new code sends `page: 'https://example.com/home'`. Server-side URL parsing, matching, or logging that expects a path-only value may break or produce incorrect results.

summary: NATIVE bid validation stricter: now requires `bid.native.impressionTrackers` with non-empty array; old colossusssp accepted any truthy `bid.native`
failure_scenario: Server returns a valid native bid with creative but without impression trackers (or with an empty tracker list). The old adapter would accept and forward this bid; the new adapter silently drops it in `interpretResponse`, reducing fill rate.

summary: `buildRequests` replaces `request.data` with a hand-picked subset, silently dropping `coppa`, `tmax`, `bcat`, `badv`, `bapp`, `battr`, `device` that the `buildRequestsBase` library function sets
failure_scenario: Library adds a new request field in a future version (e.g., a new consent or targeting parameter). The adapter's explicit field-whitelist reconstruction silently drops it, so the new feature never reaches the colossusssp server. Existing dropped fields like `coppa` and `tmax` are also lost from bid requests.

summary: end_date is formatted via str() instead of strftime(), producing an incompatible date format for the ISOC Pulse API
failure_scenario: User runs `ingestr ingest --source-uri 'isoc-pulse://?token=xxx' --source-table 'https' --interval-end 2023-12-31`. The `interval_end` from main.py is a `datetime` object. `str(datetime(2023,12,31))` produces `'2023-12-31 00:00:00'` (or `'2023-12-31T00:00:00+00:00'` for pendulum), but the API expects `'2023-12-31'` (the format used by start_date via strftime). The API rejects the request or misinterprets the date, causing the ingestion to fail.

summary: https metric path construction always treats opts[-1] as a country code, so 'https:topsites' (global topsites, no country) creates path 'https/country/topsites' with 'topsites' as the country
failure_scenario: User runs `ingestr ingest --source-table 'https:topsites'` for global HTTPS topsites data. After colon-splitting, `opts = ['topsites']`. The `https` branch sets `path = 'https/country/topsites'` treating 'topsites' as a country code. The API receives a request to `/api/https/country/topsites` which is not a valid ISO country code, returning a 404 or error. The ipv6 branch correctly handles this pattern by checking `'topsites' in opts` first and not appending `/country/` to the path.

summary: Quarter calculation `math.floor(date.month / 4) + 1` is incorrect for months 7, 10, and 11, mapping July to Q2, October/November to Q3
failure_scenario: User queries resilience metrics with `--interval-start 2023-07-15` (July). `date.month = 7`, `math.floor(7/4) + 1 = 2` (Q2), but July is in Q3. The API request includes `quarter=2` instead of `quarter=3`, returning Q2 resilience data instead of Q3 data. Similarly, October (month 10) and November (month 11) map to Q3 instead of Q4. The correct formula is `(date.month - 1) // 3 + 1` or `math.ceil(date.month / 3)`.

summary: URLs in urlset entries that fail Url::parse() are silently dropped, while the original JS code unconditionally passed all non-file, non-xml URLs to the urlsHandler callback.
failure_scenario: A sitemap contains <url><loc>https://example.com/path with spaces</loc></url>. The unencoded spaces cause Url::parse to fail. The URL is silently dropped — it falls into neither xml_sitemaps nor valid_urls. The _process_sitemap function returns Ok without error, so the JS caller never knows the URL was lost and never triggers the JS fallback logic that would have handled it.

summary: The new parseSitemapXml and processSitemap methods duplicate the exact same promise/error-handling/RUSTFC:ERROR block pattern from filterLinks, creating a maintenance burden where any fix must be replicated across three nearly identical code blocks.
failure_scenario: A future developer fixing a bug in the RUSTFC:ERROR prefix parsing logic (e.g., edge cases in the res.split call) fixes filterLinks but misses parseSitemapXml or processSitemap, leaving inconsistent error handling across the three FFI wrappers.

summary: Exception in usage-limit error handler silently falls through, bypassing the limit and corrupting state
failure_scenario: When _check_usage_limit returns an error and _format_result or _telemetry.tool_usage_error raises within the try block (lines 205-209), the bare except at line 210 catches it with no return statement. Execution falls through. Since result is still the error string (not None), the 'if result is None:' guard at line 214 is skipped. The code continues to line 284 where _telemetry.tool_usage fires (reporting the tool as used), line 296 emits on_tool_use_finished, line 312 appends to agent.tools_results, and critically, line 315 increments current_usage_count. The tool appears successfully used despite being over its limit, and the limit counter advances, allowing further uses. The tool invocation block (lines 214-269) is also skipped because result is not None, so no actual tool execution occurs -- but the system believes it did.

summary: BaseTool.from_langchain and Tool.from_langchain construct new instances without propagating max_usage_count or current_usage_count
failure_scenario: A tool with max_usage_count=5 enters the agent pipeline at base_agent.py:189, which calls Tool.from_langchain(tool). The factory at line 258-263 constructs a new Tool with cls(name=..., description=..., func=..., args_schema=...). Since max_usage_count and current_usage_count are not extracted from the source tool and passed to the constructor, the new instance defaults to max_usage_count=None (unlimited) and current_usage_count=0. The usage limit is silently lost for any tool that passes through from_langchain. Same gap exists in BaseTool.from_langchain at line 150.

summary: CrewStructuredTool.from_function accepts **kwargs but never forwards them to the constructor, silently dropping max_usage_count
failure_scenario: A caller invokes CrewStructuredTool.from_function(func=my_func, max_usage_count=3). The **kwargs parameter at line 61 collects max_usage_count=3, but the cls(...) constructor call at lines 105-111 passes only name, description, args_schema, func, and result_as_answer -- no **kwargs. The max_usage_count value is silently discarded. The resulting CrewStructuredTool has the default max_usage_count=None, giving it unlimited usage despite the caller's intent. The docstring at line 72 even states that **kwargs are 'Additional arguments to pass to the tool,' misleading callers.

summary: BaseTool.run() increments current_usage_count but never checks max_usage_count, allowing unlimited direct execution
failure_scenario: A tool with max_usage_count=2 is invoked directly via tool.run() 10 times. Each call successfully executes _run() and increments current_usage_count at line 85. No pre-check against max_usage_count exists in run(), so the limit is tracked but never enforced. The limit is only enforced in ToolUsage._use() (agent path). Direct callers like the LangGraphToolAdapter at langgraph_tool_adapter.py:37-41 call tool.run() and completely bypass usage-limit enforcement. The PR's own test (test_tool_usage_limit) only calls run() twice (equal to max_usage_count=2) and never tests blocking a third call, masking this gap.

summary: reset_usage_count on BaseTool does not reset the CrewStructuredTool wrapper's counter used by the agent path
failure_scenario: A tool is used through the agent. to_structured_tool() at line 101 creates a CrewStructuredTool with current_usage_count copied from the BaseTool at construction time. Both objects then have independent counters. Calling tool.reset_usage_count() (line 89) resets the BaseTool's counter to 0, but the CrewStructuredTool in ToolUsage.tools retains its old counter. The agent still sees the tool as having reached its limit. Since CrewStructuredTool has no reset_usage_count method, there is no way to reset the counter for agent-mediated tool usage through the public API.

summary: Zoom-out button uses `>=` instead of `>`, preventing users from reaching the declared minimum zoom level of 0.25
failure_scenario: Starting at zoom level 0.5 (50%), clicking zoom out would go to 0.25 (25%) which equals minZoom. The condition `minZoom >= nextZoomOut` evaluates to `0.25 >= 0.25` = true, disabling the button. Users can only zoom down to 0.5, not 0.25. Compare with the zoom-in condition on line 42 which correctly uses strict `<` (`maxZoom < nextZoomIn`), allowing zoom exactly to maxZoom.

summary: moduleNameMapper regex `\^lucide-react$` escapes the start anchor, turning it into a literal `^` character that never matches any module name
failure_scenario: The JSON key `"\\^lucide-react$"` parses to the string `\^lucide-react$`. When Jest creates a regex from this, `\^` means 'escaped caret' matching a literal `^` character. Since module names like `lucide-react` do not start with a literal `^`, the regex never matches. The mock file at `__mocks__/lucide-react.js` is never applied. All 8 source files that import from `lucide-react` (CtlBar.tsx, Designer/Canvas/index.tsx, AlignWidget.tsx, DetailView/index.tsx, ListView/Item.tsx, Designer/RightSidebar/index.tsx, Spinner.tsx, UnitPager.tsx) will receive the real lucide-react module instead, causing snapshot test failures. The fix is `"^lucide-react$"` (without the backslash before the caret). Every other entry in moduleNameMapper (lines 85-91) uses un-escaped `^` as the start anchor.

summary: England driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (England is part of the UK, which drives on the left)
failure_scenario: Any downstream consumer looking up England's driving side gets 'right' instead of the correct 'left' — routing, navigation, or vehicle-configuration software would produce wrong results.

summary: Northern Ireland driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (Northern Ireland is part of the UK, which drives on the left)
failure_scenario: Consumer software that queries Northern Ireland's driving side receives 'right', leading to incorrect lane-assignment or vehicle-orientation decisions.

summary: Scotland driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (Scotland is part of the UK, which drives on the left)
failure_scenario: Software relying on this dataset for Scotland produces wrong driving-side output, affecting any downstream application that uses it for routing or compliance.

summary: Wales driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (Wales is part of the UK, which drives on the left)
failure_scenario: A lookup for Wales returns 'right' instead of 'left', causing incorrect behavior in any system that depends on accurate driving-side data for Wales.

summary: Bermuda driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory and drives on the left)
failure_scenario: All other British Overseas Territories in this file (Anguilla, Cayman Islands, Falkland Islands, Gibraltar, Montserrat, Pitcairn, Turks and Caicos, British Virgin Islands) are correctly listed as 'left'. Bermuda is the sole outlier, so any consumer relying on consistent territory-side rules gets wrong data.

summary: US Virgin Islands driving side incorrectly listed as 'right'; should be 'left' (the USVI inherited left-hand driving from its Danish colonial period and never switched)
failure_scenario: Software that looks up driving side for 'Virgin Islands, U.S.' gets 'right' instead of the correct 'left' — this is a well-known exception where a US territory does not follow the mainland US convention.

summary: New Caledonia driving side incorrectly listed as 'left'; should be 'right' (New Caledonia is a French overseas collectivity and all French territories drive on the right)
failure_scenario: Every other French overseas territory in this file (French Guiana, French Polynesia, French Southern territories, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Reunion, Saint Pierre and Miquelon) is correctly listed as 'right'. New Caledonia is an isolated error that would cause consumers to treat it as left-driving.

summary: Wallis and Futuna driving side incorrectly listed as 'left'; should be 'right' (Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity and all French territories drive on the right)
failure_scenario: Same as New Caledonia — the only two French territories listed as 'left' in an otherwise consistently-right French block. A consumer that groups territories by sovereignty would get wrong results.

summary: Duplicate country entry: 'East Timor' (line 248) and 'Timor-Leste' (line 880) refer to the same country, creating a redundant entry
failure_scenario: Code that iterates all entries and counts or aggregates by country processes Timor-Leste twice. Code that does a first-match lookup with one name may miss the other entry, though both currently agree on 'left'. If one entry were later updated and the other missed, they would diverge.

summary: to_str().unwrap() panics and crashes the entire Node.js process when HTML input contains non-UTF-8 byte sequences
failure_scenario: A scraped web page serves HTML with an encoding mis-declared as UTF-8 but containing Latin-1 bytes in the 0x80-0xFF range. The scraper's HTTP client decodes it into a JS string with replacement characters, but if the actual response bytes are passed directly as a C string through koffi FFI, to_str() fails and the entire service process terminates.

summary: CString::new().unwrap() panics and crashes the Node.js process if a base href attribute contains an embedded null byte
failure_scenario: A malicious or corrupted HTML page contains <base href="https://example.com/\x00evil">. The scraper extracts the href value containing the null byte, CString::new() panics, and the entire service process terminates.

summary: extractLinksRust parses the same HTML twice (once to extract links, once to extract base href), each via a separate parse_html() call in Rust
failure_scenario: On the scrape hot path with large HTML documents (e.g., 500KB+ pages), the duplicate full-HTML parse doubles CPU time spent in the Rust HTML parser, adding measurable latency per scrape. A single combined Rust function returning both links and base href would parse once.

summary: Duplicate text output in streaming mode (the default): raw delta events print incremental text, then the message_output_item RunItemStreamEvent prints the same full text again via ItemHelpers.text_message_output
failure_scenario: Any streaming REPL session (the default since stream=True) prints every agent response twice -- once character-by-character from ResponseTextDeltaEvent deltas (line 47), and again as the full assembled message when the message_output_item event arrives (line 54). The user sees garbled duplicate output for every turn.

summary: No exception handling around Runner.run_streamed() or Runner.run() -- any agent exception (MaxTurnsExceeded, guardrail tripwires, ModelBehaviorError, etc.) crashes the entire REPL instead of printing an error and continuing the loop
failure_scenario: After 10 conversation turns with the default max_turns, a MaxTurnsExceeded exception is raised -- it propagates uncaught out of the while-loop, crashes the REPL, and discards all conversation state. Same behavior for guardrail tripwires or any other AgentsException.

summary: Whitespace-only input (e.g. spaces, tabs) bypasses the empty-input guard because 'if not user_input' checks the raw string, while the exit check uses strip().lower() -- result: a whitespace-only content message is sent to the agent
failure_scenario: User types three spaces and presses Enter. user_input = '   '. '   '.strip().lower() = '' which is not in {'exit', 'quit'}, so the exit check does not break. 'not "   "' is False, so the empty-input guard does not trigger. The loop proceeds to append {'role': 'user', 'content': '   '} to input_items and sends a whitespace-only message to the model.

summary: _numBranches=1 is incorrectly treated as separation (0) in the UI, causing display corruption and silent data mutation.
failure_scenario: Open the gene editor on a gene with _numBranches=1 (one branch). Line 93 copies the value (1), line 94-96 decrements it to 0, then line 97 checks the decremented value `numBranches > 0` which is now false, so numBranchesOptional becomes std::nullopt. The ComboOptional shows 'no selection' instead of '1 branch'. If the user makes no change to this field, line 107 executes `gene._numBranches = 0`, silently converting the gene from 1 branch to separation.

summary: Type change from std::optional<int> to int for _numBranches breaks loading old serialized data containing non-separation branch values, causing std::bad_variant_access crash.
failure_scenario: A user has a saved game/file created with the old code where a gene had _numBranches = optional<int>(2). The Cereal VariantData at key Id_Gene_NumBranches was serialized as std::optional<int>. When loading with the new code, Cereal deserializes it as std::optional<int> (still in the VariantData type list), but the loadSave function at line 100 calls `std::get<int>(variantData)`, which throws std::bad_variant_access because the variant actually holds std::optional<int>, not int. Application crashes on load.

summary: _set_root_namespace fails to detect the end of a multi-line docstring — in_docstring stays True forever after entering, causing all subsequent content (imports, assignments) to be silently dropped
failure_scenario: An __init__.py containing '\"\"\"Multi-line\ndocstring\"\"\"\nfrom ._version import VERSION' has in_docstring=True from line 1 and never toggles back (the closing \"\"\" on line 2 does not start with triple quotes, so no toggle occurs; a closing \"\"\" alone on a line does start with \"\"\" but the condition also requires NOT ending with \"\"\", which is False — so still no toggle). All lines after the docstring are skipped, content is empty, and _set_root_namespace returns None. discover_namespace then falls back to the next __init__.py or ultimately to name.replace('-', '.') — producing an incorrect namespace. For azure-eventhub-checkpointstoreblob, this could yield 'azure.eventhub.checkpointstoreblob' instead of 'azure.eventhub.extensions.checkpointstoreblob', silently breaking sphinx docs, mypy/pyright type checking, and import verification.

summary: _set_root_namespace does not exclude single-line triple-quoted docstrings from the content list, inflating the line count and causing false 'substantial content' detection
failure_scenario: An __init__.py containing '\"\"\"Azure SDK.\"\"\"\n__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)' has the single-line docstring incorrectly added to content (because it starts AND ends with \"\"\", so the toggle condition 'starts but does not end' is False and in_docstring stays False; the line is not a #-comment so it passes the append filter). The extension line is also added, giving content 2 items. len(content) > 1 causes the function to return the module name, treating this namespace-extension-only file as substantial. The wrong (shallower) namespace is used.

summary: _set_root_namespace does not filter blank/empty lines, which are appended to the content list and can inflate the line count past 1 for extension-only __init__.py files
failure_scenario: An __init__.py with a blank line followed by '__path__ = __import__("pkgutil").extend_path(__path__, __name__)' has the empty line (stripped to '') added to content because 'not "".startswith("#")' evaluates to True. Both the blank line and the extension line are in content, giving len(content) > 1, so the function incorrectly returns the module name instead of None. This causes discover_namespace to stop at this file and use the wrong namespace.

summary: requires can be None when pyproject.toml [project] lacks a 'dependencies' key, causing TypeError on line 491 where None is iterated by map()
failure_scenario: A pyproject.toml with a valid [project] section but no 'dependencies' key (which is optional per PEP 621) has project_config.get('dependencies') return None. Line 491 calls any(map(lambda x: ..., None)), which raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable. This crashes parse_pyproject for any dependency-free package using pyproject.toml. (Pre-existing bug; the setup.py path handles this with a [ ] default.)

summary: Array.includes() on ISwapNetwork objects uses reference equality; filter always removes all user-disabled network entries
failure_scenario: Server returns a provider with isSupportSingleSwap=true and supportSingleSwapNetworks=[{networkId:'evm--1'},{networkId:'evm--56'}]. User had previously disabled 'evm--1' for this provider (provider.disableNetworks=[{networkId:'evm--1'}]). The filter `provider.disableNetworks?.filter((net) => findProvider?.supportSingleSwapNetworks?.includes(net))` calls `includes()` on ISwapNetwork objects from different JSON parse origins; reference equality fails for all entries, returning `[]`. disableNetworks saved to simpleDb is empty, all user-disabled networks are silently re-enabled. Correct fix: compare by networkId field (e.g. `.some(sn => sn.networkId === net.networkId)`).

summary: Analytics log fires before async cleanSwapHistoryItems() completes in onDeletePendingHistory, reporting successful clean before operation finishes
failure_scenario: User taps 'Clear pending history'. Dialog onConfirm calls `void backgroundApiProxy.serviceSwap.cleanSwapHistoryItems([PENDING])` (fire-and-forget async) then immediately logs `cleanSwapOrder({cleanFrom: LIST})`. The log fires before the Promise resolves; if the clean operation fails (e.g. storage error), the analytics event incorrectly reports a successful cleanup. Contrast with onDeleteHistory (line 158) which properly awaits the operation before logging.

summary: Removal of defensive early-return; when findProvider is undefined, uninitialized serviceDisable/serviceDisableNetworks (undefined) override existing provider values via spread
failure_scenario: If a provider exists in simpleDb but findProvider resolves to undefined (edge case, e.g. race between findNoProvider cleanup and re-fetch), the old code returned `provider` unmodified (preserving provider.serviceDisable and provider.serviceDisableNetworks). The new code returns `{...provider, serviceDisable: undefined, serviceDisableNetworks: undefined}`, overwriting any existing service-disable state with undefined. A previously service-disabled provider would appear enabled. Likelihood is low due to upstream cleanup guards, but the defensive protection is lost.

summary: Missing validation that input depth C is divisible by blocksize^2; the CPU kernel enforces this but the WebGPU kernel does not
failure_scenario: Input with shape (N=1, C=9, H=1, W=1) and blocksize=2. C=9 is not divisible by 4. The kernel computes c' = 9/4 = 2 (integer truncation), builds a 6D override shape with 8 elements while the actual input has 9 elements. The debug-only ValidateVariable (shader_helper.cc:279, gated by #ifndef NDEBUG) is the only check that catches this element-count mismatch; in a release build this check is skipped. The shader executes reading only a subset of input elements, producing a wrong output without any error. Compare CPU kernel at space_depth_ops.h:55-58 which validates 'input_depth % (blocksize_ * blocksize_) != 0' and returns a clear INVALID_ARGUMENT Status.

summary: AppendPermFunction generates shader perm() signature with input_indices_t parameter type instead of output_indices_t; works only by coincidence when input and output ranks are equal
failure_scenario: The generated WGSL function is 'fn perm(i: input_indices_t) -> input_indices_t' but the call site passes output.OffsetToIndices("global_idx") which produces output_indices_t. In this PR both the input and output override shapes have rank 6 so the WGSL types are identical. If this helper were reused in a context where input and output override shapes have different ranks, the WGSL compiler would reject the shader due to a type mismatch. The existing TransposeProgram (transpose.cc:85) correctly declares 'fn perm(i: output_indices_t)->a_indices_t'.

summary: StakeProgress component is conditionally hidden during deposit-only flows when token allowance is already sufficient, removing the visual step indicator that was previously always rendered
failure_scenario: User opens the staking form for a token they have already approved (allowance >= deposit amount) — e.g. allowance=1000, they enter amount=100. The `isShowStakeProgress` condition `!!amountValue && (isApprove || showStakeProgressRef.current[amountValue])` evaluates to false because `isApprove` is false (allowance covers 100) and the ref was never set (no approve flow ran). The `<StakeProgress>` (showing '1. Approve / 2. Deposit' steps) is not rendered at all. Before this change the progress was always visible, showing the deposit step as active with a checkmark on the already-complete approve step.

summary: showStakeProgressRef entry set before approval navigation is never cleared on cancel or failure, leaving a stale entry that can incorrectly re-activate the progress indicator after external allowance changes
failure_scenario: User enters amount='100', clicks Approve, cancels the transaction → `showStakeProgressRef.current['100']` remains true. Later, allowance increases externally (e.g., the user approves the same token through another app or flow) and returns to this screen with amount='100' still typed. `isApprove` becomes false (allowance now covers 100) but the stale ref still has true for key '100', so `isShowStakeProgress` evaluates to true. The StakeProgress incorrectly shows as if the approval had completed in this session.

summary: poolFee data is still collected from details and passed as a prop to ProviderInfo but the rendering code for it was removed in this diff, leaving dead code in ProviderSection that wastes computation and the ProviderInfo destructuring parameter that TypeScript may flag as unused
failure_scenario: ProviderSection collects `details.provider.poolFee` into `providerProps.poolFee` (lines 201-205) and passes it to ProviderInfo. ProviderInfo destructures `poolFee` in its parameter list (line 51) but the grid item that rendered it was deleted. This dead code path computes and passes a value that is never consumed, and the unused destructured variable may trigger linter warnings. The poolFee value was moved to ProfitSection for display inside the MorphoApy popover, but the ProviderSection collection and prop threading were not cleaned up.

summary: Missing UNIQUE constraint on (building_schema_id, number) allows duplicate version numbers under concurrent writes; the application-layer optimistic concurrency check at createNewVersion.ts line 96 is read-then-write and not atomic.
failure_scenario: Two users edit the same building schema simultaneously. Both POST requests pass the version-number check (both see actualLatestVersionNumber=3), both compute nextVersionNumber=4, and both INSERT succeeds. The table now has two rows with number=4 for the same building_schema_id, corrupting the version lineage.

summary: JSON Pointer escape sequences (~0 for literal ~, ~1 for literal /) are not decoded before using path segments as object keys, violating RFC 6901.
failure_scenario: A key named 'nested/key' in the building schema causes fast-json-patch's compare() at createNewVersion.ts line 76 to generate a reverse_patch with path '/nested~1key'. When that reverse_patch is later applied, applyPatchOperations looks up the literal key 'nested~1key' (not 'nested/key'), silently operating on the wrong key or doing nothing.

summary: operationsSchema validates and accepts 'move', 'copy', and 'test' operations, but applyPatchOperations throws on these operation types via its .otherwise() clause, making the validator inconsistent with the implementation.
failure_scenario: A client sends a valid JSON Patch containing a 'move' operation. The route handler validates it successfully (operationsSchema accepts it), calls createNewVersion, which calls applyPatchOperations(newContent, patch) at line 73. applyPatchOperations hits the .otherwise() clause and throws 'Operation type 'move' is not implemented'. Worse, if such an operation is persisted to the DB, every future attempt to replay history at line 68 will fail identically, permanently blocking new versions for that schema.

summary: getOrCreateObject silently overwrites a primitive intermediate value with an empty object when traversing a path, instead of throwing an error as the JSON Patch spec requires.
failure_scenario: Building schema content is { 'name': 'John' }. A buggy or malicious client sends operation { op: 'add', path: '/name/first', value: 'Jane' }. getOrCreateObject finds that target['name'] is 'John' (a string, not a record), silently replaces it with {}, and the value 'John' is irretrievably lost. The result is { name: { first: 'Jane' } }.

summary: No try/catch around createNewVersion() call; DB failures and other thrown errors bubble up as opaque Next.js 500 responses with no structured error body.
failure_scenario: The Supabase database is temporarily unreachable. createNewVersion throws 'Failed to fetch building schema: ...'. The route handler has no catch block, so Next.js returns a generic 500 Internal Server Error page. The client receives no JSON error payload and cannot distinguish this from other server crashes.

summary: Custom applyPatchOperations reimplements functionality already provided by the fast-json-patch library (which is added as a dependency in this same PR), but with fewer features and known bugs.
failure_scenario: The fast-json-patch library's applyPatch() function supports all six JSON Patch operation types (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test) and correctly decodes JSON Pointer escapes. The hand-rolled applyPatchOperations supports only three, misses escape decoding, and silently overwrites primitives. Maintenance cost: 57 lines of duplicate code that must be kept in sync with the library.

summary: Non-CacheError exceptions from runCachedTest (e.g. getNormalizedComponentStringByCoords failures) bypass fallback-to-AI and fail the test outright; old code fell back on all errors
