failure_scenario: During cached step replay, the browser page disconnects or navigates unexpectedly between get() and execute(), causing browserTool.getNormalizedComponentStringByCoords(x,y) at line 423 to throw (not a CacheError). The catch block at line 183-184 checks `if (!(error instanceof CacheError)) throw error` and rethrows it. The test fails immediately with the raw browser error instead of falling back to normal AI execution as the old code did via its catch-all fallback path.

summary: Added {delay:200} to page.mouse.click introduces a 200ms gap between mousedown and mouseup; some web apps treat slow clicks as long-press or drag-start instead of click
failure_scenario: A web app with a custom interaction handler that distinguishes mousedown-mouseup timing (e.g., treating intervals >100ms as a drag gesture or long-press context menu) would fire the wrong handler when the test automation issues a click with a 200ms mousedown-to-mouseup delay. The old code used page.mouse.click() with no delay (default 0ms gap), which always triggered standard click behavior.

summary: install(FILES my_package-config.cmake ...) references a file that does not exist in the repository, causing cmake --install failure when FTXUI_BUILD_MODULES=ON and FTXUI_ENABLE_INSTALL=ON.
failure_scenario: Build with -DFTXUI_BUILD_MODULES=ON -DFTXUI_ENABLE_INSTALL=ON, then run 'cmake --install .' or 'make install'. CMake fails with error: 'Cannot find source file: my_package-config.cmake'. This is a placeholder filename that was never replaced with the actual config file path.

summary: Duplicate install(EXPORT ftxui-targets ...) conflicts with the one already defined in cmake/ftxui_install.cmake line 25 — the modules version omits NAMESPACE ftxui:: and adds CXX_MODULES_DIRECTORY, while the install version has NAMESPACE ftxui:: but no CXX_MODULES_DIRECTORY. CMake may silently overwrite one with the other.
failure_scenario: Build with both FTXUI_BUILD_MODULES=ON and FTXUI_ENABLE_INSTALL=ON. Depending on CMake version and processing order, either (a) the installed ftxui-targets.cmake lacks the ftxui:: namespace prefix, breaking find_package(ftxui) consumers, or (b) the installed export file lacks CXX_MODULES_DIRECTORY information, making installed modules unusable by downstream consumers.

summary: sed -i on lines 15-21 and 25-26 uses GNU sed syntax without a backup extension; the script fails on macOS/BSD where sed -i requires an argument (e.g., sed -i '').
failure_scenario: A developer runs ./tools/generate_examples_modules.sh on macOS. sed -i '' /#include "ftxui/d' treats the empty string '' as the backup suffix and the next argument as the sed command, causing 'sed: 1: "/#include "ftxui/d": invalid command code f' or similar error. The script aborts without generating the examples_modules directory.

summary: @file doxygen tag reads 'canvas.cppm' but the actual filename is 'elements.cppm' — copy-paste error from the canvas module file.
failure_scenario: Generated documentation incorrectly attributes the elements module documentation to canvas.cppm, leading to confusion when developers search for the elements module's doxygen documentation.

summary: @file doxygen tag reads 'box.cppm' but the actual filename is 'deprecated.cppm' — copy-paste error from the box module file.
failure_scenario: Generated documentation incorrectly attributes the deprecated module documentation to box.cppm, leading to confusion.

summary: SidebarProvider writes sidebar_state cookie on every toggle but never reads it back on mount; sidebar always resets to expanded (defaultOpen=true) on any full page navigation
failure_scenario: User collapses the sidebar, then navigates from one project to another (or from project to account page). The SidebarProvider re-mounts, `_open` is initialized to `defaultOpen=true`, and the sidebar reopens. The cookie intended to persist state across sessions is never consumed.

summary: Separator element in sidebarLinks.map() lacks a `key` prop, causing React reconciliation warnings
failure_scenario: The ProjectSidebarLayout passes footerSidebarLinks containing a {separator:true} item. When RenderSidebarGroup maps over this array, the separator returns `<SidebarSeparator className='my-1' />` with no key. React logs a warning. If separators were ever reordered, DOM state (focus, animations) could become mismatched.

summary: SidebarMenuSkeleton uses Math.random() inside useMemo during render, causing SSR hydration mismatch
failure_scenario: Server renders skeleton with random width '67%', client hydrates with random width '82%'. React logs a hydration mismatch error and may re-render the component, causing a visible layout flicker. The component is currently unused but exported from the module.

summary: Separator element in RenderSidebarLinks lacks a `key` prop, same defect as in RenderSidebarGroup
failure_scenario: If any consumer of RenderSidebarLinks (mobile sidebar, contract page layouts) adds a separator to its links array, React will warn about missing keys.

summary: prefetch={false} added globally to all NavLink instances, disabling Next.js link prefetching for every sidebar navigation link
failure_scenario: Users hover over sidebar links or scroll them into viewport; Next.js no longer prefetches the target page's JS and data. On click, the user experiences a full network round-trip delay instead of an instant client-side transition. Affects all consumers: CustomSidebar, FullWidthSidebarLayout, and the nebula app's ChatSidebarLink.

summary: RenderSidebarGroup does not render an external-link icon for links with http-prefixed hrefs, unlike the old RenderSidebarLinks which renders ExternalLinkIcon
failure_scenario: In the new project sidebar, 'Documentation' and 'Playground' links (hrefs: https://portal.thirdweb.com, https://playground.thirdweb.com/...) appear identical to internal links. The old sidebar always showed an ExternalLinkIcon next to external links. Users cannot visually distinguish internal from external navigation targets in the new sidebar.

summary: Cookie set without SameSite or Secure attributes; sidebar_state cookie is sent on cross-site requests where it should not be
failure_scenario: On a cross-origin request to the application, the sidebar_state cookie is attached to the request. While the value ('true'/'false') is non-sensitive, the lack of SameSite=Lax means CSRF-style side effects could be possible in some configurations.

summary: MobileSidebarTrigger creates a new array reference [...contentSidebarLinks, ...(footerSidebarLinks || [])] on every render, defeating the useMemo inside useActiveSidebarLink
failure_scenario: On every re-render of FullWidthSidebarLayout, useActiveSidebarLink receives a new array reference, causing its internal useMemo to re-run and re-scan all links even when neither contentSidebarLinks nor footerSidebarLinks have changed.

summary: Async messages_modifier callable returns unawaited coroutine -- callable() check does not distinguish async from sync, and the inner wrapper calls it without await, passing a coroutine object to the model instead of LanguageModelInput.
failure_scenario: User passes an async function as messages_modifier (e.g., async def my_modifier(messages): return 'Hello'). At runtime, callable(messages_modifier) is True at line 124. The inner prompt function at line 126-127 calls messages_modifier() without await, returning a coroutine object. This coroutine flows through RunnableCallable and the | pipeline into the model's invoke(), where a chat model receives a coroutine instead of a string or message sequence, causing a TypeError or silent incorrect behavior.

summary: Inner prompt function's return type annotation Sequence[BaseMessage] is inconsistent with the widened MessagesModifier type -- the actual return flows through messages_modifier which now returns LanguageModelInput (includes str and PromptValue, neither of which is Sequence[BaseMessage]).
failure_scenario: A type checker like mypy or pyright would flag the return statement as returning LanguageModelInput incompatible with the declared Sequence[BaseMessage] return type. This would fail CI in projects that enforce static type checking on this file, despite no runtime crash.

summary: parseApiVersionStringToArray returns NaN for non-beta release versions because the condition matchResult[2] === '' incorrectly assumes the optional capture group is '' when absent, but it is undefined
failure_scenario: When a non-beta release version like 'v2' is added to the migrations folder, parseApiVersionStringToArray('v2') returns [2, NaN]. The sort comparator numberCompare(parsedA[1], parsedB[1]) calls Math.sign(NaN - x) = NaN, returning NaN from the sort callback which produces unpredictable sort order. Non-beta versions would sort incorrectly among beta versions.

summary: Version prefix matching uses string startsWith without enforcing a segment boundary, so paths like /api/v2beta1-extra/something incorrectly match the v2beta1 served route
failure_scenario: A request to /api/v2beta1-extra/something would be matched as a v2beta1 request because '/api/v2beta1-extra/something/' starts with '/api/v2beta1/'. The middleware would then try to rewrite it using replace('/api/v2beta1', '/api/v2beta2'), producing the path /api/v2beta2-extra/something and potentially routing to an unintended handler or returning a confusing error.

summary: String.prototype.replace() without a global flag replaces only the first occurrence of the version prefix, producing incorrect paths for URLs that contain the version string multiple times
failure_scenario: A crafted request like /api/v1/api/v1/simple would have replace('/api/v1', '/api/v2beta1') produce /api/v2beta1/api/v1/simple (only first occurrence replaced). The repeated version string causes the middleware to rewrite to an unintended intermediate path. This is low-likelihood in normal use but is incorrect URL rewriting.

summary: The invoke property type changes from Promise<Response> to Promise<Res>, a breaking API change for any code that calls a smart-route-handler's .invoke() method expecting an HTTP Response
failure_scenario: Any existing (non-diff) code that calls handler.invoke(smartRequest) and expects to receive an HTTP Response object would instead receive a SmartResponse object (a plain object with statusCode, bodyType, etc.), causing runtime failures when trying to use .status, .json(), .text() etc. on the returned value. Currently the only caller (v2beta3 migration route) is new code in this same PR and handles it correctly, but any future or external invoker needs to be aware of this change.

summary: catch handler spreads args from Promise.catch which always receives a single error argument, making the spread unnecessary and potentially hiding error detail depending on console.error formatting
failure_scenario: When main() throws, Promise.catch receives exactly one argument (the error). The spread ...args passes it as separate arguments to console.error, which may not format it as helpfully as console.error(error) would. Additionally, if the error is a non-Error primitive (e.g. a string), the spread would pass it piecemeal, potentially losing context compared to passing a single object.

summary: TypeError crash when instance.model is None: the new string-split logic crashes because '/ in None' is invalid, whereas the old code tolerated None by f-string conversion to 'None.llm'
failure_scenario: A CrewAI LLM instance has model=None (attribute exists but not set) → llm=None → 'in' operator raises TypeError → the outer except catches it and re-raises → the LLM.call wrapper crashes before wrapped() runs → the original LLM call never executes

summary: Outer except block catches ALL exceptions but logs 'Error in provider detection', misleading diagnosis when the real error is an LLM call failure or instrumentation error, and causes double-logging for exceptions from the inner span path
failure_scenario: LLM API call fails with a network error inside the span (line 448) → inner handler logs 'Error in trace creation: ConnectionError' (correct) and re-raises → outer handler catches it and logs 'Error in provider detection: ConnectionError' (wrong label) → operator investigates provider detection instead of the network issue

summary: The 'if instrumentor:' skip path returns wrapped() with no span, no duration metrics, and no CrewAI attributes, but only checks a hardcoded string match — it never verifies the target instrumentor is actually loaded, so if it is absent the LLM call runs entirely un-instrumented
failure_scenario: User configures CrewAI with model='gpt-4' but has not installed or enabled the OpenAI OpenTelemetry instrumentation (only the CrewAI instrumentor) → wrap_llm_call matches 'gpt' in the dict → skips all CrewAI instrumentation → no span, no duration metrics, no token attributes → LLM calls are invisible in traces

summary: The 'if result:' guard skips setting completion content and role attributes when the LLM returns a falsy value such as an empty string, losing valid completion data (pre-existing in the old code, within the touched function)
failure_scenario: LLM returns empty string '' as a valid response → result is falsy → span.set_attribute for COMPLETION_CONTENT and COMPLETION_ROLE are skipped → the span shows OK status but has no completion data, even though the call succeeded and returned a real (empty) result

summary: Dead code: renderInputFields method and its 4 associated styled components (InputFields, Currency, OnDemandInput, DetailTitle) plus the Input import are defined but never called. The modal's render() delegates to <OnDemandBudgetEdit> which has its own renderInputFields with dynamic per-category rendering.
failure_scenario: The method and 100+ lines of code are unreachable. The budget edit modal renders through OnDemandBudgetEdit (line 326), making this orphaned code a maintenance liability and leaving the Input import as an unnecessary dependency.

summary: Duplicate cent/dollar conversion functions coerceValue/parseInputValue copied identically from onDemandBudgetEdit.tsx. These functions are already duplicated across 5+ files in the codebase.
failure_scenario: A bug fix or behavior change to the conversion logic (e.g., handling decimals instead of parseInt truncation) would need to be replicated across all copies. The modal independently defines parseInputValue using parseInt (line 45), which silently drops decimal fractions if a desktop user types '42.50' in the type='text' input.

summary: parseOnDemandBudgets uses for...in to iterate over the budgets object, iterating inherited enumerable properties in addition to own properties. The sibling function convertOnDemandBudget (line 272) correctly uses Object.entries instead.
failure_scenario: If any enumerable property exists on Object.prototype (from a polyfill or library), the loop would process it as a budget category, creating unexpected keys like 'toStringBudget' on the returned object. This malformed object would then be sent to the API on save via normalizeOnDemandBudget.

summary: Removed fallback for mktemp failure. Old version had 'mktemp /tmp/sentry.envrc.$$.out || mktemp /tmp/sentry.envrc.XXXXXXXX.out' but new version has only the primary mktemp call with no fallback.
failure_scenario: If /tmp is full or unwritable, the old code would try a second mktemp pattern as a fallback. The new code fails immediately, causing error-reporting log capture to be silently broken for that direnv session.

summary: Removed migration 0936 that added a composite index on (feature, organization_id, project_id) for PromptsActivity, and simultaneously removed the equivalent inline Meta indexes from the model. Queries in seer_setup.py filter on exactly these three fields and would benefit from this index.
failure_scenario: Calls to get_seer_user_acknowledgement() and get_seer_org_acknowledgement() filter PromptsActivity by (feature, organization_id, project_id) with no existing composite index. At scale, this results in sequential scans instead of index scans. Additionally, a future makemigrations would generate a DROP INDEX migration since the Meta definition was removed.

summary: visit_Call_Expr_Node mutates AST node name via 'for node.name.name in dict' loop, appending the same node N times and corrupting the call target name to an arbitrary last dict key rather than checking if the call target is in the dict
failure_scenario: A Call_Expr_Node for 'allocated_test_nested' has its name overwritten to whichever function key appears last in self.functions_with_alloc dict order. The same node is appended to call_nodes for every key regardless of match. Downstream at line 1829, alloc_nodes is fetched for the wrong (mutated) function name, generating flag variable names for the wrong subroutine.

summary: Allocatable flag variable names derived from callee's renamed parameter don't exist in caller scope after assign_globally_unique_variable_names is enabled
failure_scenario: Entry point 'allocated_test' has allocatable arg 'data' (not renamed). Nested subroutine 'allocated_test_nested' has same-named allocatable arg 'data' renamed to 'data_var_0'. The allocatableReplacer generates call-site flag argument '__f2dace_ALLOCATED_data_var_0' from the callee's renamed name, but only '__f2dace_ALLOCATED_data' exists in the caller's scope. SDFG creation fails with undefined variable '__f2dace_ALLOCATED_data_var_0'.

summary: assign_globally_unique_variable_names generates unique names like 'd_var_0' without checking whether a user-defined variable with that exact name already exists, risking name collision
failure_scenario: A Fortran program defines a variable named 'd_var_0' in one module, and another variable 'd' in a different module collides. The rename generates 'd_var_0' for the second one, creating two distinct variables with the same name 'd_var_0', breaking all references that rely on unique names.

summary: Rewritten pointer test lost all correctness assertions; test now only validates SDFG structure without compiling or running, removing regression coverage for pointer-to-array semantics
failure_scenario: A future change breaks pointer dereferencing (e.g., p_area(1,1,1) resolves to wrong element). The old test would have caught this via 'assert np.allclose(lout[0], 6.5)'. The new test only calls validate() and simplify() and will silently pass regardless of output correctness.

summary: Dual-lock failure leaks the first CPU's FileChannel, FileLock, and lock file because releaseLock(id) is called before locks[id] was assigned
failure_scenario: Two processes share an HT box. Process A locks CPU 4 independently. Process B calls acquireCore(), trying to lock core 0 (CPUs 0 and 4). tryAcquireLockOnFile(0) succeeds, producing a valid lockReference. tryAcquireLockOnFile(4) then fails (returns null) because Process A holds the lock on CPU 4. At line 118, releaseLock(0) is called, but locks[0] is null (never assigned at lines 113-115 since that code only runs when BOTH locks succeed). releaseLock(0) checks locks[0] != null at line 184, finds null, returns false without closing the live FileChannel + FileLock in lockReference or deleting the lock file. The lockReference variable falls out of scope on line 121 with the channel+lock still open. CPU 0's lock file remains on disk with an exclusive OS file lock held until JVM exit or GC-triggered Cleaner close, which is indefinite. All subsequent attempts to acquire CPU 0 (by any process) fail permanently.

summary: Crew detection logic silently breaks support for the class-based factory pattern (callable with crew() method) -- only module-level Crew instances are now found
failure_scenario: A user's crew.py defines `class MyCrew: def crew(self): return Crew(...)` (the previous supported pattern). get_crew() iterates module attributes, finds MyCrew (a class, not a Crew instance), isinstance(attr, Crew) is False, so it is skipped. No matching attribute is ever found, the function returns None, and reset_memories_command raises ValueError('No crew found.'). Previously, callable(MyCrew) was True, hasattr(MyCrew, 'crew') was True, and MyCrew().crew() returned the Crew instance successfully.

summary: ImportError handler uses parameter name 'crew_path' instead of full OS path 'crew_os_path', degrading diagnostic error messages
failure_scenario: A user's crew.py has a syntax error or missing import. The except block formats the error as 'Error importing crew from crew.py: No module named X'. The old code used the reassigned crew_path variable (full path like '<HOME>/myproject/crew.py'), which told the user exactly which file failed. Now the message shows only the basename parameter, so if multiple crew.py files exist in different directories, the user cannot identify which one caused the error.

summary: Documentation typo: 'KNOWLEDEGE' is misspelled (extra 'E' before the final 'E') -- should be 'KNOWLEDGE'
failure_scenario: Users reading the docs see 'Reset KNOWLEDEGE storage' in the CLI options table, which is confusing and looks unprofessional. The actual CLI option and code use the correct spelling 'knowledge'. This has no functional impact but misleads readers.

summary: Removed [650, 1168] from SUPPORTED_AD_SIZES, causing bid requests for that ad size to be rejected by isBidRequestValid when they were previously accepted
failure_scenario: A publisher has ad slots of size 650x1168 configured for the condorx bidder. Since [650, 1168] is no longer in SUPPORTED_AD_SIZES, isValidAdSize([650, 1168]) returns false, isBidRequestValid returns false, and the bid request is dropped silently — no bids are returned for that ad slot. The engageya adapter in the same codebase still lists [650, 1168] as a supported size, confirming this is a real ad dimension in use.

summary: Silent attribute data loss: (attributes as IReadOnlyList<AttributeStatement>) ?? [] drops all attributes when a non-IReadOnlyList IEnumerable is passed (e.g. LINQ Where() result); same bug at line 73. ConstructorProvider.Update at line 105 correctly uses ?? [.. attributes] as fallback.
failure_scenario: Caller passes attributes: someList.Where(a => a.Type == typeof(ObsoleteAttribute)) to the constructor — the as cast returns null for the LINQ iterator, and [] replaces all attributes with an empty list, silently discarding them. ConstructorProvider.Update in the same file uses the correct [.. attributes] fallback, proving the fix was known but not applied uniformly.

summary: Same silent attribute data loss in MethodProvider constructors (lines 52, 74) and Update (line 106): (attributes as IReadOnlyList<AttributeStatement>) ?? [] drops non-IReadOnlyList enumerables.
failure_scenario: Same as above — any caller passing a LINQ query or iterator result for attributes gets them silently dropped. MethodProvider.Accept at line 124 also copies updated.Attributes without verifying it is non-null, so a visitor returning a mock with uninitialized Attributes would propagate null to CodeWriter methods that access .Attributes.Count, causing NullReferenceException.

summary: Same silent attribute data loss in FieldProvider constructor (line 69) and new Update method (line 130). Additionally, FieldProvider.Update only re-initializes _parameter (the Lazy<ParameterProvider>) when 'name' changes (line 104), but not when only type/wireInfo/description/attributes change — causing stale cached parameter if AsParameter was already evaluated.
failure_scenario: Data loss: same as above. Stale parameter: field is created with Type=int, AsParameter is accessed and caches a ParameterProvider with Type=int. Then field.Update(type: stringType) changes Type to string, but _parameter's Lazy already holds the old ParameterProvider, so AsParameter returns a ParameterProvider with Type=int.

summary: Same silent attribute data loss in PropertyProvider constructor (line 127) and Update (line 303). Additionally, PropertyProvider.Update does not invalidate cached _variable (AsVariableExpression), _asMember (MemberExpression implicit conversion), or _parameter (AsParameter) when type/name change, unlike FieldProvider.Update which does handle _variable and _asMember.
failure_scenario: Data loss: same as above. Stale caches: property.Update(type: newType, name: 'newName'); then AsVariableExpression returns a VariableExpression still holding the old type and old name; the implicit MemberExpression cast returns old name.

summary: Same silent attribute data loss in ParameterProvider constructor (line 100) and Update (line 303). Additionally, the Attributes property lost its default = [] initializer when visibility was widened from internal to public, relying solely on constructors to initialize it.
failure_scenario: Data loss: same as above. Missing default: if any reflection-based or deserialization-based construction path creates a ParameterProvider without going through a constructor that sets Attributes (e.g. FormatterServices.GetUninitializedObject), Attributes stays null and CodeWriter.WriteParameter at line 436 would throw NullReferenceException on accessing Attributes.Count.

summary: TypeProvider.Update uses the correct [.. attributes] fallback (line 465), unlike the other 9 locations in ConstructorProvider, MethodProvider, FieldProvider, PropertyProvider, and ParameterProvider constructors/Updates that silently drop non-IReadOnlyList enumerables via ?? [].
failure_scenario: This location is correct, but its existence proves the correct pattern was known. The 9 wrong locations in the other files should be changed to match this pattern (using [.. attributes] or OrDefaultIfEmpty equivalent as fallback).

summary: Unused import: using System.Reflection.Metadata; was added but no type from this namespace is referenced anywhere in the file. Likely an IDE auto-complete mistake (confused with System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis where ExperimentalAttribute lives).
failure_scenario: No crash, but the unused import pollutes the namespace, may cause confusion during maintenance, and suggests the wrong namespace was added instead of System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis if ExperimentalAttribute references were intended here.

summary: CSV support removed from SUPPORTED_MIME_TYPES, UI, and all tests, but MIME_TYPES_SUPPORTED in GeminiExtractor still maps 'text/csv' to Kind.DOCUMENT; unit test and paid integration test for CSV were both removed, leaving no regression coverage for the still-functional extractor code path.
failure_scenario: An existing CSV document in the database gets extracted via ExtractorRunner -> GeminiExtractor._extract -> _get_kind_from_mime_type('text/csv'), which still returns Kind.DOCUMENT. If a Gemini API model update later breaks or changes CSV extraction behavior, no existing test will catch it because test_get_kind_from_mime_type no longer parametrizes 'text/csv' and test_extract_csv was deleted entirely.

summary: onScroll now calls C.ChatReadMessages individually per unread message instead of batching them into a single range-based call via onReadStop, causing N server roundtrips per scroll-stop instead of 1
failure_scenario: User scrolls through a chat with 80 unread messages. Old code: 1 batched ChatReadMessages(range) call after scroll-stop. New code: 80 individual ChatReadMessages(orderId, orderId) calls spread across scroll events, multiplying network requests and server load with no compensatory benefit.

summary: timeoutScrollStop class property is dead code — initialized to 0 and cleared in componentWillUnmount but never assigned a timer ID after the scroll-stop debounce was removed from onScroll
failure_scenario: The property wastes a few bytes of instance memory and window.clearTimeout(0) at unmount is a harmless no-op. The deferred-batch mechanism it supported was replaced by the immediate-read approach, leaving this leftover.

summary: When only one of system_template or prompt_template is provided, the user's custom template is silently discarded and defaults are used with no warning
failure_scenario: User creates Agent with system_template='You are a helpful AI' but forgets prompt_template (leaving it None). _build_prompt's condition 'not system_template or not prompt_template' evaluates True, falls back to default I18N formatting. The user's custom system prompt is never used, and no warning indicates this.

summary: Available-variable list incorrectly drops {input}, which is still replaced downstream by CrewAgentExecutor (line 370: prompt.replace('{input}', inputs['input']))
failure_scenario: User reads the updated docs, sees only {role}/{goal}/{backstory} listed, removes {input} from their custom prompt_template thinking it is unavailable. The template no longer receives the actual task input at runtime, silently producing prompts with literal '{input}' text instead of the real task description.

summary: Copy-paste error in test docstring: test_agent_with_only_prompt_template says 'only system_template' but the test exercises prompt_template only
failure_scenario: Developer debugging a test failure sees the misleading docstring, wastes time looking at the wrong template configuration. The test body is correct (it tests prompt_template= alone), but the docstring is wrong.

summary: Three new tests only verify Agent construction succeeds; none call create_agent_executor() or execute_task(), so the _build_prompt fix (core of this PR) is not exercised
failure_scenario: A regression in _build_prompt's template handling (e.g., a misplaced f-string interpolation or wrong variable scope) would pass all three new tests because they stop at Agent() creation and never trigger _build_prompt execution.

summary: ToolCommand.login() accesses current_organization['uuid']/'name' without checking if the key exists or is None, crashing on valid-but-unexpected login responses.
failure_scenario: The login API returns a 200 response that lacks the 'current_organization' key (e.g., backend change or user has no organization). A KeyError propagates as an unhandled exception, producing a full traceback to the user instead of a controlled error message.

summary: ToolCommand.login() saves org context to Settings but does not update the already-constructed self.plus_api_client.headers; subsequent API calls in the same process (publish_tool, get_tool) lack the X-Crewai-Organization-Id header.
failure_scenario: User runs 'crewai tool publish --public' without a pre-set organization. login() succeeds, writes the returned org UUID to Settings, then publish() calls self.plus_api_client.publish_tool() — but the PlusAPI instance was created before login so its headers dict lacks X-Crewai-Organization-Id. The publish request either fails with a 403 or publishes to an incorrect org scope.

summary: The org group has invoke_without_command=True but the handler body is just 'pass', so 'crewai org' silently exits with no output instead of showing the current organization.
failure_scenario: User runs 'crewai org' (without a subcommand) expecting to see the currently selected organization. The command exits silently with exit code 0 and no output, giving zero feedback.

summary: When switch() cannot find the requested organization ID, it prints an error and returns normally (exit code 0) instead of raising SystemExit(1), inconsistent with all other error paths in the codebase.
failure_scenario: A script runs 'crewai org switch invalid-id && echo switched'. The switch fails silently (exit 0), the 'echo switched' runs, and the user believes the switch succeeded when it did not.

summary: list() and switch() access org['name'] and org['uuid'] with bare bracket notation; if the API returns an incomplete org object, a KeyError produces a misleading error message.
failure_scenario: API returns an org dict missing the 'name' field. list() hits a KeyError, the broad except catches it, and the user sees 'Failed to retrieve organization list: 'name'' — the user thinks the API call failed when it actually succeeded but the response format was unexpected.

summary: OrganizationCommand.switch() and ToolCommand.login() duplicate the org-setting logic (assign org_name, org_uuid, call dump()), risking drift between the two implementations.
failure_scenario: A future maintainer adds org-field validation to switch() but misses the identical logic in login(). The two code paths now enforce different rules, and login()-based flows (tool publish, tool install) accept org states that switch() rejects.

summary: Dead code: _log_feedback_error (lines 588-596) and _log_max_retries_exceeded (lines 598-606) are never called after _get_llm_feedback_response was removed; import of MAX_LLM_RETRY at line 20 is now only used in these dead methods
failure_scenario: Developers reading this code will be misled into thinking these methods are part of active error-handling paths; they consume the MAX_LLM_RETRY constant import and add maintenance burden with no benefit

summary: Stale @pytest.mark.vcr decorator on test_agent_human_input references a deleted cassette file (tests/cassettes/test_agent_human_input.yaml) and is unnecessary since _invoke_loop is now mocked
failure_scenario: The VCR marker is misleading -- it suggests the test uses cassette replay when it actually patches _invoke_loop to avoid all HTTP calls. The decorator serves no purpose and will confuse future maintainers

summary: Test coverage regression: _invoke_loop is patched with a fixed return_value=AgentFinish(output='Hello'), so the test cannot verify that _process_feedback_iteration properly appends feedback to messages or that the LLM processes feedback correctly
failure_scenario: If _process_feedback_iteration had a bug (e.g., it fails to append the feedback instructions to self.messages before calling _invoke_loop), the test would still pass because the mock always returns 'Hello' regardless of the actual message state. The deleted cassette test previously verified real LLM feedback processing behavior

summary: pip_release is 'autogen-agentchat' but version constraints target 0.2.x; 'autogen-agentchat' only has 0.4.x+ releases
failure_scenario: CI version matrix (dev/set_matrix.py) calls get_released_versions('autogen-agentchat') which returns only >=0.4.0 versions, then min=0.2.36/max=0.2.40 plus unsupported=['>=0.4'] filter out everything, yielding zero test configurations and silently skipping autogen CI. Also, user-facing version-warning messages in mlflow/utils/autologging_utils/__init__.py:391 tell users to upgrade/downgrade 'autogen-agentchat' when they actually need 'autogen'. The generated ml_package_versions.py:297 has the same wrong pip_release. The requirements/extra-ml-requirements.txt correctly uses 'autogen' (0.2.x), confirming this yml entry is stale.

summary: _get_top_level_retrieval_spans excludes a retriever span when walking the parent chain hits a missing ancestor, even though no retriever ancestor was found
failure_scenario: A retriever span has a non-retriever parent whose own parent_id references a span outside this trace (e.g. a cross-trace reference or pruned upstream span). The while loop at line 126 does all_spans.get(parent_id), gets None, breaks out, and the for-else does not add the span. The retriever span — which has genuine document outputs — is silently dropped from extract_retrieval_context_from_trace. Fix: treat a missing ancestor as reaching the root (append the span) rather than breaking.

summary: parse_inputs_to_str returns list(inputs.values())[0] for single-key dicts, which may be a non-string type, violating the -> str return annotation
failure_scenario: Caller passes parse_inputs_to_str({'query': ['multi', 'part', 'prompt']}) expecting a string for judges API compatibility. The function returns the list ['multi', 'part', 'prompt'] instead of its JSON serialization. Downstream code that builds HTTP request bodies with the result would serialize incorrectly or raise a TypeError when the non-string is used where a string is expected.

summary: set_span_chat_messages type hint narrowed from list[Union[dict, ChatMessage]] to Union[dict, ChatMessage] despite all 15+ callers passing a list
failure_scenario: Static type checkers (mypy/pyright) will report errors at every call site (e.g. mlflow/anthropic/autolog.py:110, mlflow/bedrock/_autolog.py:188, mlflow/crewai/chat.py:24, mlflow/dspy/callback.py:121, mlflow/gemini/autolog.py:63, mlflow/groq/_groq_autolog.py:50, mlflow/langchain/langchain_tracer.py:231, etc.) because they pass list[dict] to a parameter typed as Union[dict, ChatMessage]. No runtime impact since types are not enforced, but this breaks type-checking CI and IDE assistance.

summary: extract_retrieval_context_from_trace docstring says 'Only consider the last retrieval span' but the implementation returns all top-level retrieval spans
failure_scenario: A caller reading the docstring expects a single retrieval context (the last one) but receives a dict mapping multiple span_ids to their documents, causing downstream code that assumes a single context to process more data than expected or to mishandle the multi-key dict. The test at tests/genai/utils/test_trace_utils.py:211 also has a contradictory comment ('only take the last top-level one') while asserting both spans are included.

summary: Missing `assert batch_size > 0` guard in Producer.run() causes silent busy-loop with zero throughput when batch_size=0
failure_scenario: User runs `benchmark --enqueue-batch-size 0`. Old code would raise AssertionError immediately at the former `assert batch_size > 0` inside `producer()`. New code enters Producer.run(), creates `entrypoints = []` (empty list from `["syncfetch", "asyncfetch"] * 0`), and loops calling `self.queries.enqueue([], [], [])` which returns `[]` without error -- a database round-trip doing nothing each cycle. The benchmark completes with 0 steps and 0 rate, misleading the user into thinking the system cannot process jobs.

summary: Removal of reshape(-1) causes 0-D numpy arrays to crash with TypeError instead of being handled gracefully
failure_scenario: Calling model.predict(np.array(42)) passes the supported_input_types check, reaches line 123 where len(np.array(42)) raises TypeError: len() of unsized object. The old code's reshape(-1) converted 0-D to 1-D before the length check.

summary: yaml.dump rewrites tspconfig.yaml unconditionally even when the inner guard (line 423) is false and no api-version mutation occurred; the file is reformatted (comments stripped) but the api-version override is silently not applied, with no warning logged
failure_scenario: Input data contains apiVersion='2023-01-01' but tspconfig.yaml has no @azure-tools/typespec-python key under options. The file is rewritten by yaml.dump (losing all comments and reformatting), but the api-version is never set. The code generator runs with the wrong (default) api-version, and no warning tells the operator the override was silently dropped.

summary: yaml.safe_load returns None for empty or comment-only YAML files; subsequent content.get('options', {}) at line 423 raises AttributeError on NoneType, crashing gen_typespec with a misleading failure message
failure_scenario: A tspconfig.yaml file exists but is empty (0 bytes) or contains only comments (e.g., '# WIP'). yaml.safe_load returns None. Line 423 calls content.get('options', {}) on None, raising AttributeError. The error propagates to the caller's except Exception handler, which logs 'fail to generate sdk' even though code generation never started.

summary: Adding onInput={handleInput} alongside the existing onChange causes the parent onChange callback to fire twice per slider tick
failure_scenario: User drags the range slider: React's synthetic onChange fires handleInput (via the wrapper), and onInput also fires handleInput directly. Both call onChange?.(value, e) on the parent callback. If the parent uses onChange to persist data (e.g., a debounced network save), each drag tick produces duplicate writes/requests.

summary: getAlertsUrl call does not pass the interval parameter, unlike the deleted CreateAlertButton which used useChartInterval() to pass it
failure_scenario: A chart is displayed at a 5-minute interval. User clicks the chart actions dropdown and selects 'Create Alert for' a metric. The alert URL is generated without the interval parameter, defaulting to 1h in getAlertsUrl (getInterval returns '1h' for undefined input). The resulting alert rule uses a 1h interval instead of matching the chart's 5m interval, causing the alert to evaluate at the wrong granularity.

summary: Removed conditional merge of STATIC_SEMVER_TAGS into stringAttributes when SpanIndexedField.RELEASE is present in EAP span search, removing semver filter keys
failure_scenario: A user searches EAP spans and the release field is available from the backend. Previously, STATIC_SEMVER_TAGS (release.build, release.package, release.version.*, etc.) were merged into the filter keys, providing autocomplete and filtering for semver sub-fields. With this merge removed, those filter keys are no longer suggested or accepted, so users cannot filter spans by release.build or release.package even though the span data contains those fields.

summary: CRITICAL: Inner scanner goroutine does not return after detecting context cancellation, continues sending to outputChan which the outer goroutine may have already closed via defer close(fr.outputChan), causing a panic (send on closed channel) or a goroutine leak (if the outer select picks ctx.Done() instead of errChan).
failure_scenario: Input has 5 lines, context is cancelled after line 2. Inner goroutine detects cancellation on line 3, sends ctx.Err() to errChan (line 144), but falls through to line 147-149 sending line 3 to outputChan. Then scanner.Scan() returns true for line 4, inner goroutine detects cancellation again, tries errChan <- ctx.Err() on line 144 — blocks if errChan still full. If outer goroutine receives and returns, defer close(fr.outputChan) fires. Inner goroutine unblocks, sends ctx.Err() to now-empty errChan, reaches line 149 (fr.outputChan <- line) → PANIC on closed channel. If outer goroutine picks ctx.Done() instead, inner goroutine blocks forever on errChan send → goroutine leak.

summary: Race condition in outer select: when inner goroutine sends io.EOF to errChan (line 155) and immediately calls cancel() (line 156), both errChan and ctx.Done() become ready simultaneously. Go's select picks non-deterministically, so Run may return context.Canceled instead of io.EOF for normal EOF termination, breaking the API contract and causing TestFileReader_EmptyFile to fail intermittently.
failure_scenario: Create FileReader with empty file. Inner goroutine: scanner.Scan() returns false immediately, scanner.Err() is nil, errChan <- io.EOF sent, cancel() called. Outer select (line 160) has both cases ready (errChan with io.EOF, ctx.Done() because cancel() just fired). If ctx.Done() wins (~50% probability), Run returns context.Canceled instead of io.EOF. TestFileReader_EmptyFile checks err != io.EOF → test fails intermittently.

summary: cancel() is not called when the scanner encounters an error (line 151-153); it is only called in the else branch (line 156). When the input reader fails (e.g., permission error on stdin), FileReader returns the error but the engine continues running because no cancellation is propagated to sibling workers.
failure_scenario: os.Stdin encounters a read error mid-operation. Scanner.Err() returns non-nil. Inner goroutine sends the error to errChan (line 153) but never calls cancel(). Outer goroutine receives the error and returns. defer close(fr.outputChan) fires. HTTPPostSender sees closed inputChan and returns nil. But OutputProxy and SSEWorker keep running because no ctx cancellation was triggered. runWorkersAndWait blocks on wg.Wait() forever because the remaining workers never exit. Engine hangs until process is killed.

summary: io.EOF is logged as 'Error reading input' via fr.logger.Errorw on line 162. When the scanner reaches EOF normally, io.EOF is sent through errChan and logged at error level. This is misleading — EOF is normal end-of-input, not an error — and additionally causes runWorkersAndWait (line 101) to log 'Worker exited with error' for normal termination.
failure_scenario: Engine runs normally, stdin provides input and then closes (EOF). FileReader reaches EOF, sends io.EOF through errChan. Outer select receives io.EOF, logs 'Error reading input err=EOF' at error level. Then runWorkersAndWait logs 'Worker exited with error err=EOF'. Operators investigating logs see error-level messages for what is normal shutdown behavior.

summary: Loop variable 'name' is captured by reference in the goroutine closure at line 97-102. In Go, range loop variables are reused across iterations, so by the time goroutines execute their log statements (lines 99 and 101), 'name' may contain the value from a later iteration, reporting incorrect worker names.
failure_scenario: Workers map has keys 'file-reader', 'http-post', 'stdout'. Goroutine for 'file-reader' starts but is not immediately scheduled. Loop continues to next iteration, 'name' is now 'http-post'. First goroutine finally runs: logs 'Starting worker worker-name=http-post' for what is actually the file-reader worker, and later logs 'Worker exited with error worker-name=http-post' for the file-reader's result. Tracing and debugging is misled by wrong worker names in logs.

summary: The 'reachedEOF' boolean field (read on line 27, written on line 34) has no synchronization — no mutex, no atomic. If multiple goroutines read from the same BlockReader concurrently, there is a data race. Currently only bufio.Scanner (single-goroutine) reads from it, but the type is exported and the assumption is fragile.
failure_scenario: Two goroutines share a BlockReader and call Read concurrently. Goroutine A reads reachedEOF (line 27) as false while goroutine B sets it to true (line 34). This is a data race. Go race detector flags it. If reachedEOF is non-atomically written while being read, the read may observe a partial/incorrect value, causing the reader to either falsely block (thinking EOF was already reached) or falsely read (thinking EOF was not yet reached when it was).

summary: Several test functions (TestFileReader_FileError at io_test.go:137, TestOutputProxy_WriteFails at io_test.go:197, TestHTTPPostSender_InvalidURL at http_test.go:137, TestSSEWorker_EventChannelClosure at sse_test.go:307) create a cancel context with context.WithCancel but never call cancel() and have no defer cancel(), leaking the context and its internal propagateCancel goroutine.
failure_scenario: Test creates ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()), passes cancel to Run(). Run returns (due to error or channel closure), but cancel is never invoked. The propagateCancel goroutine started internally by context.WithCancel blocks forever on parent.Done() (Background, never fires) and child.Done() (child never cancelled). Each leaked goroutine holds ~4KB of stack. Accumulates over test runs. This is a regression: the old code used context.Background() (no cancel context) and had no leak.

summary: Firecrawl Search Tool sidebar entry was replaced (not augmented) by Oxylabs, orphaning the still-existing firecrawlsearchtool.mdx page from sidebar navigation while the overview page still links to it
failure_scenario: A user navigating the docs sidebar under 'Web Scraping & Browsing' no longer sees Firecrawl Search Tool. The firecrawlsearchtool.mdx page file still exists on disk at docs/tools/web-scraping/firecrawlsearchtool.mdx and the overview page at docs/tools/web-scraping/overview.mdx line 28 still shows a Card linking to it, but there is zero sidebar entry for it anywhere in docs.json — the page is effectively hidden from discovery unless the user clicks through from the overview CardGroup.

summary: Wrong domain description in OxylabsAmazonSearchScraperTool parameters: 'Domain localization for Bestbuy' should say 'Amazon' (this is an Amazon search tool, not Bestbuy)
failure_scenario: A developer reading the OxylabsAmazonSearchScraperTool parameter docs sees 'Domain localization for Bestbuy' for the domain parameter and is confused about whether this is an Amazon or Bestbuy tool, or worse, configures a Bestbuy domain for an Amazon search query.

summary: Typo in frontmatter description: 'Google Seach' should be 'Google Search'
failure_scenario: The published documentation page displays 'Google Seach' as one of the available scraper sources, a visible typo that reduces trust in documentation accuracy.

summary: handle_llm_tool_usage_started, handle_llm_tool_usage_finished, and handle_llm_tool_usage_error all print to console unconditionally without checking the verbose flag
failure_scenario: User sets verbose=False on the formatter. When an LLM executes a tool via available_functions, all three handlers still call self.print() and self.print_panel(), emitting tool-usage tree output and error panels to the console that the user explicitly disabled. The existing handle_tool_usage_started/finished/error methods (lines 475-585) all guard with 'if not self.verbose: return' -- the new LLM variants lack this guard.

summary: get_llm_tree() mutates the shared tree by calling tree.add(text) each time it is invoked, and it is invoked independently by handle_llm_tool_usage_started, handle_llm_tool_usage_finished, and handle_llm_tool_usage_error, producing duplicate 'Using X from LLM available_function' nodes in the console tree
failure_scenario: A successful LLM tool call fires ToolUsageStartedEvent then ToolUsageFinishedEvent. handle_llm_tool_usage_started calls get_llm_tree() which adds a 'Using get_weather...' node at line 437; then handle_llm_tool_usage_finished also calls get_llm_tree() which adds a second identical node. The tree ends up with two 'Using...' nodes, both 'Tool Usage Started' and 'Tool Usage Completed' nodes present, and the started node is never updated to show completion. In the original non-LLM path, the same tool branch is tracked via current_tool_branch and updated in-place -- the new LLM path creates divergent nodes instead.

summary: current_llm_tool_tree is declared as a class attribute on ConsoleFormatter but is never assigned or read by any method
failure_scenario: Dead code adds maintenance burden. The attribute was apparently intended to track the LLM tool tree across started/finished/error lifecycles (analogous to current_tool_branch in the non-LLM path) but was never wired up, leaving the duplication bugs above unresolved.

summary: wc_tsip_AesCtr uses uninitialized 'ret' when aes->ctx.keySize is neither 16 nor 32, causing silent success without encryption/decryption
failure_scenario: A caller uses AES-192 (keySize=24) with wc_tsip_AesCtr. After tsip_hw_lock() returns 0 (TSIP_SUCCESS), neither the keySize==16 nor keySize==32 branch executes, leaving ret==0. The 'if (ret == TSIP_SUCCESS)' check passes, the IV counter is advanced, tsip_hw_unlock() is called, and the function returns 0 (success). No encryption/decryption was performed -- the output buffer contains unencrypted data. Contrast with wc_tsip_AesCbcEncrypt at line 574 which correctly returns -1 for unrecognized keySize.

summary: Missing 'out' and 'outLen' declarations in non-SMALL_STACK path when HAVE_ECC_DHE is defined but HAVE_ECC_SIGN is not, causing compilation failure
failure_scenario: Building with -DHAVE_ECC -DHAVE_ECC_DHE -DNO_ECC_SIGN (all valid independent flags per settings.h lines 2995-3015). In the non-SMALL_STACK path, 'byte out[256]' and 'word32 outLen' are only declared inside '#if defined(HAVE_ECC_SIGN) && defined(HAVE_ECC_VERIFY)' at line 59542, but 'out' and 'outLen' are used at line 59627 inside '#ifdef HAVE_ECC_DHE' for wc_ecc_shared_secret(key, pub, out, &outLen). Compiler errors on undefined identifiers.

summary: WOLFSSL_NO_GETPID safeguard removed from WOLFSSL_LINUXKM section, risking getpid() call in kernel context
failure_scenario: Building wolfSSL as a Linux Kernel Module (WOLFSSL_LINUXKM defined) where HAVE_GETPID happens to be defined (e.g., from a config.h). The removed '#define WOLFSSL_NO_GETPID' previously forced WOLFSSL_NO_GETPID on, preventing random.c lines 1671-1672 and 2045-2047 from calling getpid() -- which is unavailable in kernel space. Without this guard, the kernel module calls getpid(), causing a linker error (unresolved symbol) or kernel panic at runtime.

summary: Copy-paste error: 'dec->ctx.keySize = enc->keylen' should be 'dec->keylen' in tsip_aes256_ctr_test
failure_scenario: In the 256-bit CTR test, the decryption key's keySize is set from 'enc->keylen' instead of 'dec->keylen'. The 128-bit version (line 323) correctly uses 'dec->keylen'. Currently both keys are 256-bit so the value is identical, but if the test or the SetKeyDirect call for 'dec' were ever changed to use a different key size, the decryption object would carry the wrong keySize value, causing the hardware CTR call to fail or use the wrong algorithm.

summary: Pre-existing: XMALLOC(sizeof(byte)) allocates 1 byte for 'out' pointer used as 256-byte buffer in SMALL_STACK path
failure_scenario: In the SMALL_STACK with malloc path, 'out' is allocated as 1 byte via 'XMALLOC(sizeof(byte), ...)'. If the crypto callback fails to intercept (returns NOT_COMPILED_IN), wc_ecc_sign_hash or wc_ecc_shared_secret writes up to 256 bytes of ECC data into this 1-byte buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow. Pre-existing in base commit but re-exposed by the extensive restructuring of this function in the diff.

summary: Copy-paste error: AES-GCM async HW condition checks WC_ASYNC_ENABLE_3DES instead of WC_ASYNC_ENABLE_AES
failure_scenario: When WOLFSSL_ASYNC_CRYPT and WC_ASYNC_ENABLE_AES are defined (the correct AES async flag per wolfssl/wolfcrypt/aes.h line 370), but WC_ASYNC_ENABLE_3DES is not defined, the HW AES-GCM benchmark at line 3269 is silently skipped. summary: Missing #ifndef NO_SW_BENCH guard for bench_cmac(0) despite having a BENCH_DEVID HW counterpart at line 3554 — the diff adds this guard to bench_aesctr and bench_curve25519KeyGen but misses this identical case

summary: Missing #ifndef NO_SW_BENCH guard for bench_curve25519KeyAgree(0) despite having a BENCH_DEVID HW counterpart at line 3853 — same incomplete-fix pattern as bench_aesctr/bench_curve25519KeyGen
failure_scenario: On Renesas platforms with NO_SW_BENCH defined, the software Curve25519 key agreement benchmark compiles and runs when only HW benchmarks are desired. summary: Operator precedence: && !defined(NO_HW_BENCH) only gates the MAX3266X sub-condition, not the entire AES-GCM HW condition — HW bench can fire when NO_HW_BENCH is defined
failure_scenario: Define both NO_HW_BENCH and WOLFSSL_ASYNC_CRYPT (or HAVE_RENESAS_SYNC, or WOLFSSL_CAAM, etc.). Due to C preprocessor precedence (&& binds tighter than ||), the expression becomes 'A || (B && !NO_HW_BENCH)'. Since WOLFSSL_ASYNC_CRYPT is in the 'A' group (not gated by NO_HW_BENCH), the condition evaluates to true and bench_aes_aad_options_wrap(bench_aesgcm, 1) compiles and runs despite NO_HW_BENCH. The fix needs outer parentheses: (A || B) && !defined(NO_HW_BENCH).

summary: OpenAIOnlineRequestProcessor does not override compatible_provider property, causing online status tracker to show $0.000 per-token pricing for external providers like inference.net
failure_scenario: Using curator.LLM(model_name='meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct/fp-16', backend='inference.net') in online mode → process_requests_from_file() passes compatible_provider=self.compatible_provider to OnlineStatusTracker, but the inherited property from BaseOnlineRequestProcessor returns 'base' (not 'inference.net'). summary: Example file uses response[0]['response'] while the batch counterpart and all klusterai examples use response['response'] without list indexing
failure_scenario: If a user copies the inference_net_online.py example verbatim, and the LLM call returns a Dataset (dict-like access pattern as used by all other provider examples), accessing response[0] would raise a TypeError because dict objects are not subscriptable by integer. summary: Race condition: new await introduces an async suspension point in a previously synchronous code path inside a useEffect with no abort/cleanup mechanism; concurrent effect re-runs can race on paintMapRef.current and React state
failure_scenario: User opens painter panel on an existing non-aggregated paint map (same-channel editing path). The new await decompressBitMap(...) begins. Before it completes, user changes a column via another UI control. MobX triggers a useEffect re-run with a different paintInfo (e.g., new dimensions). Both IIFEs execute concurrently — the first run's decompress completes later and overwrites paintMapRef.current and React state (setDict, setDomainX, etc.) with stale data from the old encoding, corrupting the paint editor display and potentially the saved paint map.

summary: Missing error handling: painter useEffect does not handle paintInfo returning { type: 'error', ... }, causing an infinite loading spinner; the new validation in visualSpecStore.ts makes this reachable for the existPaintField path
failure_scenario: User opens the painter panel with a valid encoding. While the panel is open, user changes a column to a temporal type (or adds/removes columns so count != 1). paintInfo now returns { type: 'error', key: 'temporal' } due to the new validation at visualSpecStore.ts line 310. The useEffect re-runs: setLoading(true) fires, then destructures paintInfo. The 'if (paintInfo)' block is entered (error objects are truthy), but no branch matches 'error'. setLoading(false) is never called. The loading spinner persists indefinitely until the user manually closes the dialog. The same gap also swallows any exception thrown by decompressBitMap or other async operations inside the untry-wrapped async IIFE.

summary: Duplicated validation logic: the columns/rows count check, aggName check, and field ID checks at lines 304-324 in paintInfo are identical to those in paintFields at lines 237-257 (non-aggregated) and partially overlap lines 265-281 (aggregated); any future change to these rules must be made in three places
failure_scenario: Maintenance burden. A developer adding a new paint restriction (e.g., blocking 'ordinal' type) to paintFields may forget to also update paintInfo's pre-validation, causing the existPaintField path to bypass the new restriction and return exist data for an invalid encoding. The dual-layer validation is defensive but the cost is divergence risk.

summary: Missing temporal check in paintFields aggregated path: the non-aggregated path (line 243) rejects temporal fields but the aggregated path (line 265) does not; now papered over by paintInfo's new validation but latent inconsistency remains
failure_scenario: If paintFields is ever consumed directly (not through paintInfo), aggregated paint configurations with temporal columns would be generated despite temporal paint being unsupported ('range on temporal need use a temporal Domain, which is not implemented'). The resulting invalid paint map would fail at render time with a cryptic error rather than a clear validation message.

summary: pubProvidedId was removed from the user.ext object in getOpenRTBUserObject, dropping all publisher-provided user identifiers from the bid request sent to the ad exchange
failure_scenario: A publisher configures the pubProvidedId user ID module. Prebid.js populates bidderRequest.userId.pubProvidedId with the publisher's user identifier. When the Adot adapter calls getOpenRTBUserObject() to build the OpenRTB request, the returned user.ext object no longer includes pubProvidedId. The ad exchange receives a user object with only the GDPR consent string and no user identifier, resulting in reduced match rates, less relevant bids, and lost ad revenue. The removed guard expression 'bidderRequest.userId && bidderRequest.userId.pubProvidedId' was the sole mechanism for forwarding this data -- no replacement path exists elsewhere in the adapter.

summary: finishNavigation() uses stale CSS class selector '.bce-item-row' which does not exist in the new Blueprint-based ItemList; focus() silently fails, leaving keyboard focus unset after folder navigation completes
failure_scenario: User navigates to a subfolder. After items load (percentLoaded === 100), finishNavigation() calls focus(this.rootElement, '.bce-item-row'). summary: closeModals() uses stale CSS class selector '.bce-item-row-${focusedRow}' which does not exist in the new Blueprint-based ItemList; focus restoration after closing a modal silently fails

summary: Keyboard arrowdown handler introduces a 'document.activeElement &&' guard in grid view that prevents focusing the first item when no element is currently focused (activeElement is null), a regression from the old isFocusOnItem() behavior
failure_scenario: Page loads fresh, nothing is focused (document.activeElement is null). The old code's isFocusOnItem() returned false (via !undefined === true), triggering focus on the first item. summary: Keyboard arrowdown handler introduces a 'document.activeElement &&' guard in list view that prevents focusing the first item when no element is currently focused, same regression pattern as the grid-view case
failure_scenario: Same as above but for list view: pressing arrowdown with nothing focused does nothing, whereas the old code unconditionally focused the first row and set focusedRow to 0.

summary: getElementBySelector() calls itself recursively instead of calling getElementsBySelector(), causing a stack overflow when invoked
failure_scenario: Calling helpers.getElementBySelector('.be-ItemList-item') or helpers.getListItemByIndex(0) triggers infinite recursion: getElementBySelector calls this.getElementBySelector(selector) which is itself. Stack overflow crashes the test runner.

summary: Duplicate test blocks: two identical tests named 'renders component with correct columns for medium screen devices' at lines 41 and 50, likely an unintentional copy-paste
failure_scenario: The same assertions run twice, wasting test execution time. No behavioral impact, but the duplicate suggests the second block may have been intended to test a different scenario (e.g., 'shoulder render grid view mode' was also a copy-paste typo fixed in the same PR).

summary: ContentProps.focusedRow is declared as a required prop but is never destructured or used in the component body after the refactor; ContentExplorer still passes it but it is silently dropped

summary: EVENT_NOP1 passes describeUnknownEvent(statusByte) as description for a known NOP event

failure_scenario: Every loop end in a HudsonSnes sequence displays 'Loop End' with description 'Unknown Event: 0xNN'. A known control flow event is mislabeled as unknown, making debugging loop logic harder.

summary: Function-calling path always fails: LLM.call receives tools but no available_functions, causing empty text_response when the LLM responds with a tool call. json.loads('') fails, fallback text parsing returns ready=False with empty plan, leading to wasted API calls and an ineffective reasoning plan.
failure_scenario:
Agent with reasoning=True and an LLM that supports function calling. The handler calls llm.call(messages, tools=[function_schema]) without available_functions. The LLM responds with a tool call (content=''). LLM._handle_non_streaming_response sees available_functions is None and returns text_response=''. json.loads('') raises JSONDecodeError, fallback returns ('', False). The refinement loop runs max_attempts iterations making API calls that produce empty plans. The task description gets '

Reasoning Plan:
' with no actual plan content.

summary: Task description accumulates reasoning plans on each execution retry. When execute_task retries after an error (line 422 recursion), the reasoning block runs again and re-appends the plan via +=, causing unbounded growth of the task description.
failure_scenario: Agent with reasoning=True and max_retry_limit=2. First execute_task call appends reasoning plan to task.description and begins execution. Execution fails (non-litellm error). execute_task recurses at line 422, reasoning runs again on the already-mutated task, appending a second Reasoning Plan section. The task description now contains duplicate reasoning plans. If the second attempt also fails and retries, a third plan is appended. The LLM prompt balloons with redundant reasoning plans.

summary: Agent reasoning only considers task.tools, ignoring agent.tools. The actual execution uses both, so the reasoning plan is generated with incomplete tool information.
failure_scenario: An agent has agent.tools=[SearchTool, Calculator] but the task has task.tools=None. __format_available_tools returns 'No tools available'. The reasoning plan tells the LLM 'Available tools: No tools available'. During actual execution at agent.py line 354, tools = [] or [SearchTool, Calculator] or [] = [SearchTool, Calculator]. The LLM receives tools for execution that it was told don't exist in the reasoning plan, causing a mismatch between the planned and actual execution environment.

summary: reasoning=True is silently ignored when using kickoff() or kickoff_async(). The reasoning block only exists in execute_task, while kickoff methods delegate to LiteAgent which has no reasoning support.
failure_scenario: User creates Agent(role='Analyst', reasoning=True) and calls agent.kickoff('Analyze this data'). No reasoning occurs; no warning is produced. The user expects the agent to reflect and create a plan before execution, but the plan is never generated because kickoff bypasses execute_task entirely and uses LiteAgent which lacks a reasoning parameter.

summary: Dead code: ReasoningFunction pydantic model is defined but never instantiated, imported, or referenced anywhere in the codebase. The function-calling path constructs the schema as a raw dict instead of using this model.
failure_scenario: Maintenance cost: the unused class adds 4 lines of code that serve no purpose. A developer reading the file may waste time understanding why it exists. The raw dict at line 153 duplicates the schema fields (plan, ready) that ReasoningFunction already defines.

summary: parseRetryAfter rejects valid RFC 7231 delay-seconds with leading zeros (e.g. '05' returns null instead of 5) because the strict string check `trimmed === seconds.toString()` requires exact match with parseInt's decimal output
failure_scenario: Server returns `Retry-After: 05` (5 seconds, valid per RFC 7231 `delay-seconds = 1*DIGIT` grammar). `parseInt('05',10)` correctly yields 5, but `'05' === '5'` is false. The function falls through, `/^-?\d+$/.test('05')` is true so date-parsing is skipped, and null is returned. The retry-after header is ignored, falling back to exponential backoff instead of respecting the server's coordinated 5-second delay. The same defect affects any leading-zero delay like `'08'`, `'005'`.

summary: Template changed to instruct AI to generate vitest-style tests but the `run_test` tool at line 91 still executes with `node --test` (Node built-in runner), which may not discover tests registered via vitest's `test()` function
failure_scenario: The genai template tells the AI to `import { test, beforeEach, describe } from 'vitest'` (line 27) and the tool description says 'run test code with vitest' (line 73). But `run_test` executes `node --import tsx --test filename` (line 91). If the installed vitest version does not provide full `node --test` compatibility, vitest's `test()` function will register tests in vitest's internal queue rather than with Node's built-in test runner. `node --test` would find zero tests, exit with code 1 (or 0 depending on Node version), and the AI would either waste cycles fixing a non-code issue or accept silently-passed tests that never actually ran.

summary: FeatureTypeBadge component signature changed from {type} prop to full Feature object, but two callers in CheckAccess.tsx (lines 184, 199) were not updated and still pass type={val}. Non-Boolean features will display 'single use' badge instead of the correct type.
failure_scenario: Onboarding with metered features: selectedFeature.type is 'metered', passed as {type:'metered'} to FeatureTypeBadge. The new component reads feature.config?.usage_type which is undefined (no config prop passed). Falls through to 'single use' display. User sees wrong feature type label in the onboarding CheckAccess step.

summary: Debugging console.log(cusContext) left in production code, leaks the full customer context object (potentially including customer data, features, env info) to the browser console.
failure_scenario: Any page load in the customer detail view triggers `useCustomerContext()` then logs it. Customer data (IDs, feature assignments, product states) appears in browser devtools for any user who opens the console, violating data hygiene expectations.

summary: Debugging console.log('feature', feature) left in production code, will fire on every render of the FeatureTypeBadge component and spam the console with full feature objects.
failure_scenario: FeaturesTable renders a row per feature; FeatureTypeBadge is called once per row. Every render cycle logs all feature data to console, producing noisy output and potentially leaking feature config details.

summary: React 'Check' and 'Track' code snippet templates call useCustomer() hook at module level instead of inside a React component function, teaching users invalid hook usage patterns.
failure_scenario: User copies the displayed example code (const { allowed } = useCustomer() at module level) into their own React component. React throws 'Invalid hook call' / 'Hooks must be called inside a function component' error. The old snippet wrapped hooks inside an export default function component.

summary: FeatureTypeBadgeProps interface is defined but never used after the component signature was changed to accept (feature: Feature) directly. Dead code.
failure_scenario: Maintainers reading the code see the interface and may assume it is the contract, leading to confusion about the actual component interface. Unused interface adds noise.
