failure_scenario: A coding error in generate_markdown_description (e.g., wrong attribute access after a refactor) raises AttributeError; it is silently caught and replaced with getattr(model, 'description', None), masking the bug indefinitely while producing degraded (or None) descriptions for all models.

summary: New get_models iterates context.context.models (all models) instead of context.map (only file-backed models), causing models without file paths to appear in completions
failure_scenario: A purely programmatic or in-memory model with _path=None (excluded from context.map by LSPContext.__init__) now appears as an autocomplete candidate; selecting it inserts a model name that has no source file to navigate to and may not be user-facing.

summary: Broad except Exception: pass silently drops ALL context macros if any single value in _macros lacks .func (Executable has no .func, and the type is ExecutableOrMacro)
failure_scenario: If any entry in context.context._macros is an Executable (which lacks .func), getattr(m.func, '__doc__', None) raises AttributeError on m.func evaluation -- not on the getattr itself, so the default=None never comes into play. The except Exception: pass then discards every remaining context macro, not just the failing one. Type annotation explicitly allows ExecutableOrMacro values.

summary: multiply docstring renders with an unmatched opening double-quote because the closing " of "column > 0" is consumed by the """ delimiter
failure_scenario: The docstring literal is """untyped column will be a sqlglot column and return a sqlglot exp "column > 0""". Python's tokenizer treats the final three " as the closing """, so the docstring content becomes: 'untyped column will be a sqlglot column and return a sqlglot exp "column > 0' -- with a stray unmatched " that was meant to be the opening quote of "column > 0". Cosmetic documentation defect; no runtime crash.

summary: Image file path changed from file-relative (Path(__file__).parent.parent) to cwd-relative string 'tests/resources/images/test.png', breaking test when pytest is not invoked from repo root
failure_scenario: Run `cd tests/anthropic && pytest test_anthropic_autolog.py::test_messages_autolog_multi_modal` — open() looks for tests/anthropic/tests/resources/images/test.png (does not exist) instead of the repo-root-relative path. FileNotFoundError.

summary: Image file path changed from file-relative (Path(__file__).parent.parent) to cwd-relative string 'tests/resources/images/test.png', breaking test when pytest is not invoked from repo root
failure_scenario: Run `cd tests/bedrock && pytest test_bedrock_autolog.py -k 'test_converse_multi_modal'` — open() looks for tests/bedrock/tests/resources/images/test.png (does not exist). FileNotFoundError.

summary: reset_mlflow_autolog_and_traces fixture uses get_traces().clear() which only clears a local list, not the backend trace store — dead code masquerading as cleanup (former conftest called purge_traces() which actually deleted traces)
failure_scenario: While the root tracking_uri_mock fixture provides per-test database isolation today, get_traces().clear() is a no-op on the backend. If the isolation mechanism is ever changed or removed, traces will leak between tests, causing len(get_traces()) == 1 assertions to fail when stale traces from prior tests accumulate.

summary: Same get_traces().clear() dead code in reset_mlflow_autolog_and_traces fixture — does not purge traces from the backend
failure_scenario: Same latent trace-leakage risk as the fluent test file above. The deleted conftest.py correctly imported and called purge_traces().

summary: Same get_traces().clear() dead code in reset_mlflow_autolog_and_traces fixture — does not purge traces from the backend
failure_scenario: Same latent trace-leakage risk. All three pydantic_ai test files share this defective cleanup pattern.

summary: skip_when_testing_trace_sdk changed from pytest.mark.skipif (collection-time skip, fixtures do not run) to runtime pytest.skip() in a wrapper (fixtures execute before skip), causing autouse fixture side-effects to fire unnecessarily for skipped tests
failure_scenario: When IS_TRACING_SDK_ONLY is True, any test decorated with @skip_when_testing_trace_sdk will now run its autouse fixtures (e.g. tracking_uri_mock creating temp databases, reset_autolog_state mutating globals) before the skip fires — wasting CI time and risking fixture side-effects that the old skipif mark avoided by skipping at collection time.

summary: Binary EXIF tag values (ArrayBuffer, TypedArray, thumbnail) are stringified to "{}" by JSON.stringify, permanently corrupting the tag data on save
failure_scenario: User uploads a JPEG with MakerNote or thumbnail EXIF tags, edits any visible field, clicks Save — the binary tags become `{}` in the saved file, and the original binary data is permanently lost

summary: f.type.startsWith('image/') accepts PNG/GIF/WebP but piexif.load() and piexif.insert() only work with JPEG, silently corrupting non-JPEG images
failure_scenario: User uploads a PNG with EXIF metadata, edits a field, clicks Save Image — piexif.insert() embeds JPEG EXIF bytes into the PNG data URL, producing a corrupted file that can no longer be opened as a valid image

summary: zipStream.readable.pipeTo(fileStream) is not awaited, so stream errors (download denied, quota exceeded) become unhandled promise rejections with no user feedback
failure_scenario: User converts multiple HEIC files to a zip, browser denies the StreamSaver download (permission popup dismissed) — pipeTo rejects silently, zipStream.close() still succeeds, progress completes, but no usable zip file is ever saved to disk

summary: writer.write(outputBuffer) returns a Promise but is not awaited before writer.close(), so close may fire before the write completes, truncating data
failure_scenario: User converts a large HEIC photo, writer.write() begins transferring the converted JPEG blob, writer.close() fires synchronously before the write promise settles — the zip entry is truncated or empty, and the downloaded zip contains a corrupt or zero-byte file

summary: parseFloat(size) || 0 passes negative values through (e.g. -5 is truthy), producing a negative byte count that yields negative time strings like "-1h"
failure_scenario: User accidentally types "-5" into the file size input (e.g. clearing a number and the minus persists) — the calculator displays a nonsensical negative time estimate such as "-1h" instead of showing an error or clamping to zero

summary: Module-scoped let zipFileReader and let zipReader are overwritten on each unzip() call without ever calling zipReader.close(), leaking the previous zip reader and its file handle
failure_scenario: User opens zip A, then opens zip B — zip A's reader is overwritten without close() being called, the underlying BlobReader retains a reference to zip A's data in memory; repeated across many files, memory usage grows unboundedly until the tab crashes

summary: readFileTillEnd never calls reject on error; if file.slice().arrayBuffer() throws (deleted file, permission change), the promise hangs forever with no error propagation
failure_scenario: User starts zipping files via ZipFilesTool, one file is deleted or moved mid-read — readFileTillEnd's readSlice async function rejects unhandled, the outer Promise stays pending forever, the zip progress bar freezes, and the user sees an unresponsive tool with no error message

summary: richFile.entry.getData(fileStream) can throw (corrupt zip entry, invalid offset) but the rejection from handleAction is unhandled, leaving the user with no error feedback
failure_scenario: User clicks a file inside a partially-corrupt zip archive — getData throws because the compressed data is invalid, the promise from handleAction rejects without a .catch, the console shows an unhandled rejection, and the download never starts with no visible error to the user

summary: The built-in data model exploration tool receives a description prefix telling the agent to call it after itself, creating a circular/contradictory instruction.
failure_scenario: An EnrichMCP app is created with title 'My API'. The explore_my_api_data_model tool's final description becomes: 'This is a retriever for the My API server. Use it after calling explore_my_api_data_model. IMPORTANT: Call this tool FIRST...' The LLM agent sees conflicting ordering instructions -- the prefix says to use this tool only after calling explore_my_api_data_model, while the body says to call this tool first. The agent may delay calling the data-model tool (looking for a nonexistent prerequisite), loop, or ignore the FIRST instruction, degrading the quality of subsequent tool interactions.

summary: Bare `except Exception: pass` silently swallows all errors in `get_macros()`, including AttributeError when `context.context._macros` does not exist (version mismatch, corrupted state, unexpected Context subclass)
failure_scenario: If `_macros` is missing from the inner context (e.g., a Context subclass that shadows the attribute, or a refactoring that renames it), the function silently returns only built-in macros with no log entry, making the root cause undetectable without a debugger.

summary: `triggered_by_at` check depends on client behavior for subsequent completion requests; some LSP clients clear `triggerCharacter` on re-filter requests, causing `insert_text` to change from `macro_name` to `@macro_name` mid-typing, which produces `@@macro_name` on insertion
failure_scenario: User types `@` (triggers completion, triggered_by_at=True), then types `ea` to filter (VS Code sends a new request with triggerCharacter=undefined, triggered_by_at=False), then selects `@each` -- the insert_text sent is `@each` but the `@` is already on the line, producing `@@each`.

summary: `get_macros()` accepts but never uses the `file_uri` parameter, giving a misleading API alongside `get_models()` and `get_keywords()` which both use `file_uri` to scope results
failure_scenario: No crash, but a future caller passing a `file_uri` expecting file-scoped macro filtering (matching the behavior of get_models and get_keywords) silently gets all macros regardless of file, leading to incorrect completions.

summary: `@staticmethod` decorator combined with a parameter named `self` is misleading -- `self` has no special semantics for staticmethods and callers must explicitly pass the context; this design invites future bugs if a maintainer calls it as `instance.get_completions(uri, content)` expecting normal method binding
failure_scenario: A maintainer adds a call `lsp_context_instance.get_completions(uri, content)` -- the URI is bound to the `self` parameter and content to `uri`, producing the wrong `AllModelsResponse` with no type-error warning since all parameters accept Optional[LSPContext] and Optional[URI].

summary: Comment says 'Skip the macro completions test as regular checks because they are flaky' but neither `test.describe.skip` nor `test.skip()` is applied -- the flaky tests will run and may cause CI failures
failure_scenario: CI runs `pnpm run test:e2e`, the macro completion tests execute, and due to their documented flakiness fail intermittently, blocking unrelated PRs from merging.

summary: Test assertion changed from `>` to `>=` weakens the guarantee that context-specific keywords are being added; the test now passes even if `get_keywords` returns only the base tokenizer keywords without any model-dialect augmentation
failure_scenario: A future change breaks dialect-specific keyword loading so `get_keywords()` returns only `TOKENIZER_KEYWORDS`; the `>=` assertion passes (equal), hiding the regression that models would lose dialect-aware completions.

summary: __getattr__ does not cache lazy-imported classes in the module namespace, causing the full import to re-execute on every single attribute access
failure_scenario: Any code that accesses azure.ai.evaluation.AIAgentConverter or SKAgentConverter more than once (e.g., in a loop, or from multiple call sites in the same process) re-runs __import__, getattr, and _patch_all.append on every access. The _patch_all list grows without bound on repeated access. Even with dependencies installed, every attribute lookup is a fresh import — classes are never cached in the module globals.

summary: Changing from print+continue to raise ImportError in the except block silently alters import behavior — plain import of the red_team module now requires Pyrit installed
failure_scenario: Previously, import azure.ai.evaluation.red_team would succeed without Pyrit (printing an info message and loading the module without the red-team classes). Now the same import raises ImportError. Code that does import azure.ai.evaluation.red_team and then conditionally checks for available classes (hasattr pattern) will see an ImportError instead of a loaded module.

summary: Tests re-implement _create_lazy_import locally instead of importing the real module — the actual __init__.py lazy-import mechanism is never exercised
failure_scenario: The core bug (__getattr__ not caching) would never be caught by these tests because they test a local copy of the pattern, not the real module. A developer relying on these tests alone would ship the caching defect. The test_no_messages_during_module_import test only asserts that dict assignment does not print, which is vacuously true.

summary: _patch_all.append(class_name) inside lazy_import is dead code — __all__ is already fully computed at module load time before any __getattr__ call can fire
failure_scenario: At module load (line 143), __all__.extend runs against _patch_all which is still empty. When __getattr__ later triggers lazy_import and appends to _patch_all, nobody reads it. The append is harmless but misleading — it suggests the list is still live when it is not.

summary: ImportError re-raise in lazy_import discards the original exception chain by omitting 'from e', losing root-cause context for debugging
failure_scenario: If the underlying import fails for a non-obvious reason (e.g., a transitive dependency version conflict inside _ai_services.py), the original ImportError with its traceback is silently replaced by a generic message. The developer sees only 'Could not import AIAgentConverter. Please install azure-ai-projects' even though azure-ai-projects IS installed but has an internal conflict.

summary: Thread-unsafe concurrent access to shared member mDisasm: converting from per-call stack-local QZydis to a shared member introduces data races when GUI_GET_DISASSEMBLY is called from multiple threads (debugger thread via dbg commands + GUI thread via repaint), corrupting ZydisTokenizer intermediate state and the Zydis decoder.
failure_scenario: A dbg command handler (debugger thread) and a GUI repaint (GUI thread) both call GuiGetDisassembly concurrently. Both threads call mDisasm->DisassembleAt(), which calls mTokenizer.Tokenize() writing shared members mInst and mSuccess, then reads mTokenizer.Size() and mTokenizer.GetZydis(). One thread reads the other's token list, wrong instruction length, or corrupted decoder state. Additionally, configUpdatedSlot (main thread) can concurrently call UpdateArchitecture()->mZydis.Reset() while another thread is inside mZydis.DisassembleSafe(), corrupting the decoder and potentially crashing. The old per-call stack-local QZydis avoided all of this because each thread had its own isolated tokenizer and decoder.

summary: After 'delete mDisasm' in the destructor, the pointer is not set to nullptr; the !mDisasm guard in processMessage can be bypassed with a dangling pointer leading to use-after-free.
failure_scenario: During Bridge destruction, setDbgStopped() marks the bridge as stopped. A thread already past the mDbgStopped check in processMessage reaches the !mDisasm guard. mDisasm was deleted but not nulled, so the dangling pointer passes the null check. The thread then calls mDisasm->DisassembleAt() on freed memory, causing a use-after-free crash. The old code had no such risk because the QZydis was stack-allocated per call, never separately freed.

summary: setSelectedObjectId performs a redundant O(n) findIndex on the data array every time the selection changes, even though the row index is already known at every call site (handleCellClick receives row, keyboard handlers compute newRow, context menu has row). This introduces a performance regression not present before the prefetch changes.
failure_scenario: User holds the down-arrow key to rapidly navigate through the data browser. Every keypress triggers setSelectedObjectId, which scans the entire data array (potentially thousands of rows after infinite-scroll loading) with findIndex, discarding the newRow value that was already computed just one line above in the keyboard handler. The redundant scan accumulates latency on each keystroke.

summary: componentDidUpdate clears selectedObjectId via direct setState without going through setSelectedObjectId, leaving selectionHistory with stale entries. The new state field is not synchronised with the existing lifecycle reset.
failure_scenario: User selects several consecutive rows (history becomes [0,1,2]), then an action causes componentDidUpdate to reset selectedObjectId to undefined (line 210). selectionHistory remains [0,1,2]. The user then clicks a single row at index 5; setSelectedObjectId pushes 5, history becomes [0,1,2,5] then shifts to [1,2,5]. handlePrefetch sees last three entries [1,2,5] which are not consecutive, so no prefetch fires even though the two stale entries prevent correct history tracking for up to 3 additional selections. The stale history also wastes memory until overwritten.

summary: handleCellClick shift+range path sets selectedObjectId to undefined via direct setState (line 828), bypassing setSelectedObjectId. The selectionHistory is not updated to reflect the cleared selection.
failure_scenario: User shift-clicks to select a range of cells (size > 1), which clears selectedObjectId at line 828 without touching selectionHistory. The history retains entries from before the range selection, contaminating future prefetch decisions until 3 more non-range selections overwrite the stale entries.

summary: Mixing f-string interpolation with %-formatting on the same string causes a TypeError crash when any user-controlled field (description, expected_output, role, goal, tools repr) contains '%' followed by a valid conversion character (e.g., '95% success', '80% done', '50% reduction').
failure_scenario: Task description is 'Model achieves 95% success rate'. The f-string evaluates first, embedding the literal text '95% success' into the string that now ends with '%s%s'. The %-formatting pass then interprets '95% success' as containing the format specifier '% s' (space-flag + %s), consuming one of the two tuple arguments. The two trailing '%s' specifiers now have only one remaining argument, raising 'TypeError: not enough arguments for format string' and crashing the planning pipeline.

summary: Only the first knowledge source's content is included in the task summary; all subsequent knowledge sources are silently dropped.
failure_scenario: Agent has three knowledge sources: [company_policy, product_docs, competitor_analysis]. _get_agent_knowledge returns a list of all three content strings, but _create_tasks_summary accesses only knowledge_list[0] (company_policy). The LLM never sees product_docs or competitor_analysis, and the generated plan is missing critical context.

summary: _get_agent_knowledge assumes all knowledge source .content attributes are strings, but BaseFileKnowledgeSource subclasses (PDF, CSV, Excel, JSON, text file) store content as Dict[Path, str], and CrewDoclingSource stores it as List[DoclingDocument], producing garbled text in the LLM prompt.
failure_scenario: Agent uses a PDF knowledge source (extends BaseFileKnowledgeSource). source.content is {PosixPath('knowledge/report.pdf'): 'the actual extracted text...'}. The list comprehension returns this dict as a list element, and _create_tasks_summary embeds its Python repr into the prompt pseudo-JSON. The LLM receives '"agent_knowledge": "[\"{PosixPath('knowledge/report.pdf'): 'the actual extracted text...'}\"]"' — garbled output that fails to convey the knowledge.

summary: Knowledge content is embedded into a pseudo-JSON string without escaping double quotes, backslashes, or newlines, breaking the structured prompt format.
failure_scenario: Knowledge content contains 'The CEO said "ship it now"'. The f-string injects this raw into '"agent_knowledge": "[\\"The CEO said "ship it now"\\"]"'. The unescaped double quotes in the content break the pseudo-JSON structure, causing the LLM to misparse the knowledge field and potentially hallucinate or ignore the knowledge.

summary: The try/except AttributeError wraps the entire list comprehension; if any single knowledge source lacks a .content attribute, all knowledge sources are dropped and only a warning is logged.
failure_scenario: Agent has 5 knowledge sources. Source #3 is a custom BaseKnowledgeSource subclass that stores knowledge in a differently-named attribute (not .content). The list comprehension raises AttributeError on source #3, the except block logs a warning and returns [], and the valid knowledge from sources 1, 2, 4, and 5 is also silently dropped.

summary: Unused import 'json' adds no value and is dead code.
failure_scenario: The import clutters the namespace and misleads readers into thinking JSON serialization is used. Maintenance cost: every reader must verify it is unused.

summary: The condition 'str(knowledge_list) != "None"' is dead code — str([]) is "[]", never "None", and the preceding 'knowledge_list and' already guards against empty lists.
failure_scenario: The dead condition suggests the author was uncertain whether _get_agent_knowledge could return None (it always returns []). Maintenance cost: confusing code that future maintainers must decode.

summary: The pytest fixture 'mock_knowledge_source' is defined but never used by any test function.
failure_scenario: Dead test fixture adds confusion and maintenance burden. A reader expects it to be consumed by a parametrized test or setup logic, but it is orphaned.

summary: Imports 'MagicMock', 'Optional' (line 1), and 'BaseModel' (line 5) are never referenced in the test file.
failure_scenario: Unused imports add noise and can mask missing coverage (they suggest functionality that is not actually tested).

summary: Cross-organization data leakage: Supabase query filters only by created_by_user_id, omitting the organization_id column that every other design_sessions query in the codebase uses for scoping.
failure_scenario: A user belongs to Org A and Org B. They are viewing Org A's dashboard. The RecentsSection fetches sessions with only .eq('created_by_user_id', userId), returning sessions from both Org A and Org B. Session names from Org B (which may contain project-sensitive information) are exposed in the Org A nav. Additionally, GlobalNav has currentOrganization available (line 15, 108) but never passes it to RecentsSection — RecentsSection only receives isExpanded (line 119), so it has no way to scope by the active organization.

summary: useEffect starts an async fetch with no AbortController and no mounted guard; state setters fire on unmounted component after navigation away.
failure_scenario: User opens a page, the RecentsSection component mounts and starts fetching sessions. User navigates to another page (via router.push or a link) before the fetch completes. The component unmounts but the in-flight promise resolves and calls setSessions() and setLoading() on the unmounted component, producing a React warning ('Can't perform a React state update on an unmounted component') and leaking the promise closure. The comparable useEffect in GlobalNav.tsx (line 29) correctly cleans up its subscription in the return function.

summary: Supabase query errors are silently swallowed: on any error the function returns [] after logging, indistinguishable from the user having no sessions.
failure_scenario: The Supabase endpoint is temporarily unreachable or returns a permission error (e.g., RLS policy change). fetchRecentSessions catches the error, logs it, and returns []. The RecentsSection renders 'No recent sessions' — the user sees an empty state and assumes they have no history, when in reality the data could not be loaded. This hides production failures and makes debugging harder.

summary: Multiple unused default-value local variables left behind after refactoring — the old code used default instances for random-exclusion logic but the new code accesses none of them, leaving 13 dead declarations across the file.
failure_scenario: The variables at lines 7, 26, 38, 49, 68, 69, 141, 160, 174, 201, 252, 266, and 309 each construct a default description object (e.g. CellDescription, ParticleDescription, ConstructorDescription, etc.) but are never read afterward. This is unreachable dead code that compilers warn about; it misleads readers into thinking default values are still consulted, and it wastes constructor/destructor work for non-trivial types.

summary: Variable named 'randomNode' no longer holds a random value — the underlying factory method now produces deterministic hardcoded data.
failure_scenario: A future maintainer reading the test may assume the variable contains randomized test data and spend time debugging an intermittent failure that cannot exist. The name is misleading after the factory rename. Rename to e.g. 'nonDefaultNode'.

summary: Cache requests lack request tags and can NPE after fragment destroy
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Cache stories', then navigates away before the 20 Algolia API calls complete. The outer and inner Volley requests have no `setTag(requestTag)`, so `onDestroyView()`'s `queue.cancelAll(requestTag)` cannot cancel them. The success callback `res -> Utils.cacheStory(getContext(), id, res)` fires after fragment detach; `getContext()` returns null, causing NullPointerException in `SettingsUtils.saveStringToSharedPreferences(null, ...)` at `ctx.getSharedPreferences(...)`. The `Toast.makeText(getContext(), ...)` calls (lines 862, 867) also NPE on null Context.

summary: Unguarded Long.parseLong in hasCachedStories crashes RecyclerView binding on corrupted cache data
failure_scenario: If the cached-stories StringSet in SharedPreferences contains an entry like 'abc-def' (valid split length but non-numeric timestamp, e.g. from backup corruption), `Long.parseLong(split[1])` at line 215 throws NumberFormatException. This method is called from `StoryRecyclerViewAdapter.onBindViewHolder()` (line 295) during RecyclerView binding on the main thread. The uncaught RuntimeException crashes the app whenever the stories list header is bound, making the app unusable until cache data is cleared externally.

summary: Unguarded Integer.parseInt / Long.parseLong in loadCachedStories crashes on corrupted cache data
failure_scenario: Same root cause as hasCachedStories: if the cached-stories StringSet contains a corrupted entry where `split[0]` is non-numeric or `split[1]` is non-numeric, `Integer.parseInt(split[0])` at line 237 or `Long.parseLong(split[1])` at line 238 throws NumberFormatException. This propagates up through `showCachedStories()` → click listener callback, crashing the app when the user taps 'Show cached stories'. Unlike the JSON parsing block (line 257 catch), these parse calls are outside any try-catch.

summary: 'Stories cached' Toast fires before inner per-story requests complete, misleading users
failure_scenario: The 'Stories cached' success Toast at line 862 fires in the outer request's success callback, immediately after queueing up to 20 inner per-story fetch requests via `queue.add(r)`. None of the inner requests have completed yet. The user sees confirmation that caching is done, but if they navigate away or close the app, the inner requests either run to completion (if untagged — see finding 1) or are lost, resulting in only a partial cache. The Toast should fire only after all inner requests complete.

summary: showingCached boolean field is written at 4 locations but never read — dead code
failure_scenario: The `showingCached` field is set to true in `showCachedStories()` (line 873) and set to false in `attemptRefresh()` (line 589) and the type-click listener (line 263), but it is never checked anywhere — no guard in `onResume()`, scroll listener, `loadStory()`, or any other code path. This creates a maintenance burden (future readers assume it gates behavior) and wastes the work of maintaining it. If it is meant to prevent `onResume` from showing the update button or changing settings while cached stories are displayed, that protection is missing.

summary: Runtime crash: imports removed singleton 'tokenTracker' -- 'trackUsage' called on undefined
failure_scenario: Agent calls dedupQueries() at agent.ts:447 or :481. dedup.ts:3 imports { tokenTracker } from token-tracker.ts but that named export was deleted. At line 122, tokenTracker.trackUsage('dedup', tokens) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined, crashing the entire getResponse() workflow. All API requests fail with error events through the SSE endpoint.

summary: Runtime crash: imports removed singleton 'tokenTracker' -- 'trackUsage' called on undefined
failure_scenario: Agent calls analyzeSteps() at agent.ts:409. error-analyzer.ts:3 imports { tokenTracker } but the export was removed. At line 128, tokenTracker.trackUsage('error-analyzer', tokens) throws TypeError. All API request error-analysis paths crash.

summary: SSE progress events never sent: ActionTracker listener registered after all events already emitted
failure_scenario: server.ts line 83 awaits getResponse() which completes fully, emitting all 'action' events during its execution. Line 85 then registers context.actionTracker.on('action', emitProgress) -- but EventEmitter does not replay past events, and no more trackAction() calls will ever fire for this context. SSE clients on /api/v1/stream/:requestId receive only the final { type: 'answer' } event; all intermediate progress updates are silently dropped.

summary: rewriteQuery called without token tracker -- token usage silently discarded from budget tracking
failure_scenario: Agent loop at line 476: rewriteQuery(thisStep) is called without passing context.tokenTracker. The fallback (tracker || new TokenTracker()) in query-rewriter.ts:118 creates a throwaway tracker whose data is never added to the budget. Each query-rewrite call's Gemini API token usage is invisible to the budget check at line 271, so the agent may exceed tokenBudget without detection.

summary: CLI main() prints zero-token summary: creates fresh empty TokenTracker instead of using context's
failure_scenario: main() at line 659 correctly destructures getResponse() into { result, context } but then ignores context. Line 661 creates new TokenTracker() with zero usage entries and calls printSummary(). CLI output always shows { total: 0, breakdown: {} } regardless of actual tokens consumed.

summary: Multiple -1 dimensions silently produce wrong output: loop resolves only the last -1, leaving earlier -1 values unmodified in dim, corrupting stride computation and data layout
failure_scenario: ccv_cnnp_reshape(0, DIM_ALLOC(-1, -1, 4), ...) with 24-element input → auto_idx=1, known=4, dim becomes {-1, 6, 4, ...}. The surviving -1 at index 0 passes into ccv_nnc_tensor_get_stride(dim, ...) which computes stride[0]=24 from a product of -1*6*4 (as int, producing -24), corrupting the output tensor vias ccv_nnc_tensor_symbol_alias_new.

summary: Divisibility validation (tensor_count % known == 0) guarded by assert() is removed in release builds, allowing impossible reshapes to silently produce truncated dimensions
failure_scenario: Release build (NDEBUG defined): reshape a 10-element input via DIM_ALLOC(-1, 4). known=4, tensor_count=10, but assert() is compiled out. dim[auto_idx] = 10/4 = 2 (integer truncation). Result is a 2x4 output tensor whose element count (8) mismatches the input (10), silently producing wrong results.

summary: `receive()` uses `__class__.__name__` string lookup for adapter detection, breaking all subclasses of ChatAdapter, JSONAdapter, and XMLAdapter
failure_scenario: User creates `class CustomAdapter(JSONAdapter): pass` and uses it with streaming. `receive()` computes `adapter_name = "CustomAdapter"`, which is not in the `adapter_identifiers` dict (keyed by "ChatAdapter", "JSONAdapter", "XMLAdapter"), so it raises `ValueError("Unsupported adapter for streaming: CustomAdapter...")` even though the adapter inherits JSONAdapter's behavior and `flush()` (line 187) would handle it correctly via `isinstance()`. The old code used `isinstance()` for all adapter detection; the refactor to a dict-keyed-by-`__name__` lost subclass polymorphism.

summary: ChatAdapter `flush()` does not guard against `find()` returning -1, silently dropping the last character of the buffer
failure_scenario: If the ChatAdapter's `end_identifier` regex in `receive()` (line 161) matches but `find("[[")` in `flush()` returns -1 (edge case where the closing `]]` pattern is in the buffer but `[[` is somehow absent, or threading/settings change between the two calls), then `boundary_index = -1` and `last_tokens[:-1]` silently drops the last character of the accumulated output. The new XMLAdapter branch (lines 188-189) correctly handles `find()` returning -1 with a length fallback, making this inconsistency visible.

summary: Dead logging code: `file_extension == ["php"]` compares a string to a list, always False
failure_scenario: `file_extension` is a string like `"php"`, so `file_extension == ["php"]` is always `False`. The PHP extension-specific logging block at line 346-356 never executes, silently losing observability for PHP file processing. The same bug exists at line 358 for `== ["rb"]`. Compare with the correct patterns at line 322 (`== "py"`) and line 334 (`in ["js", "jsx"]`). Pre-existing in the touched function, not introduced by this diff.

summary: Dead logging code: `file_extension == ["rb"]` compares a string to a list, always False
failure_scenario: Same bug as line 346 but for the Ruby extension block. `file_extension == ["rb"]` is always `False` because `file_extension` is a string. The Ruby-specific logging never fires.

summary: Unhandled Organization.DoesNotExist from new get_from_cache call; previously no org dependency existed
failure_scenario: The new `Organization.objects.get_from_cache(id=repo.organization_id)` call can raise `Organization.DoesNotExist` if the org was deleted between task dispatch and execution. The old code never touched the org in `safe_for_comment`, so this exception path is a regression. The calling code at line 583 (`get_pr_files_safe_for_comment`) and the task at `tasks.py:277` do not catch this exception, so it propagates to the Celery worker as an unhandled failure.

summary: Unhandled Organization.DoesNotExist from new get_from_cache call; same regression as github integration
failure_scenario: Identical issue to github `safe_for_comment` — the new `Organization.objects.get_from_cache(id=repo.organization_id)` at line 348 introduces a previously nonexistent `Organization.DoesNotExist` exception path that propagates unhandled through `get_pr_files_safe_for_comment` (line 402) to the task caller.

summary: CSharpParser method_declaration_regex cannot match generic method declarations directly; depends on local_function_regex fallback via backtracking
failure_scenario: A C# method like `public void GetItems<T>(int id)` is not matched by `method_declaration_regex` because it expects `\(` immediately after the function name (line 288), but generic type parameters `<T>` appear between. The regex only works because `local_function_regex` (line 308) happens to match it as a fallback after the lazy `[^=]*?` backtracks past the modifiers. If the regex list order or patterns were changed, generic C# methods could silently stop being detected.

summary: Sort comparator violates Array.sort() contract: never returns 0 when both elements are PRODUCTION_LABEL or both are LATEST_PROMPT_LABEL
failure_scenario: If prompt.labels contains duplicate 'production' or 'latest' entries (e.g., from a server bug or migration), the sort comparator returns -1 instead of 0 for equal elements, breaking the compare(a,b) === -compare(b,a) symmetry that JavaScript's sort engine relies on. Combined with key={label} on React elements, this also produces duplicate-key React warnings and unstable DOM ordering.

summary: Badge rendering logic duplicated identically between visible labels (lines 52-71) and hover-card content (lines 87-108)
failure_scenario: Any future change to badge styling (e.g., adding a tooltip, changing colors, adjusting padding) must be made in two places. The two code blocks are identical — a missed update in one location produces visual inconsistency between the inline badges and the hover-card badges.

summary: COT two-call strategy discards token usage and cost from the first API call; only the final call's usage is captured
failure_scenario: A task using a non-reasoning-capable model with chain-of-thought prompting (run_strategy='cot_two_call') makes two LLM API calls. The first call's response (line 86, cot_response) contains usage data (e.g., 500 input tokens, 200 output tokens, $0.005 cost) but that data is never passed to usage_from_response(). Only the second call's response (line 111) has its usage extracted at line 175. The resulting TaskRun.usage under-reports total token counts and cost by approximately half.

summary: JavaScript falsy-zero bug: cost of exactly 0 is hidden from the display because 0 is falsy in the ternary check
failure_scenario: A TaskRun has usage.cost = 0.0 (free-tier API call or local Ollama run). The expression `run?.usage?.cost ? ...` evaluates to false for a zero value, producing undefined instead of '$0.000000'. The user sees no Cost field for a legitimate zero-cost run. The same pattern applies to total_tokens on line 66, where 0 tokens would also be hidden. The fix is to check for null/undefined explicitly: `run?.usage?.cost != null ? ...`

summary: Dot-access on private litellm attribute _hidden_params is fragile and will silently lose cost data if the internal field name changes
failure_scenario: litellm library changes the internal attribute name from _hidden_params to something else in a future version. The AttributeError on response._hidden_params propagates up through _run(), crashing invoke_returning_run_output() and causing all model invocations to fail. Even if the attribute exists but the 'response_cost' key is renamed, cost tracking silently breaks with only a warning log — no cost data is ever recorded for any run.

summary: THREADS.remove(thread_id) is never reached if super().run() raises an exception, causing a permanent TID leak in the THREADS set
failure_scenario: A mo.Thread is started whose target function raises an unhandled exception (e.g., ValueError). The thread's run() method calls THREADS.add(thread_id) at line 94, then super().run() at line 95 propagates the exception, skipping line 96 entirely. The TID stays in THREADS forever. Over repeated thread failures, THREADS accumulates stale entries. If the OS later reuses a leaked TID for an unrelated Python thread, print_override will incorrectly take the mo.Thread code path for that non-marimo thread, calling get_context() and potentially broadcasting CellOps with a stale or mismatched cell_id. Fix: wrap lines 95-96 in try/finally.

summary: print_override silently ignores the 'file' keyword argument; prints directed to explicit file handles are instead broadcast as cell console output
failure_scenario: User code inside a mo.Thread target function calls print('important data', file=open('output.csv', 'w')). The print_override function checks tid in THREADS (True), gets the execution context (success), then extracts only 'sep' and 'end' from kwargs. The 'file' argument is discarded, and the data is sent as a CellOp to the cell's console output instead of being written to output.csv. The file remains empty and the user's data is lost. Fix: at the start of the thread-aware path (after confirming tid in THREADS), add: if 'file' in kwargs: _original_print(*args, **kwargs); return.

summary: New `if (path)` block always returns early, making all custom-domain verification, CORS, and redirect logic unreachable.
failure_scenario: Any request to a custom domain (e.g. acme.cap.so) sets the `x-current-path` header and returns `NextResponse.next()` — the function never reaches the `mainDomains` check or the custom-domain CORS/verification/redirect paths. Custom domain users lose API CORS headers, domain-verification cookie caching, and incorrect-path redirects.

summary: CapCard URL generation drops the `domainVerified` guard; clicking a cap link for a space with an unverified custom domain navigates to the unverified domain.
failure_scenario: A workspace has `customDomain = 'acme.com'` but `domainVerified = false`. The old SharedCapCard checked both before using the custom domain; the new CapCard uses `activeSpace?.space.customDomain` alone. The generated URL points to `https://acme.com/s/...`, which the middleware will redirect back to cap.so — a broken link loop.

summary: "Or" divider text has identical foreground and background colors (`text-gray-1` on `bg-gray-1`), rendering it invisible in any theme.
failure_scenario: An unauthenticated user viewing a shared cap sees the AuthOverlay dialog. The "Or" separator between the Google sign-in button and the email form is invisible because the span has `bg-gray-1 text-gray-1` — both resolve to the same CSS variable, producing zero contrast.

summary: useEffect cleanup unconditionally resets `document.body.className = 'light'` on theme change, causing a visible flash before the new theme class is applied.
failure_scenario: User clicks the dark/light toggle. `setThemeHandler` sets body to 'dark' and updates state. React re-renders, runs the cleanup from the previous effect (body = 'light'), then runs the new effect body (body = 'dark'). The brief 'light' assignment between them produces a visible flash of the wrong theme.

summary: Heading text uses `text-gray-1` which in dark mode resolves to near-black, creating near-zero contrast against the dashboard's `bg-gray-1` container.
failure_scenario: A new user with an empty dashboard sees the 'Hey! Record your first Cap' heading. In dark mode `gray-1` ≈ hsl(0,0%,8.5%), the heading text is effectively invisible on the identically-colored `bg-gray-1` content area.

summary: `publishedAt` is read via `(post.metadata as any).publishedAt` with a fallback to `new Date().toISOString()`, silently showing the current time for any post whose metadata is missing the publish date.
failure_scenario: A blog post has malformed frontmatter missing `publishedAt`. The destructured `publishedTime` is `undefined` but unused in the JSX; the inline `(post.metadata as any).publishedAt` also resolves to `undefined`, so the `||` fallback kicks in and every page view displays 'right now' as if the post was just published — misleading to readers.

summary: Server action `setTheme` is defined but never imported or called anywhere; the client-side `js-cookie` path in DynamicSharedLayout is the sole writer of the theme cookie, leaving this file as dead code.
failure_scenario: No runtime failure, but the file adds confusion: two cookie-setting paths exist (server action vs. client js-cookie) and a future developer might wire this in, creating a race between server-side and client-side cookie writes.

summary: Login page reads theme from `localStorage` while the rest of the app reads it from a cookie, creating two conflicting sources of truth for the theme toggle.
failure_scenario: User sets dark mode in the dashboard (writes cookie via js-cookie). User signs out and lands on `/login`. The cookie has theme='dark' and layout.tsx sets body class to 'dark'. But localStorage lacks a 'theme' key, so the login form defaults to 'light' and does NOT add `.dark` to `document.documentElement` — but body already has `.dark`. Radix dark selectors still match via body, so it mostly works, but the inconsistency means the HTML element never gets the `.dark` class that other CSS selectors might rely on.

summary: get_key_from_rule_data raises IndexError (or TypeError) if rule.data['actions'] is an empty list [] or None, because dict.get() only returns the default [{}] when the key is absent, not when it is present but falsy or empty
failure_scenario: A Rule is created with data={'actions': []} (empty actions list, e.g. via direct ORM create or a migration edge case). When the opsgenie client calls get_key_from_rule_data(rule, 'workflow_id'), rule.data.get('actions', [{}]) returns the actual [] (not the default), then [][0] raises IndexError, crashing the Opsgenie notification pipeline. Similarly, if data['actions'] is None, None[0] raises TypeError. The callers at client.py:48 and client.py:61 do not catch either exception; they only assert the result is not None, which never executes once the crash occurs.

summary: get_key_from_rule_data return type annotation is 'str' but dict.get() can return None (when key is missing from the first action dict) or any stored type (e.g. int from pre-migration rules)
failure_scenario: A type checker like mypy would flag the mismatch. At runtime, callers in client.py assert the result is not None (catching the None case), but future callers that trust the 'str' annotation without a None guard would propagate None downstream, potentially causing AttributeError on string methods like .upper() or .isnumeric(). Also, if a legacy rule stores workflow_id as an integer, the function returns int not str, and callers expecting string-specific operations would break.

summary: build_description_workflow_engine_ui still accepts workflow_id: int, but create_link_to_workflow (called from it at line 77) was changed by this PR to expect str
failure_scenario: A static type checker will flag that an int is passed to a str parameter. At runtime the f-string in create_link_to_workflow coerces int to str, so no immediate crash. However, if create_link_to_workflow is later extended with string-specific operations (e.g. .isnumeric(), .upper()), passing an int would raise AttributeError. The build_description_workflow_engine_ui signature should be updated to workflow_id: str to match the new contract, or the value from data.get('workflow_id') (which may now be a string per the workflow-engine migration) should be explicitly coerced.

summary: Removal of _unpack() from create_api_specific_request_online breaks multimodal batch processing -- OpenAIBatchRequestProcessor now sends raw _MultiModalPrompt Pydantic objects in messages instead of unpacked chat-format content blocks.
failure_scenario: User runs a batch job with multimodal prompts (e.g., returning text and Image(content=...) from prompt()). The batch processor calls create_api_specific_request_online, which now uses generic_request.messages directly without unpacking. The _MultiModalPrompt instance in message content is not JSON-serializable, causing TypeError at json.dumps() when building the batch file. Even if serialization were handled, the OpenAI API would receive a model dict with texts/images/files keys instead of expected chat content blocks, resulting in an API error.

summary: Missing try/except for pydantic.ValidationError in _unpack_multimodal -- when is_multimodal_prompt is None (user returns list of pre-formatted messages), the method tries model_validate on potentially plain-string content without the safety net from the old OpenAIRequestMixin._unpack().
failure_scenario: User prompt() returns a list of message dicts with plain-text content, e.g. [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]. prompt_formatter.py sets is_multimodal_prompt=None. In _unpack_multimodal, is_multimodal_prompt is False check is skipped, and _MultiModalPrompt.model_validate("hello") raises pydantic.ValidationError which propagates unhandled through process_requests_from_file, crashing the entire request processing pipeline.

summary: File.__post_init__ is dead code -- Pydantic v2 BaseModel does not call __post_init__ (a dataclasses hook); the Pydantic equivalent is model_post_init. MIME type auto-detection from URL never runs, so File.mime_type stays None when not explicitly provided.
failure_scenario: User creates curator.types.File(url='https://example.com/doc.pdf') without mime_type. The __post_init__ calling mimetypes.guess_type() is never invoked. file.mime_type remains None. Downstream consumers expecting a MIME type get None, potentially causing issues in future code paths.

summary: ValueError message broken by comma between two f-strings -- raise ValueError(f"...", f"...") passes two separate string args instead of one concatenated message, producing a confusing tuple-like error representation.
failure_scenario: A multimodal image upload exceeds 20MB via LiteLLM OpenAI provider. file_upload_limit_check raises ValueError with two args, producing an error that displays as a tuple instead of a single readable sentence.

summary: _multimodal_prompt_supported narrowed from always True to checking only model name prefixes in a hardcoded set of three models -- compatible OpenAI-provider models with vision not in the set are incorrectly rejected.
failure_scenario: User configures an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a vision-capable deployment name that does not start with gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, or gpt-4o-vision (e.g., a custom deployment or a future gpt-5o model). _multimodal_prompt_supported returns False, and _unpack_multimodal raises TypeError preventing any multimodal requests.

summary: Nil pointer dereference: accesses currentUser.Uid and currentUser.Gid before checking error from user.Current()
failure_scenario: When user.Current() fails (e.g., user entry missing from /etc/passwd during container/NFS upload), currentUser is nil. The code dereferences currentUser.Uid on line 305 (before the error check on line 309), causing a panic.

summary: Nil pointer dereference in listing callback: direct dereference of *fileProperties.NFSFileType, *fileProperties.LinkCount, and *fileProperties.ID without nil checks
failure_scenario: When getShareProtocolType API fails (e.g., network error), it returns the fallback value matching the user's --nfs flag with no error. If the share is actually SMB, the listing response has nil NFS-specific fields. The direct dereference on lines 209-211 panics. The morpher code path (line 268) safely uses adapter methods with IffNotNil, so this inconsistency between the two code paths creates a crash surface.

summary: Silent error swallowing: when worker returns nil output with non-nil error, the error is dropped by the 'if out != nil' guard
failure_scenario: Any transform worker (parallel.PoolFunc) that returns (nil, someError) will have its error silently discarded instead of propagated to the output channel. The NFS skip path returns (nil, nil) which is safe, but future code or third-party transformers could silently lose errors.

summary: Original file access time (atime) is overwritten with modification time during NFS download
failure_scenario: PutNFSProperties sets both atime (syscall.Timeval[0]) and mtime (syscall.Timeval[1]) to the same lastWriteTime value, discarding the source file's actual access time which is available via FileAccessTime(). When downloading from NFS shares, the atime is silently replaced with the mtime.

summary: Race condition: getUmask() temporarily changes process-wide umask to 0 during capture via sync.Once
failure_scenario: On first invocation, syscall.Umask(0) sets the process-wide umask to 0 before restoring it. If another goroutine creates a file during this brief window, it will be created with permissions 0666/0777 instead of the intended masked permissions. The sync.Once caches the result so subsequent calls are safe, but the initial capture window affects all threads.

summary: performNFSSpecificValidation silently ignores --preserve-posix-properties flag with no error or warning
failure_scenario: When user runs 'azcopy copy --nfs --preserve-posix-properties=true', the POSIX properties flag is silently dropped because performNFSSpecificValidation's return type omits preservePOSIXPropertiesVal (it returns only 4 values vs. performSMBSpecificValidation's 5). The NFS path assigns cooked.preservePOSIXProperties only via the retain-zero-value path. Users get no indication their flag was ignored.

summary: getShareProtocolType silently returns fallback protocol on API error, masking protocol mismatches
failure_scenario: When shareClient.GetProperties() fails (network error, permissions, transient outage), the function logs an info message and returns the fallback protocol value (matching the user's --nfs flag) with nil error. This means protocol validation passes regardless of the actual share protocol, and subsequent code will proceed with potentially wrong protocol assumptions.

summary: JS falsy-zero: replaceMacros(val || '') converts AUCTION_PRICE=0 to empty string, corrupting macro-replaced URLs
failure_scenario: Server returns a bid response with price=0 (a zero-dollar fill). In replaceAllMacrosInPlace, the macros object has AUCTION_PRICE: 0. When replaceMacros substitutes ${AUCTION_PRICE} in nurl/lurl/adm, the expression 'val || ""' evaluates 0 as falsy, replacing the macro with empty string instead of "0". The resulting win notification URL becomes e.g. "https://adserver.example.com/win?price=" (trailing equals, no value) instead of "https://adserver.example.com/win?price=0", silently dropping the price parameter. This also applies to any other macro whose value evaluates to zero.

summary: Missing `options.container` in the useEffect dependency array; the effect reads it but won't re-run when it alone changes.
failure_scenario: User renders `<NovuUI options={{ container: newShadowRoot, localization: stableRef, tabs: stableRef, options: stableNovuOptions, routerPush: stableRef }} />`. React re-renders because `options.container` changed, but the effect's deps are `[novuUI, adaptedAppearanceForUpdate, options.localization, options.tabs, options.options, options.routerPush]` — none of which changed. The effect does not re-run, `updateContainer` is never called, and portaled content (popovers, tooltips) continues targeting the old container.

summary: `updateContainer()` only updates the reactive signal but never moves `#rootElement`; the root div stays in the original container.
failure_scenario: A JS SDK user calls `novuUI.updateContainer(differentShadowRoot)`. The `container()` signal updates, so PopoverContent and TooltipContent portals now mount into `differentShadowRoot` and register event listeners there. But `#rootElement` — the div that holds all non-portaled content (Inbox, Bell, etc.) — was appended to the original ShadowRoot during construction and is never relocated. The Inbox renders in the old shadow tree while its Popover renders in `differentShadowRoot`, breaking style inheritance and event handling.

summary: When the container is `document.body`, `handleClickOutside` is registered twice on the same element, invoking `onClose()` twice per click.
failure_scenario: A JS SDK user passes `container: document.body`. On mount, the code calls `document.body.addEventListener('click', handleClickOutside)` at line 76 and `container()?.addEventListener('click', handleClickOutside)` at line 77 — both targeting `document.body`. Every outside click fires `handleClickOutside` twice. While `onClose()` is likely idempotent, the double invocation wastes cycles and would cause observably incorrect behavior if any side effect in `onClose` (or downstream state updates) is not idempotent.

summary: claudeResponse.Usage dereferenced without nil check in HandleClaudeResponseData; the old completion path was safe (used info.PromptTokens + CountTextToken) but this safe path is removed, making the nil-dereference risk unconditional
failure_scenario: An API response (e.g., from AWS Bedrock with a malformed or edge-case response) that passes the error check but has no usage field will cause a nil pointer panic on claudeResponse.Usage.InputTokens.

summary: claudeResponse.Delta.Text accessed in FormatClaudeResponseInfo without checking that claudeResponse.Delta itself is non-nil for content_block_delta events
failure_scenario: A stream event of type content_block_delta with a nil Delta pointer (malformed or unexpected API response) causes a nil pointer dereference panic when accessing claudeResponse.Delta.Text.

summary: claudeResponse.Delta.StopReason dereferenced in StreamResponseClaude2OpenAI without nil-checking claudeResponse.Delta or StopReason for message_delta events
failure_scenario: A message_delta stream event with a nil Delta or a nil StopReason pointer crashes with a nil pointer dereference at stopReasonClaude2OpenAI(*claudeResponse.Delta.StopReason).

summary: ResponseText2Usage error is silently discarded (claudeInfo.Usage, _ = ...) and the result is dereferenced (*claudeInfo.Usage) on the next line when ShouldIncludeUsage is true, risking nil pointer panic if token counting fails
failure_scenario: If service.ResponseText2Usage returns an error (e.g., unknown model name), claudeInfo.Usage becomes nil; then helper.GenerateFinalUsageResponse dereferences *claudeInfo.Usage and panics.

summary: Dead code: RequestOpenAI2ClaudeComplete function is defined but has zero callers after the diff removed the only call site in ConvertOpenAIRequest
failure_scenario: The function (approximately 25 lines) is still compiled and shipped, adding unused binary size and maintenance burden. Any future refactor might waste time updating it.

summary: Unused parameter: StreamResponseClaude2OpenAI accepts reqMode int but no longer branches on it; callers in claude/adaptor.go, vertex/adaptor.go, and aws/relay-aws.go still pass values that are ignored
failure_scenario: Future maintainers may spend time tracing what requestMode values are valid and whether the parameter still has meaning, when it no longer affects any code path.

summary: Unused parameter: ResponseClaude2OpenAI accepts reqMode int but never uses it in its body; called from HandleClaudeResponseData with the ignored value
failure_scenario: Same as above -- dead parameter adds confusion for future readers and could mislead someone adding a new branch that checks the mode expecting it to be meaningful.

summary: OpenCL mask kernel applies one scalar mask check to kercn vectorized elements, leaking threshold across pixels when kercn > 1
failure_scenario: Single-channel 8-bit image (640x480): predictOptimalVectorWidth returns kercn=4. Each work-item reads one mask byte at line 36 and applies it to all 4 elements read as uchar4 at line 35. If mask covers pixel 0 but not pixels 1-3, pixels 1-3 are incorrectly thresholded (or vice versa). The per-work-item mask_index uses gx/CN (integer division), but when T aggregates multiple elements, gx indexes work-items not individual elements. This applies equally to multi-channel images whenever kercn > 1.

summary: Division by zero in getThreshVal_Otsu when maskCount is 0 (all-zero mask), producing NaN threshold that silently propagates
failure_scenario: Call thresholdWithMask(src, dst, allZeroMask, 0, 255, THRESH_BINARY | THRESH_OTSU). maskCount stays at 0 because every mask pixel is zero. scale = 1.0/0 = inf. mu = 0*inf = NaN. h[i]*scale = 0*inf = NaN for every bin. sigma becomes NaN, max_sigma comparison always false, max_val stays at 0 (uninitialized garbage value), returned as the computed threshold. The subsequent threshold operation uses this garbage value.

summary: getThreshVal_Triangle_8u template<true> has default empty mask argument, enabling a null-pointer dereference at call sites
failure_scenario: Future code calls getThreshVal_Triangle_8u<true>(src) omitting the mask argument. The default empty _mask causes useMask=true but pMask comes from _mask.ptr<unsigned char>(i) which returns a null or invalid pointer on an empty Mat. Then pMask[j] at line 1377 dereferences null, causing a segmentation fault.

summary: ~100 lines of depth-type edge-case logic duplicated identically between cv::threshold (line 1647) and cv::thresholdWithMask (line 1793)
failure_scenario: A future bug fix corrects an edge-case in cv::threshold's CV_8U path (e.g., the saturate_cast or setTo logic at line 1665-1668) but the identical code in thresholdWithMask (line 1811-1814) is not updated. The two functions diverge, and thresholdWithMask produces different results than threshold for identical inputs when a trivial all-ones mask is used, breaking the documented equivalence.

summary: CALL_HAL hardware acceleration and type-specific SIMD paths (thresh_8u/thresh_16s/thresh_32f/thresh_64f) are entirely skipped when a mask is present, forcing generic scalar loops
failure_scenario: User calls thresholdWithMask on a CV_8U image on a machine with Intel IPP. The non-masked path would use IPP or SIMD intrinsics achieving ~10x throughput. The masked path calls threshGenericWithMask (a simple for-loop at line 141-144). On a 4K image this adds hundreds of milliseconds of latency compared to what the non-masked path delivers, surprising users who expect similar performance.

summary: runSync() deadlocks if called after quit(): runAsync silently returns when running_ is false, but runSync still blocks on promise.get_future().wait() forever
failure_scenario: ReactInstanceWin::Destroy() calls jsMessageThread->quitSynchronous() which sets running_=false. If any code subsequently calls MessageQueueThreadImpl::runOnQueueSync() — the TOCTOU between isRunning() check and runSync() allows entering the deadlock path — runAsync returns immediately without posting the task (running_ is false), the promise is never set, and the calling thread hangs permanently.

summary: runOnQueue() and runOnQueueSync() silently drop work when the thread is not running, losing pending tasks after quitSynchronous()
failure_scenario: A caller queues a cleanup task via runOnQueue() after quitSynchronous() has stopped the thread, or a task is in-flight between isRunning() check and actual quit. The task is silently dropped — its captured resources (shared_ptrs, callbacks) are destroyed without execution, potentially leaking state that relied on the task completing. The old dispatch-queue design processed pending tasks via Shutdown(PendingTaskAction::Complete) before tearing down.

summary: Unused context capture in lambda after JSDispatcher removal — context variable captured but never referenced in getValue callback
failure_scenario: The lambda at getValue:59 captures `context = pThis->m_context` but the body only calls `callback(value)`, never using context. This retains the ReactContext reference in every callback lambda, wasting memory (sizeof ReactContext per callback) and keeping the context alive longer than necessary. Same pattern repeats at startAnimatingNode:131.

summary: JsiAbiRuntime constructor acquires recursive_mutex lock, then calls GetFromJsiRuntime which acquires the same lock recursively — a design smell that forced the mutex to be recursive
failure_scenario: The constructor (line 228) takes s_jsiRuntimeMapMutex via lock_guard, then calls GetFromJsiRuntime (line 252) which also takes the same mutex via lock_guard. This works only because the mutex is recursive (line 226). If the mutex were ever changed to a regular std::mutex, this would deadlock instantly. The recursive lock also masks the fact that GetFromJsiRuntime is called while the constructor already holds invariants it may not expect. Refactoring to an internal unlocked lookup helper would eliminate the need for recursion.

summary: cleanup() returns immediately before executing any cleanup logic, leaving injected data-onlook-id attributes in user source files, orphaned child processes (dev servers), lingering PTY terminal processes, and an unterminated Supabase auth auto-refresh loop on every app exit and auto-update
failure_scenario: User opens a project (which injects data-onlook-id tracking attributes into source files and starts a dev server via PTY), then clicks 'Update and Restart'. updater.quitAndInstall() calls cleanup() which returns at line 98 without calling run.stopAll() (to remove injected IDs and close file watchers), terminal.killAll() (to kill the dev server PTY process), or cleanupAuthAutoRefresh() (to stop token refresh). The injected attributes persist permanently in the user's source files, the dev server remains alive occupying its port, and the Supabase auto-refresh continues making API calls. When the new app version starts, it fails to bind the dev server port (already in use by the orphaned process from the previous instance).

summary: InferenceProviderMapping.__init__ pops 'providerId' (camelCase) but the dataclass field is 'provider_id' (snake_case); constructing with snake_case kwarg raises KeyError
failure_scenario: Calling InferenceProviderMapping(hf_model_id='x', status='live', task='t', provider_id='id') -- i.e. using the Python field name -- crashes at kwargs.pop('providerId') with KeyError because the __init__ only looks for camelCase 'providerId'. All internal callers currently pass 'providerId', so this is latent, but it makes the interface fragile for any future user who naturally uses the snake_case field name.

summary: InferenceProviderMapping.__init__ pops 'adapterWeightsPath' (camelCase) not 'adapter_weights_path' (snake_case) -- snake_case keyword is silently dropped and defaults to None
failure_scenario: If someone constructs InferenceProviderMapping(adapter_weights_path='lora/my_weights.safetensors', ...) using the snake_case field name, the __init__ skips this kwarg (since it only pops 'adapterWeightsPath'), so self.adapter_weights_path defaults to None. The LoRA weights path is silently lost, and the Fal AI inference client will skip adding loras to the payload. The remaining kwargs wind up set on the instance via self.__dict__.update, creating a confusing duplicate attribute.

summary: _prepare_mapping_info calls provider_mapping.task on a value that _could_ be a raw dict instead of InferenceProviderMapping if ModelInfo conversion was skipped on a falsy-but-typed response
failure_scenario: Although the current code path prevents this, if the Hub API ever returns inferenceProviderMapping as a non-None, non-dict truthy value (e.g., a single mapping object due to API evolution), ModelInfo.__init__ would skip the conversion and _fetch_inference_provider_mapping would return the raw value. Then _prepare_mapping_info would attempt provider_mapping.task on a non-InferenceProviderMapping, raising AttributeError with a misleading traceback instead of the intended ValueError('Model ... is not supported').

summary: ModelInfo.__init__ uses truthiness check 'if self.inference_provider_mapping:' to gate InferenceProviderMapping conversion -- empty dict {} is falsy so would skip conversion if API returns empty mappings
failure_scenario: If the Hub API returns inferenceProviderMapping as an empty dict {} (plausible for models with no registered providers), the conversion loop is skipped. _fetch_inference_provider_mapping returns the raw empty dict, callers get None from .get(provider), and the correct 'not supported' ValueError is raised. This actually works correctly for empty dicts, but the truthiness test is fragile: if the API evolves to return a non-dict truthy value, the .items() call in the conversion loop crashes, or worse, the conversion is skipped and downstream code fails with an opaque AttributeError.

summary: FalAITextToImageTask._prepare_payload_as_dict hardcodes revision='main' when constructing the LoRA weights URL, which fails if the weights live on a different branch/revision
failure_scenario: If a registered model's adapter_weights_path points to a LoRA file that was committed to a branch other than 'main' (e.g., 'lora-v2' or a pinned commit SHA), the URL constructed from constants.HUGGINGFACE_CO_URL_TEMPLATE with revision='main' will 404, and the Fal AI inference request will fail. The revision should either be configurable per-mapping or derived from the API response.

summary: FalAITextToImageTask unconditionally sets payload['loras'] and payload['model_name'], overwriting any same-named keys the user passed in parameters
failure_scenario: A user calls inference with parameters={'loras': [...custom...], 'model_name': 'my-model'} and the provider has adapter_weights_path set. The **filter_none(parameters) spread includes the user's loras and model_name into the payload dict early, but they are later overwritten by payload['loras'] = [...] and payload['model_name'] = 'stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0'. The user's custom loras/model are silently discarded, and no error is raised.

summary: Test mocks for _fetch_inference_provider_mapping use inconsistent attribute names: 'providerId' (camelCase) at line 84 vs 'provider_id' (snake_case) at lines 98, 114, 131
failure_scenario: The task mismatch test mock uses providerId='mapped-id' while staging/live/lora tests use provider_id='mapped-id'. Since mocker.Mock auto-creates any attribute, tests pass regardless. But this means the task mismatch test does not verify that _prepare_mapping_info correctly handles the real InferenceProviderMapping attribute mapping. A future change to InferenceProviderMapping.__init__ that breaks the providerId->provider_id mapping would pass all tests but fail at runtime.

summary: Provider template doc (new_provider.md) still shows old _prepare_payload_as_dict signatures with 'mapped_model: str' instead of 'provider_mapping_info: InferenceProviderMapping'
failure_scenario: A developer following the template to add a new provider writes code with `def _prepare_payload_as_dict(self, inputs, parameters, mapped_model: str)` matching the template. At runtime, the call from TaskProviderHelper.prepare_request passes `provider_mapping_info=provider_mapping_info` as a keyword arg, which becomes an unexpected keyword argument for the old signature, raising TypeError.

summary: First/prev/next/last navigation links no longer have setVersioned(false); Wicket will serialize link state into every page version, bloating HTTP sessions and risking stale-link state on version restore
failure_scenario: A user navigates across 5 pages of a data table. With Wicket's default page versioning enabled, each navigation creates a new page version that serializes the state of every versioned component. The old SakaiPagingNavigator explicitly called link.setVersioned(false) on each of the 4 navigation links to prevent this; the replacement standard AjaxPagingNavigator does not. After browsing, the user's HTTP session holds serialized copies of 4 links x 5 versions = 20 extra serialized objects. When Wicket restores an old page version (back-button), the versioned links may point to a different page than the non-versioned navigator, causing a mismatch where the 'next' link thinks the user is on page 2 but the navigator shows page 5.

summary: Numbered page navigation (PagingNavigation 1|2|3|...) now rendered visibly; the deleted SakaiPagingNavigator.newNavigation() override that hid it (isVisible() returning false) was not re-established
failure_scenario: A data table with 40 data pages renders 40 numbered page links (1 | 2 | 3 | ... | 40) inline alongside the first/prev/next/last buttons and the row-size-selector dropdown, producing a wide, cluttered toolbar row that was previously compact. The deleted SakaiPagingNavigator overrode newNavigation() to return a PagingNavigation whose isVisible() returns false, suppressing these number links. The replacement AjaxPagingNavigator uses the standard Wicket PagingNavigation which renders them visibly. In tables with many pages this causes toolbar overflow or wrapping.

summary: Missing @classmethod decorator on a model_validator(mode='before') — will raise PydanticUserError on Pydantic v2.5+, crashing Agent construction for any from_repository usage
failure_scenario: User runs with Pydantic >= 2.5 (compatible with the project's pydantic>=2.4.2 constraint). Any Agent(from_repository='x') call raises PydanticUserError: 'A model validator with mode="before" should be a classmethod' at model class creation time. Every other mode='before' validator in this codebase (base_agent.py:165, security_config.py:73, task.py:225) correctly uses @classmethod.

summary: Network exceptions (ConnectionError, Timeout, SSLError) and auth failures from get_auth_token() are not caught or wrapped in AgentRepositoryError — raw exceptions propagate through Pydantic's model validation giving confusing error messages
failure_scenario: User is offline or the CrewAI+ API is unreachable. Calling Agent(from_repository='my_agent') raises a raw requests.ConnectionError wrapped inside a pydantic_core.ValidationError with a message like '1 validation error for Agent ... ConnectionError'. The user gets no indication this is a repository loading failure. Similarly, if the user is not logged in, get_auth_token() raises Exception('No token found...') which leaks through as a ValidationError instead of a clear AgentRepositoryError.

summary: response.json() is called without a try/except after checking only status_code — a 200 response with a non-JSON body (e.g. gateway HTML error page) raises uncaught JSONDecodeError
failure_scenario: A proxy or load balancer returns HTTP 200 with an HTML error page (common with misconfigured gateways). The status_code check passes, but response.json() raises requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError, which propagates through Pydantic as an unhelpful ValidationError instead of an AgentRepositoryError.

summary: importlib.import_module('crewai_tools') is called inside the for-loop over tools — the module is re-imported for every single tool unnecessarily
failure_scenario: An agent from the repository has 10 tools. importlib.import_module('crewai_tools') executes 10 times inside the loop instead of once before the loop begins. While importlib caches the module so the I/O cost is only paid once, the repeated function call and cache lookup waste CPU on a hot path (construction of every Agent from a repository). The import should be hoisted before the for loop.

summary: The if from_repository: guard inside _load_agent_from_repository is dead code — the sole caller validate_from_repository already verifies from_repository is truthy before invoking this method
failure_scenario: Not a runtime crash, but a code-quality defect: the guard implies the method handles empty-string input, but returning {} silently for an empty from_repository would create an Agent with no role/goal/backstory set (violating BaseAgent's required-field validation) and from_repository='' still stored on the instance. If this code path were ever reached (e.g. future refactor of the caller), it would create a broken agent with no attributes loaded from the repository.

summary: NullPointerException crash on first app launch: readStringFromSharedPreferences returns null for a never-written key, then .isEmpty() is called on null
failure_scenario: Fresh install: SharedPreferences has no entry for KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_HISTORIES. sharedPref.getString(key, null) returns null. Java expression null.isEmpty() throws NullPointerException, crashing MainActivity.onCreate() before any UI appears.

summary: Existing user data loss on upgrade — old clicked-story IDs (KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_CLICKED_IDS) are never migrated to the new histories format
failure_scenario: A user upgrades from a previous version. Their Set of previously-clicked story IDs stored under the old shared-preferences key KEY_SHARED_PREFERENCES_CLICKED_IDS is completely ignored. No migration reads that key; the new history system starts empty. All stories appear unread and the old reading history is permanently lost.

summary: Clearing history in Settings only clears SharedPreferences but leaves the HistoriesUtils in-memory list untouched, so isHistoryExist() continues returning stale true values
failure_scenario: User opens Settings, taps 'Clear clicked stories'. SharedPreferences is saved as empty string, snackbar reports correct old count. User returns to the story list — HistoriesUtils.histories still contains all old entries because clear() never calls HistoriesUtils.init() or clears the list. Stories remain visually marked as 'clicked', hide-clicked filter still hides them. Only an app restart fixes it.

summary: HistoriesUtils.addHistory uses one System.currentTimeMillis() for the in-memory entry and UtilsKt.addHistory uses a separate call for persistence, producing divergent timestamps and an unsorted in-memory list
failure_scenario: User clicks a story: HistoriesUtils.addHistory records time T1=1700000000000 in memory (appended unsorted to end of list). UtilsKt.addHistory independently calls System.currentTimeMillis() giving T2=1700000000003, then sorts the persisted list by descending time. In-memory list order diverges from persisted order. On next init(), T2 overwrites T1. Repeated across a session with many clicks, the in-memory list becomes progressively more unsorted from the persisted order.

summary: Dead code — getHistorybyId() result assigned to variable h but never read, performing an unnecessary linear scan of the history list on every long-press
failure_scenario: User long-presses any story: a linear O(n) scan of the in-memory HistoriesUtils.histories list runs via getHistorybyId(story.id). The result is assigned to variable h but the variable is never referenced — no logic uses it. The scan is wasted computation on every long-press, and the unused variable suggests an unfinished feature.

summary: latest-task API filters for IN_PROGRESS/NEEDS_HELP/NEEDS_REVIEW but tasks are never transitioned from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS, so the API always returns null and DB-based session restoration never works
failure_scenario: User creates a task (status defaults to PENDING per start-task/route.ts line 24) then opens the app from a different browser with no local storage. loadTaskFromLocalStorage returns null, so fetchLatestTask is called. The API queries for tasks with status IN (IN_PROGRESS, NEEDS_HELP, NEEDS_REVIEW) but finds none because the task is still PENDING. Returns {task: null}. The user sees an empty chat and cannot resume the existing task — they must start a brand new task.

summary: completeTask() marks the task COMPLETED and then the loop breaks, but isOnAutopilot is never reset to false, deadlocking all subsequent triggerAgentWithMessage calls because setAutopilot(true) returns early when isOnAutopilot is already true
failure_scenario: First task runs to natural completion (AI responds without tool use). completeTask() at line 474 sets DB status to COMPLETED, then line 475 breaks the while loop. isOnAutopilot remains true. A second task job arrives at the worker: triggerAgentWithMessage adds the new message to messageStore and calls setAutopilot(true), which checks isOnAutopilot === value (lines 60-62) — both are true — so it returns immediately without calling runAgent(). The second task stays PENDING forever, its message never processed.

summary: Initial session message from fetchLatestTask uses raw Prisma JSON content without transforming through the same format as /api/messages, so images in tool_result blocks fail to render due to source vs image shape mismatch
failure_scenario: A task with image-bearing messages is loaded via fetchLatestTask.
