The raw DB content for an image block is {type:'image', source:{data:'...', media_type:'image/png', type:'base64'}} (per the Prisma schema comment at schema.prisma line 70). The MessageItem component at MessageItem.tsx line 36 checks block.type === 'image' && block.image — but raw DB content has 'source' not 'image', so block.image is undefined. The image does not render, showing a blank message instead.

summary: loadSession sets the initial message via setMessages but fails to call setLastMessageId(initialMessage.id), leaving lastMessageId as null and bypassing the incremental-fetch optimization on every subsequent poll
failure_scenario: Initial session loads with one message (id='abc-123'). lastMessageId stays null. Every 2-second poll sends lastMessageId=null to /api/messages, so the server returns ALL messages from the task. The client deduplicates via processedMessageIds, but the server-side createdAt > lastMessage.createdAt optimization at messages/route.ts lines 80-87 is never exercised. Every poll wastes DB bandwidth re-fetching and re-transmitting already-seen messages.

summary: startNewConversation is exported from the useChatSession hook but never destructured or called in page.tsx; the corresponding 'New Conversation' button is commented out in Header.tsx — dead code and incomplete feature
failure_scenario: Maintenance cost only. The hook return at line 249 includes startNewConversation but page.tsx lines 11-18 destructure only messages, input, setInput, isLoading, isLoadingSession, handleSend. Header.tsx lines 7-9 and 20-28 have commented-out props and button markup for a 'New Conversation' feature. The function exists but is unreachable, and the UI to trigger it was never un-commented — a partially implemented feature left in dead code.

summary: registerSyncInner replaces per-bidder userSync.canBidderRegisterSync() checks with a global filterConfig presence check, bypassing publisher-configured bidder-level include/exclude lists for user sync registration
failure_scenario: Publisher configures filterSettings: { iframe: { bidders: ['appnexus'], filter: 'include' } } to allow only AppNexus iframe syncs. The new code passes iframeEnabled=true to ALL bidders' getUserSyncs, so every bidder registers iframe syncs regardless of the publisher's per-bidder filtering.

summary: buildRequests only creates banner impression objects; video and native bid requests produce impressions missing media-type fields, silently breaking all non-banner bids
failure_scenario: A publisher configures a Preciso native ad unit. buildRequests creates an imp object { id: 'xyz', bidfloor: ..., bidfloorcur: ... } with NO native or banner field. The Preciso server receives an impression with no media type specification and returns no ad or rejects the request.

summary: emitAdRenderSucceeded changed property from 'id' to 'adId' but the function destructures 'id'; the AD_RENDER_SUCCEEDED event is emitted without adId, breaking downstream consumers
failure_scenario: A bid renders via renderAdDirect. emitAdRenderSucceeded({doc, bid, adId: bid.adId}) is called. The function destructures { doc, bid, id } so id=undefined, and the guard 'if (id)' skips setting data.adId. The AD_RENDER_SUCCEEDED event fires with { doc, bid } but no adId. Any analytics adapter or event listener that reads the adId from this event gets undefined.

summary: Removed '|| {}' fallback from getFloor() destructuring; if getFloor() returns null or undefined, destructuring throws TypeError and crashes the page
failure_scenario: A bidder adapter or floor module's getFloor() returns null (e.g., due to a misconfigured floor provider). The line const { currency, floor } = bid.getFloor({...}) throws 'TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'currency' of null'. The entire bidding process crashes.

summary: Removed optional chaining from floorInfo?.floor in getBannerBidFloor; if getFloor() returns null or undefined, accessing .floor throws TypeError
failure_scenario: A bidder's getFloor method is a function (passes isFn check) but returns null. floorInfo.floor throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'floor')'. The bid request fails with an uncaught exception.

summary: Removed isPlainObject(floorResult) guard from getFloor; if getFloor() returns null/undefined, accessing .currency throws TypeError
failure_scenario: isFn(bid.getFloor) passes, but bid.getFloor({...}) returns null. floorResult.currency throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'currency')'. Any bidder using riseUtils getFloor crashes.

summary: syncOrtb2 replaced with setBattrForAdUnit, losing all field synchronization between mediaTypes and ortb2Imp except battr; ORTB converters that read from mediaTypes now miss values set only in ortb2Imp
failure_scenario: Publisher sets ortb2Imp.video.mimes = ['video/mp4'] but not mediaTypes.video.mimes. Previously syncOrtb2 would copy it to mediaTypes.video.mimes so the ORTB converter's fillVideoImp could read it. Now the mimes value stays only in ortb2Imp and fillVideoImp reads mediaTypes.video which lacks mimes, so the ORTB request's imp.video has no mimes field.

summary: getPreparedBidForAuction now requires renderer.url; inline renderers defined without a URL property silently fail to apply
failure_scenario: Publisher defines an adUnit renderer as { render: myRenderFn } without a url property. The old code would install this renderer. The new code skips it because renderer.url is undefined. The bid renders without the publisher's custom renderer.

summary: flatSection guard narrowed from !Array.isArray to == null; a truthy non-array consent value reaches .reduceRight() and throws TypeError
failure_scenario: GPP consent data returns parsedSections[api] as a malformed object (truthy, not null, not an array). Old code would return it as-is; new code calls .reduceRight() on it, throwing 'TypeError: subsections.reduceRight is not a function'. The MSPA activity control crashes.

summary: Catch handler no longer excludes CSP NotSupportedError; pages with CSP restrictions on data: scheme for media get autoplay falsely disabled
failure_scenario: Publisher has Content-Security-Policy: media-src 'self' which blocks data: scheme media URLs. Autoplay detection video.play() rejects with NotSupportedError DOMException. The old code ignored this specific error; the new code sets autoplayEnabled=false, causing all autoplay-reliant video ads to fail.

summary: Removed storage.localStorageIsEnabled() guard before setDataInLocalStorage; throws when localStorage is disabled instead of silently skipping
failure_scenario: User has localStorage disabled (e.g., private browsing in some browsers). getapi() receives a UUID response and calls storage.setDataInLocalStorage('_pre|id', uuidValue) without checking if localStorage is available. The storage operation throws an unhandled error, breaking the bid flow.

summary: speakMessageHandler never updates assistantMessage state; the UI shows no assistant response text during non-streaming message processing
failure_scenario: A message arrives via direct_send (e.g. from messageReceiver.tsx or a timed event). speakMessageHandler processes it, calls handleSpeakAndStateUpdate which invokes speakCharacter — but neither handleSpeakAndStateUpdate nor any code in speakMessageHandler ever calls homeStore.setState({ assistantMessage: ... }). The assistantMessage store field stays empty or stale, so the UI component bound to assistantMessage shows nothing (or a previous response). In the old code, the speakCharacter onStart callback set assistantMessage: assistantMessage.join(' ') on every sentence; this was removed during the refactor.

summary: handleReceiveTextFromWsFn reads stale hs snapshot in speakCharacter's onStart callback; assistantMessage displays wrong content
failure_scenario: In external linkage mode, a WebSocket assistant response chunk arrives. upsertMessage at line 765 adds/updates the store's chatLog with the assistant message. Then speakCharacter's onStart callback (line 782) reads hs.chatLog[hs.chatLog.length - 1] — but hs was captured at line 731 before upsertMessage, so hs.chatLog is the old snapshot. For the first assistant chunk after a user message, the old last message is the user message, so assistantMessage gets set to the user's content instead of the assistant's response. For subsequent appending chunks (line 758), assistantMessage shows the pre-append content (stale by one chunk). In the old code, a local mutable updateLog was used, whose latest state was correctly read in the callback.

summary: isNewFile parameter is deserialized from the request body but never used; all chat sessions append to the same log file
failure_scenario: A user starts a new chat session. The client sends isNewFile: true (since lastSavedLogLength is 0 after rehydration). The API handler destructures isNewFile on line 25 but never references it again — it always uses getLatestLogFile() on line 42, which returns the newest existing log file. New session messages are appended to the previous session's log file instead of creating a new timestamped file. Over multiple sessions, a single log file accumulates messages from unrelated conversations, making session separation impossible.

summary: normalizeMessages now merges only messages with matching IDs, not just matching roles; old ID-less messages display as unmerged separate entries
failure_scenario: The app rehydrates chat history persisted before this change — those messages have no id field (the id property was just added to the Message type). When normalizeMessages processes consecutive same-role messages without IDs (e.g. two assistant messages), the condition lastItem.id !== undefined fails, so they fall to the 'else' branch and are inserted as separate entries instead of being merged. Users see duplicated-looking content in the chat log display, whereas previously these were combined into a single continuous message.

summary: Config-file `args` are silently dropped when `docker.distro` is not explicitly set, because `if self.args:` is incorrectly nested inside `if self.docker.distro is not None:` at line 862
failure_scenario: User writes `bentofile.yaml` with `args: {model_name: gpt-4}` and no explicit `docker.distro`. During `__attrs_post_init__`, `self.docker.distro` is None (default), so the entire `if self.docker.distro is not None:` block (lines 862–892) is skipped. The `if self.args:` block at line 889 -- nested at 12-space indent inside the 8-space `distro` guard -- never executes. Later `with_defaults()` creates a `FilledBentoBuildConfig` without forwarding `args`, so that instance's `self.args` is `{}` and the block is also skipped. The config-file args never reach `BentoMLContainer.bento_arguments`, so `bento.info.args` is `{}` and `use_arguments()` in the service sees nothing.

summary: QLinearGlobalAveragePool removed support for channels_last=1, replacing it with an assertion that crashes
failure_scenario: Any ONNX model that passes channels_last=1 to QLinearGlobalAveragePool will now hit `assert channels_last == 0` and crash with AssertionError. The old code handled channels_last=1 by permuting the input from NHWC to a spatial-first format before pooling.

summary: _check_prompt_id accepts fine-tune IDs that crash FineTunePromptBuilder at runtime -- validator only requires a non-empty suffix after 'fine_tune_prompt::' but FineTunePromptBuilder.__init__ requires 'project_id::task_id::fine_tune_id' (3 colon-delimited parts)
failure_scenario: Create RunConfig(prompt_id='fine_tune_prompt::ft_123456'). Validation passes (_check_prompt_id only checks non-empty suffix). Then BaseAdapter.__init__ calls prompt_builder_from_id which strips the prefix to 'ft_123456' and passes it to FineTunePromptBuilder, which splits by '::' and gets len=1 instead of 3, raising ValueError: 'Invalid fine-tune ID format. Expected project_id::task_id::fine_tune_id' -- a crash that the Pydantic validation layer should have prevented.

summary: Misleading comment on 'id::' validation: comment says 'check it has 4 parts' but code only checks for exactly 2 parts, consistent with the error message format 'id::[prompt_id]'
failure_scenario: A developer debugging a validation failure reads the comment and attempts a 4-part id::project::task::prompt format; the validator rejects it with the misleading message; developer wastes time trying to match the wrong comment instead of the correct 2-part format.

summary: Incomplete error message for eval_prompt:: validation: message says format is 'eval_prompt::[project_id]::[task_id]::[eval_id]' (4 parts) but code checks for exactly 5 parts (also requires eval_config_id)
failure_scenario: User provides a 4-part eval_prompt ID 'eval_prompt::p1::t1::e1' and gets the error telling them the expected format matches what they already provided; they have no idea the 5th part (eval_config_id) is missing because the error message omits it.

summary: Dead imports left behind after PromptGenerators/PromptId code extraction: 'Enum' (line 4), 'Annotated' (line 5), 'AfterValidator' (line 6) are no longer used anywhere in this file
failure_scenario: Each unused import adds noise, increases import time marginally, and can mislead maintainers into thinking this module still defines the PromptId validation types that were moved to prompt_id.py.

summary: enforceStorageTypeRule does strict string comparison against storage.type but the type can contain &-separated values (e.g. 'cookie&html5'), causing every storage access to be flagged as a mismatch
failure_scenario: User configures userSync.userIds with storage.type = 'cookie&html5' and enforceStorageType = true. When the submodule writes to cookie storage, params[ACTIVITY_PARAM_STORAGE_TYPE] is 'cookie', but submoduleConfig.storage.type is 'cookie&html5'. The !== comparison evaluates true, returning {allow: false} and blocking a valid write. The existing getConfiguredStorageTypes utility (line 907) already splits on &-separators, but enforceStorageTypeRule does not use it.

summary: enforceStorageTypeRule is never unregistered when userSync.userIds is removed from config or when init() is called again, leaving a dangling activity control rule with stale config snapshot that can incorrectly deny storage access
failure_scenario: 1) Set config: {userSync: {userIds: [{name: 'uid2', storage: {type: 'html5'}}], enforceStorageType: true}}. The rule is registered, blocking cookie writes for uid2. 2) Call resetUserIds(). This calls config.setConfig({userSync: {}}) then init(config) which creates a new closure. The old rule's unregister handle is lost in the previous init() scope — it can never be unregistered. 3) Set new config: {userSync: {userIds: [{name: 'uid2', storage: {type: 'cookie'}}], enforceStorageType: true}}. The old rule still has enforceStorageType=true with the old config snapshot (html5), so it returns {allow: false} for cookie writes. The new rule also runs but {allow: false} from any same-priority rule causes isActivityAllowed to return false immediately, so cookie writes are permanently blocked despite the new config allowing them.

summary: The includeLogProbs option was dropped from the callApi invocation; perplexity assertions will fail because providers no longer receive the flag to request log probabilities
failure_scenario: An eval with a config like 'assert: [{ type: perplexity, threshold: 5 }]' triggers callApi on the openai/azure/adaline provider. Without the third argument { includeLogProbs: true }, the provider never sends logprobs to the API, the response lacks logProbs, and the perplexity assertion handler throws 'does not support providers that do not return logProbs'.

summary: Test expectation changed to an error message ('Cannot use in operator') that the production code never throws for string results because typeof check short-circuits the in-expression
failure_scenario: The test mockRunPython.mockResolvedValue('string result') causes result to be the string 'string result'. The validation check '!result || typeof result !== "object" || (!("output" in result) && !("error" in result))' short-circuits at 'typeof result !== "object"' (true), so the in operator is never evaluated. The actual error thrown is 'The Python script call_api must return a dict..."string result"', not 'Cannot use in operator'. The test will fail when run.

summary: Discarded sycl::event from pr::uniform: GPU random threshold generation is asynchronous but its completion event is dropped; gen_random_thresholds returns a default (already-done) event, so downstream kernels may read random_bins_com before generation finishes.
failure_scenario: gen_random_thresholds calls pr::uniform (device_engine_dpc.cpp:86) which submits oneapi::mkl::rng::generate to the GPU queue. The returned sycl::event is discarded at this line. The function returns sycl::event() (line 524). The caller at line 1921-1922 waits on this no-op event and then passes random_bins_com to find_best_split. On an out-of-order SYCL queue the GPU generation kernel and the find_best_split kernel can overlap, causing find_best_split to read partially written or stale random threshold values.

summary: Assertion uses ctx.selected_row_count_ * ctx.tree_count_ instead of ctx.selected_row_total_count_ * ctx.tree_in_block_; in distributed mode selected_row_count_ is a sentinel bad_val_, and tree_count_ is the total tree count while buffers are sized for tree_in_block_.
failure_scenario: tree_order_lev_ is allocated as selected_row_total_count_ * tree_in_block_ (e.g. 256*32=8192). The assertion at line 245 checks selected_row_count_ * tree_count_. In non-distributed mode this is selected_row_total_count_ * tree_count_ (e.g. 256*100=25600), which fails whenever tree_count_ > tree_in_block_ (the common memory-constrained case). In distributed mode selected_row_count_ is never updated from its init value of bad_val_ (-1), making the assertion check a garbage product.

summary: Same wrong-constant bug as line 245: tree_order_buf assertion uses selected_row_count_ * tree_count_ instead of selected_row_total_count_ * tree_in_block_.
failure_scenario: Same root cause as finding at line 245 applied to the tree_order_buf assertion. Allocated size is selected_row_total_count_ * tree_in_block_; assertion checks a different product.

summary: Return value of pr::uniform_without_replacement (sycl::event) is discarded in a loop; for non-philox engines the internal skip_ahead_gpu may submit untracked GPU work.
failure_scenario: Each call to pr::uniform_without_replacement returns a sycl::event from a barrier kernel (device_engine_dpc.cpp:115-118) and also calls engine_.skip_ahead_gpu(count) which for state-based engines (mt2203, mrg32k3a, etc.) may submit a GPU skip operation whose event is discarded internally (skip_ahead_gpu returns void at device_engine.hpp:109-111). If a user selects a non-philox engine via the new set_engine_type API, the untracked skip operations can race with subsequent generate calls on the same device engine.

summary: Unused .to_host() copy: node_vs_tree_map is copied from device to host but the resulting host array is never read, wasting a device allocation and a D2H transfer per level.
failure_scenario: The old code used node_vs_tree_map_list_host to read tree_map_ptr[node] for per-tree engine selection. The new code uses a single shared engine and never reads this array. The to_host() allocates device memory and copies data on every call to gen_random_thresholds (once per tree level). In a 100-tree forest with depth 10 this wastes ~1000 unnecessary device allocations and D2H copies.

summary: Unused parameter engine_offset in gen_initial_tree_order: declared in the signature but never read in the function body, indicating incomplete refactoring from the old per-engine-list design.
failure_scenario: The old code indexed rng_engine_list[engine_offset + node_idx] to select a per-node random engine. The new code uses a single device engine and ignores engine_offset entirely. The caller at line 1884 still passes iter as this argument, which is dead computation. No runtime failure, but the dead parameter obscures the fact that the old skip-ahead-per-tree logic (host_engine_collection with per-engine skip callback) was completely replaced without an equivalent skip-ahead-per-tree mechanism for the single device engine.

summary: radix_sort_dpl overwrites its event variable each iteration and returns only the last row's event; if called with row_count > 1 on an out-of-order queue, earlier rows may not be complete when the caller waits on the returned event.
failure_scenario: radix_sort_dpl loops over rows (line 563) and assigns radix_sort_event = oneapi::dpl::... on each iteration (line 569). The function returns radix_sort_event (line 580) which holds only the last row's event. Currently no caller invokes the multi-row overload with row_count > 1, so this is latent, but any future caller that sorts multiple rows and waits on the returned event would proceed with incomplete sorts on earlier rows.

summary: Repeated kickoff() calls cause knowledge source chunks to grow unboundedly via extend() in source.add()
failure_scenario: If crew.kickoff() is called twice on the same Crew (e.g., retry, testing), set_knowledge() re-creates a Knowledge object and calls add_sources() again. Each source.add() appends new chunks to the source's self.chunks via extend() without clearing first. After N calls the chunks list is Nx the original size. While KnowledgeStorage.save() deduplicates by SHA-256 hash (so the vector store stays correct), the source objects leak memory and _save_documents() wastes CPU scanning a growing list.

summary: Date format validation uses substring matching, allowing invalid format strings to pass validation
failure_scenario: The check any(code in self.date_format for code in valid_format_codes) uses substring inclusion. A format string like '100% done' passes validation because '%d' is a substring of '100% done', but datetime.now().strftime('100% done') raises ValueError. The exception is caught and logged as a warning, so the date is silently not injected rather than the user being alerted to their invalid configuration. A proper check would verify that strftime can actually format the string.

summary: Useless try/except in add_sources() that catches Exception and immediately re-raises
failure_scenario: The block 'try: ... except Exception as e: raise e' is a semantic no-op that adds no error handling, logging, cleanup, or rollback. It suggests the developer intended to add error handling but never implemented it. When called from the new site in set_knowledge(), if any source.add() raises a non-ValueError/non-TypeError exception, it propagates through the no-op handler unchanged.

summary: Dead mock setup — patch('crewai.knowledge') never intercepts Knowledge creation in agent.py
failure_scenario: The test patches crewai.knowledge (the module) and sets mock_knowledge_instance.search.return_value and MockKnowledge.add_sources.return_value. But agent.py imports Knowledge directly from crewai.knowledge.knowledge, bypassing the module-level patch. These mock configurations are dead code that never take effect. The test passes only because of VCR cassette replay; without VCR, the real Knowledge class (with an empty storage, since add_sources is separately mocked) would produce different behavior.

summary: CancelButton is a no-op during loading because onCancel is never passed by any caller
failure_scenario: User sends a message → ChatInput enters loading state (isLoading=true) → CancelButton renders in active red 'canCancel' style → user clicks CancelButton expecting to abort the operation → handleSubmit fires, sees isLoading=true, calls onCancel?.() which is undefined → nothing happens, loading continues, user is confused.

summary: Hardcoded '24px' textarea height reset will diverge from CSS min-height if the stylesheet changes
failure_scenario: A future CSS change updates min-height in ChatInput.module.css from 24px to e.g. 28px for a new design system spacing token. After sending a message, the textarea resets to 24px (the hardcoded JS value) instead of 28px, producing a jarring height jump on the next keystroke as handleChange recalculates scrollHeight. This is fragile coupling between JS and CSS.

summary: Duplicate textarea auto-resize logic between useEffect (lines 29-36) and handleChange (lines 41-47)
failure_scenario: The identical 5-line resize snippet appears in two places. If the resize logic needs a fix (e.g. adding max-height clamping or scroll-padding), one site will inevitably be missed, creating inconsistent behavior between initial render and subsequent typing.

summary: Hardcoded hex colors (#459a72, #9c5b5a, and their rgba glow counterparts) bypass the project's CSS custom-property design system
failure_scenario: The design system defines --primary-accent (#1ded83) and --danger-high-contrast-text (#f75049) matching the glow colors. The hardcoded border colors #459a72 and #9c5b5a are darker custom shades with no design-token equivalent. If theming, dark/light mode, or color palette updates occur, these hardcoded values will not participate, making the ChatInput borders visually inconsistent with the rest of the UI.

summary: The `if (!v)` guard treats the number 0 as falsy, returning null for the valid epoch timestamp (1970-01-01). This breaks all callers of `newOffsetDate(offset)(value)` when value can be 0.
failure_scenario: `newOffsetDate(480)(0)` returns null instead of an OffsetDate for epoch. Downstream callers that call `.getTime()` on the result throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. Also affects `newOffsetDate(offset)('')` (falsy empty string) and `newOffsetDate(offset)(false)`. Should use `v == null` instead of `!v`.

summary: `newDate(rangeRes[MIN_ID]).getTime()` and `newDate(rangeRes[MAX_ID]).getTime()` call `.getTime()` on the result of `newOffsetDate` without a null guard, crashing when the service returns empty results.
failure_scenario: When `service(rangeQueryPayload)` returns an empty array, the destructuring default `{ [MIN_ID]: 0, [MAX_ID]: 0 }` kicks in. `newDate(0)` now returns null (due to the offset.ts `!v` bug), and `.getTime()` on null throws `TypeError`. This is a realistic crash path since the destructuring default was explicitly added to handle empty results.

summary: `newDate(x).getTime()` calls `.getTime()` on the result of `newOffsetDate` without a null guard. Crashes when a field value `x` is 0 (epoch timestamp) or another falsy value.
failure_scenario: During aggregate computation with a temporal field that has a format, `subGroup.map(r => r[mea.field])` produces field values. If any value is `0` (epoch), `newDate(0)` returns null from the offset.ts `!v` check, and `.getTime()` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getTime')`. Epoch can occur as a real timestamp when min/max aggregates return 0 for empty groups.

summary: Non-null assertion `getISOYear(v)!` suppresses TypeScript's type-checking without providing runtime safety for the null case.
failure_scenario: `getISOYear` now has a `return null` path (line 21). Although the `if (!v) return null;` guard at line 106 prevents null `v` from reaching this line, if the guard is ever removed or if `getISOYear` is refactored to return null for other reasons, `y` becomes null and propagates into `toOffsetDate(y, 0, 4)` which silently produces an invalid date (Date.UTC coerces null to 0). The `const y` should be checked for null before use, or the non-null assertion should be replaced with a proper null check.

summary: The Vega-Lite expression guard `datum[...]!==null` only checks for `null`, not `undefined`. A missing datum key passes the guard and reaches `toDate(undefined)`.
failure_scenario: If a Vega-Lite transform references a field `fid` that does not exist in some datums, `datum[fid]` evaluates to `undefined`. Since `undefined !== null` is `true`, the expression proceeds to `toDate(undefined)` which in Vega produces an invalid date result. The guard should use `datum[...] != null` or `datum[...] !== undefined && datum[...] !== null` to catch both.

summary: Same `!==null` vs undefined issue in the second Vega-Lite expression guard for non-date temporal offsets.
failure_scenario: Same as above: `datum[fid]` evaluating to `undefined` passes the `!==null` check. The expression `datum[...]${formatOffset(offsetTime)}` with undefined datum would produce `undefined${offset}` in Vega, resulting in unexpected behavior.

summary: `formatDate` returns the literal string `'null'` for null dates, which is displayed directly in UIs across data tables, pivot tables, and filter pills.
failure_scenario: Callers such as `dataTable/index.tsx:176`, `pivotTable/leftTree.tsx:39`, `filterField/simple.tsx:308`, and `filterField/tabs.tsx:660` all display `formatDate(parsedOffsetDate(...)(value))` directly. When the value is null/undefined/falsy, the chain produces the string `'null'` which appears as literal text in table cells and filter pill labels, confusing end users. Should return an empty string `''` or a localized placeholder instead.

summary: The overload signature `function creator(value: number | string | Date | null): OffsetDate | null` indicates null return only for null input, but the implementation returns null for any falsy value (0, '', false).
failure_scenario: TypeScript infers `newOffsetDate(offset)(0)` as returning `OffsetDate` (via the non-null overload at line 32), masking the runtime null return. Callers relying on TypeScript's type-checking will not see a type error, but `myDate.getTime()` will crash at runtime because the actual return is `null`. The overloads should either match the implementation's actual falsy-return behavior, or the implementation should use `v == null` to match the stated contract.

summary: Missing semicolon after `return null` statement.
failure_scenario: Style inconsistency. While JavaScript ASI inserts a semicolon, the rest of the function and codebase uses explicit semicolons. This is a minor maintainability issue but could trigger linter errors in strict configurations.

summary: Changed forbidden-import matching from module.startswith(lib) to module in libs, so submodule imports like 'from databricks.sdk import ...' are no longer detected
failure_scenario: Given config {'mlflow/*': ['databricks']}, code `from databricks.sdk.errors.platform import NotFound` at top level: old linter flags it (module='databricks.sdk.errors.platform' starts with 'databricks'), new linter silently passes (module string not an exact element of ['databricks']). The databricks_sdk_models_artifact_repo.py top-level import of NotFound at line 4 now passes the linter unchecked.

summary: Removal of 'not self.in_TYPE_CHECKING' guard means type-only imports inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks are now flagged as forbidden top-level imports
failure_scenario: An import like `from databricks.sdk import Something` placed inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (a standard pattern for type-only imports that avoids runtime dependencies) will now trigger a ForbiddenTopLevelImport lint error, causing false positives for safe, community-standard code.

summary: Same TYPE_CHECKING guard removal in visit_ImportFrom — TYPE_CHECKING imports are now flagged
failure_scenario: Same as line 400 but for `from X import Y` syntax: any forbidden module imported inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` now produces a false-positive lint error.

summary: @classmethod from_dictionary on Expectation returns hardcoded Expectation(...) instead of cls(...), breaking subclassing
failure_scenario: If a subclass `class StrictExpectation(Expectation): pass` exists, calling `StrictExpectation.from_dictionary({'value': 'test'})` returns an `Expectation` instance instead of a `StrictExpectation` instance, violating the factory-method contract.

summary: @classmethod from_dictionary on Feedback returns hardcoded Feedback(...) instead of cls(...), same subclassing breakage
failure_scenario: Any subclass of Feedback calling `SubFeedback.from_dictionary(d)` gets a base `Feedback` instance back instead of the subclass type.

summary: @classmethod from_str on Entity returns hardcoded Entity(...) instead of cls(...), breaking subclassing
failure_scenario: Any subclass of Entity calling `SubEntity.from_str('attr.something')` returns a base `Entity` instance instead of a `SubEntity`.

summary: @classmethod from_int on LoggedModelStatus returns hardcoded LoggedModelStatus.UNSPECIFIED etc. instead of cls.UNSPECIFIED, breaking subclassing
failure_scenario: Any subclass of LoggedModelStatus calling `SubStatus.from_int(1)` returns `LoggedModelStatus.PENDING` instead of `SubStatus.PENDING`.

summary: Undefined CLAMAV_ENABLED variable causes bash syntax error, crashing the container at startup
failure_scenario: Build and run the Docker image without explicitly passing `-e CLAMAV_ENABLED=true`. The variable is never defined as ARG or ENV in the Dockerfile (unlike GRAFANA_ENABLED and PUSHGATEWAY_ENABLED which have defaults at lines 11-12 and 19-20). `${CLAMAV_ENABLED}` expands to empty, making the command `if ; then` which is a bash syntax error. The entire start.sh exits with a syntax error and the container fails to start.

summary: scan() silently returns when the ScanResult is neither OK nor VirusFound, accepting unscanned files
failure_scenario: If the clamav-client library returns a ScanResult subtype other than OK or VirusFound (e.g., a scan-error or parse-failure result from the daemon), the if-else-if chain at lines 46-63 has no else/final branch. Execution falls through and the method returns normally. The controller proceeds to save the file as if it passed a clean scan. No log entry is written and no exception is thrown.

summary: uploadAgentPackage endpoint saves JAR files without ClamAV scanning, unlike the other upload endpoints
failure_scenario: An admin user uploads a JAR file containing malware via `POST /api/package/addAgentPackage`. The method calls `attachmentService.verifyAndSaveFile` directly without first calling `ClamAVScanner.getInstance().scan()`. Meanwhile, the `add` (line 136) and `addAttachment` (line 429) methods in the same controller were updated to include scanning. The JAR file is saved to disk and stored in the database with no virus check.

summary: Timeout only governs isReachable() pre-check; actual client.scan() call has no timeout, risking thread exhaustion
failure_scenario: A user uploads a large file (up to 2GB per StreamMaxLength in clamd.conf). `isReachable(timeout)` returns in 30ms confirming the daemon is alive, but the actual `client.scan(is)` call blocks for 60+ seconds as the daemon processes the file. The HTTP request thread is held for the entire duration. Under concurrent uploads, the Tomcat thread pool can exhaust and the service becomes unresponsive.

summary: InputStream parameter is never closed after scanning, risking file descriptor exhaustion
failure_scenario: The `scan(String, InputStream)` method passes the InputStream to `client.scan(is)` but never closes it in a finally block or try-with-resources. If `ClamavClient.scan()` does not close the stream (the library does not guarantee it does), each upload leaks a file descriptor. Over hundreds of uploads, the process hits the OS file descriptor limit, and subsequent uploads or file operations fail.

summary: validate_task validator short-circuits with 'return self', disabling all task-mismatch validation; dead code below references the old 'self.run_config' field (renamed to 'run_config_properties') and would crash with AttributeError if reached
failure_scenario: A TaskRunConfig with model_name='gpt-4', model_provider_name='openai', parented to task_A is accidentally parented (or re-parented) to task_B. No error is raised. When run_config() is called, it silently constructs a RunConfig with task=task_B (the wrong task), causing evaluation results to be attributed to the wrong task or the model to be invoked with wrong task instructions.

summary: run_config.prompt_id is never passed to adapter_for_task; the adapter internally creates a new RunConfig with the default prompt, silently ignoring any custom prompt_id configured in the eval's TaskRunConfig
failure_scenario: A user configures a TaskRunConfig with prompt_id='simple_chain_of_thought' expecting chain-of-thought prompting. The eval runs but uses the default SIMPLE prompt instead. The eval scores are produced with the wrong prompt strategy, invalidating the comparison. No error or warning is emitted.

summary: run_job catches all exceptions with a bare 'except Exception' and only prints to stdout, then returns False; no error details are persisted, no structured logging, and the user sees only a count of errors with no way to diagnose which jobs failed or why
failure_scenario: A transient API rate-limit error causes 3 out of 50 eval jobs to fail. The progress shows 'errors: 3' but there is no record of which dataset items failed or what the specific errors were. The user must re-run the entire eval to reproduce, and still has no per-item error log.

summary: RunConfigProperties(task=sample_task, ...) passes an invalid 'task' keyword argument; Pydantic v2 silently ignores extra fields, so the test passes but the copy-paste error from the old RunConfig API is masked
failure_scenario: A developer copies this pattern elsewhere expecting 'task' to be a valid field on RunConfigProperties. The invalid field is silently ignored at runtime. If Pydantic's extra handling is ever changed to 'forbid', this test and any copied patterns would start raising ValidationError for the wrong reason.

summary: replaceAuctionPrice not called on bid response ad/vastUrl fields -- price macros like ${AUCTION_PRICE} are left unreplaced
failure_scenario: Server returns vastUrl: 'https://vast.server.com/win?price=${AUCTION_PRICE}'. The createBid function passes it through literally. Prebid renders the win URL with the literal macro string instead of the actual CPM, breaking win-price reporting and auction clearing. The old code called replaceAuctionPrice on adm and nurl; this was removed without replacement. Every other adapter in this codebase (a1Media, adot, adxcg, alkimi, apacdex, axonix, bidtheatre, etc.) still uses replaceAuctionPrice on bid responses.

summary: getViewableDistance compares viewport-relative elementMiddle against page-relative (window.scrollY + viewportHeight), mixing coordinate systems
failure_scenario: Viewport is 800px tall, user has scrolled 1000px down the page. An element has getBoundingClientRect().top = 1200 (i.e., 1200px below the viewport top -- clearly out of view). elementMiddle = 1250 (viewport-relative), while window.scrollY + viewportHeight = 1800 (page-relative). The comparison 1250 > 1800 is false, so the 'below viewport' branch is never entered. The element is incorrectly classified and DistanceToView receives 1250 instead of 450 (the actual distance past viewport bottom). Conversely, an element fully visible in the viewport (elementMiddle = 300, viewport-relative) is correctly compared against 1800 (page-relative), 300 > 1800 is false, falls through to 'return Math.round(300)' -- a positive value reported for an element already in view when it should be 0. The correct comparison is elementMiddle > viewportHeight without adding window.scrollY.

summary: withCredentials: true removed from request options -- cross-origin cookies no longer sent with bid requests
failure_scenario: The old code set options: { withCredentials: true } on every outgoing request, allowing session cookies to be sent cross-origin. The new buildRequests omits this entirely, so the browser defaults to withCredentials: false for cross-origin POST requests. If the bidmatic server uses cookies for user identification, frequency capping, or session state, these features silently break -- the server sees every request as anonymous.

summary: isBidRequestValid logs a warning but still returns true when bid.params.bidfloor is not a number
failure_scenario: Publisher configuration has bidfloor: 'five' (a string). isBidRequestValid enters bid.params.bidfloor && !isNumber(...) branch, logs a warning, then returns isNumber(source) which is true. The invalid bid request passes validation. Downstream, getBidFloor's catch block calls isNumber('five') which returns false, so the floor is silently undefined and stripped by cleanObj. The bid goes to auction with no floor, potentially winning at any price below the publisher's intended floor.

summary: remapBidRequest accesses bidRequests[0] without checking array length -- Schain/UserEids/UserIds silently dropped on empty input
failure_scenario: remapBidRequest is called with an empty bidRequests array (e.g., a no-bid scenario or test edge case). bidRequests[0] is undefined, so deepAccess(undefined, ...) returns undefined for Schain, UserEids, and UserIds. cleanObj strips all undefined values, so the server request is sent without supply chain data (Schain), violating supply chain transparency requirements.

summary: Test name says 'should return empty array' but assertion expects undefined from getUserSyncsFn
failure_scenario: The test description on line 361 says 'should return empty array when no syncs enabled', but line 363 asserts expect(result).to.be.undefined. The function getUserSyncsFn does return undefined when no syncs are enabled (empty return on line 109 of the adapter). Either the test name is wrong (it should say 'should return undefined') or the function should return [] instead of undefined to match Prebid.js conventions. This mismatch masks a potential inconsistency where the function returns [] in some branches and undefined in others.

summary: Compile error: ProviderNotFoundException is not imported (it lives in java.nio.file.spi, not java.nio.file)
failure_scenario: The catch clause at line 70 uses `ProviderNotFoundException` which is declared in `java.nio.file.spi`. The only relevant import is `java.nio.file.*` (line 27), which does NOT cover `java.nio.file.spi`. No explicit import for `ProviderNotFoundException` exists anywhere. This will fail to compile on any JDK version.

summary: Resource leak: when obtainLock acquires the first lock but the second lock fails, releaseLock(id) is called before locks[id] is set, so the first lock's FileChannel and FileLock are never cleaned up
failure_scenario: Call obtainLock(2, 6, metaInfo) where CPU 2 is free but CPU 6 is held by another process. tryAcquireLockOnFile(2, ...) succeeds (opens a FileChannel, acquires exclusive FileLock, writes metaInfo) and returns a LockReference. tryAcquireLockOnFile(6, ...) returns null (CPU 6 is locked). The code calls releaseLock(2) at line 118, but locks[2] was never assigned (the assignment only happens at lines 109 or 114 on success paths). releaseLock(2) checks locks[2] != null, finds null, and does nothing. The FileChannel and FileLock for CPU 2 are never closed — they leak until JVM exit. The lock file for CPU 2 persists and blocks other processes from acquiring it.

summary: Resource leak: when acquireCore(false) is used (reserve without binding), LockCheck.updateCpu creates lock files for both CPUs but LockInventory.release only cleans up the primary CPU, leaking the HT pair's lock file
failure_scenario: Call acquireCore(false) to reserve a whole core without immediate binding. At line 85, LockCheck.updateCpu(cpuId, cpuId2) creates lock files for BOTH logical CPUs. Then assignCurrentThread(false, true) at line 86 sets assignedThread on the primary lock only — bindWholeCore is NOT called because bind=false. Later, calling release() iterates logicalCoreLocks at line 266, finds the primary lock (assignedThread == t) and releases it, but the HT pair lock at logicalCoreLocks[cpuId2] has assignedThread == null (never set because bindWholeCore was never called). The pair's lock file and file channel are never released, blocking other processes from acquiring it.

summary: Sentinel value 0 for 'no hyperthread pair' collides with CPU 0 when it genuinely IS the HT pair, causing FileLockBasedLockChecker.obtainLock(id, 0, ...) to wrongly skip locking the paired CPU
failure_scenario: On a system where CPU 0 is the genuine hyperthread pair of another CPU (e.g., a 2-core 2-thread system where CPU 2 has pair(2)=0), calling pair(2) returns 0. When used in obtainLock(2, 0, metaInfo), the check `if (id2 <= 0)` at FileLockBasedLockChecker line 107 treats 0 as 'no second lock' and only locks CPU 2, missing the paired CPU 0. The whole-core reservation is silently incomplete. In standard Linux SMT numbering this is unlikely but not impossible with non-standard /proc/cpuinfo layouts or user-supplied CPU layouts via fromProperties().

summary: Missing bounds check: pair(int cpuId) calls cpuDetails.get(cpuId) without validation, throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException for out-of-range input instead of returning a safe default
failure_scenario: User code calls CpuLayout.pair(-1) or pair(n) where n >= cpus(). The method calls cpuDetails.get(cpuId) which throws an uncaught IndexOutOfBoundsException. This public API method should validate input and return a safe sentinel (like -1 or 0) instead of crashing.

summary: Dead code: schemasInUse.addAll(discriminators) has no functional effect because schemasInUse is never read after this line within the same tryCleanup call, and each tryCleanup invocation creates a fresh schemasInUse HashSet
failure_scenario: The addAll call is harmless but unnecessary — the discriminators set computed at lines 159-165 is already applied to schemasNotInUse and choicesSchemasNotInUse (lines 166-167), which are the only sets used by the removal logic at lines 173-200. The schemasInUse set is not referenced again in this method body after line 168. No correctness impact, but represents either incomplete work (if transitive discriminator discovery was intended) or an unnecessary statement that can mislead maintainers about the data flow.

summary: Clipboard is not restored when the main AppleScript throws; no try/finally protects the restore call
failure_scenario: User has important text in clipboard. They call askChatGPT('some prompt'). The AppleScript times out after 120 seconds (or throws for any other reason). The clipboard was set to 'some prompt' by the script. The error is caught and rethrown at line 252, but the clipboard restore at line 225 never executes. User permanently loses their original clipboard content.

summary: encodeForAppleScript escapes only double quotes, not backslashes, causing malformed AppleScript on backslash-containing clipboard or prompt text
failure_scenario: User's clipboard contains '<WINDOWS_USER_PATH>'. encodeForAppleScript returns it unchanged. The clipboard-restore AppleScript becomes 'set the clipboard to "<WINDOWS_USER_PATH>"'. In AppleScript, \" at the end creates an escaped-quote inside the string, leaving no closing delimiter. The AppleScript call fails with a syntax error, and the clipboard is not restored.

summary: getConversations no longer calls checkChatGPTAccess, so ChatGPT is not auto-launched if not running
failure_scenario: User asks Claude to list ChatGPT conversations, but ChatGPT app is closed. The original code would call checkChatGPTAccess which tries to activate/launch ChatGPT (via 'tell application "ChatGPT" to activate'). The new getConversations runs its own AppleScript that checks process existence, returns 'ChatGPT is not running', and throws without attempting to launch. The user gets an error instead of ChatGPT being auto-launched.

summary: Global regex replacement of 'Regenerate' and 'Continue generating' strips these substrings from valid ChatGPT responses
failure_scenario: ChatGPT produces a response like 'You should regenerate the API key and continue generating the report.' After post-processing, this becomes 'You should  the API key and  the report.' -- meaningful content is silently removed from the response returned to Claude.

summary: Storing pointers to vector elements (&context_params_list.back()) while growing the same vector via push_back; reallocation invalidates previously stored pointers, so the pointer array passed to contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync contains dangling references when context_bin_map.size() > 1.
failure_scenario: Two or more binary files in context_bin_map: the first iteration push_back into context_params_list (capacity 0→1), stores pointer at context_params_ptr_list[0]. The second push_back triggers reallocation (capacity 1→2 or similar), invalidating the pointer at context_params_ptr_list[0]. contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync reads corrupted/garbage context params for the first file. Fix: reserve(context_bin_map.size()) before the loop.

summary: Null pointer dereference: SharedContext::GetInstance().GetSharedQnnBackendManager() can return nullptr (default shared_ptr), but line 724 calls qnn_backend_manager->ProcessContextFromBinListAsync(...) without a null check.
failure_scenario: If SetSharedQnnBackendManager has not been called before the async callback fires (or was ResetSharedQnnBackendManager'd), GetSharedQnnBackendManager() returns a null shared_ptr. Dereferencing it causes a segfault in the callback.

summary: Use-after-free: notifyParam (it.second.get(), a raw pointer into a vector owned by context_bin_map's unique_ptr) is passed to the async callback. In qnn_execution_provider.cc line 945, context_bin_map.clear() is called after SetupBackend returns, destroying the vector. If the callback fires asynchronously after that, it dereferences freed memory.
failure_scenario: contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync is called with the callback. SetupBackend returns, GetCapability clears context_bin_map (destroying the vector notifyParam points to). The async callback fires on another thread, calls ProcessContextFromBinListAsync which dereferences notifyParam as vector<string>* — use-after-free, heap corruption.

summary: Data race on ep_context_handle_map_: ProcessContextFromBinListAsync modifies the map under ep_context_handle_map_mutex_, but SetupBackend's early-return path (line 1170) and LoadCachedQnnContextFromBuffer (line 1075) both read the map without any lock.
failure_scenario: The async callback fires while the early-return path in SetupBackend for a second session is also iterating and reading ep_context_handle_map_. Unsynchronized concurrent read+write on unordered_map — undefined behavior, potential crash or silent corruption.

summary: Error status from async context creation silently ignored: the Qnn_ErrorHandle_t status parameter passed to ContextCreateAsyncCallback by contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync is discarded. Invalid or partially-initialized context handles may be added to the map and context list as if creation succeeded.
failure_scenario: contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync reports an error via the callback's status parameter (e.g., QNN_CONTEXT_ERROR_MEMORY_ALLOC). The callback ignores it, still calls ProcessContextFromBinListAsync, which adds the (potentially invalid/null) context handle via AddQnnContextHandle and maps all node names to it. Later inference attempts using this invalid handle crash or produce wrong results.

summary: No null-pointer check before calling qnn_interface_.contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync; the same file checks qnn_interface_.contextCreateFromBinary before calling it (line 1109). An older QNN runtime library lacking this function will crash on a null function pointer call.
failure_scenario: Code compiled against QNN SDK >= 2.26 headers but linked/loaded against an older QNN runtime library that does not export contextCreateFromBinaryListAsync. The function pointer in qnn_interface_ is null. Calling it on line 827 causes a null function pointer dereference crash.

summary: Data race on context_map_ and contexts_: ProcessContextFromBinListAsync calls AddQnnContextHandle, which modifies context_map_ (try_emplace at line 2093) and contexts_ (push_back at line 2096). This is only serialized by ep_context_handle_map_mutex_, but other paths like CreateContext (line 894) and LoadCachedQnnContextFromBuffer (line 1120) also call AddQnnContextHandle without any mutex protection.
failure_scenario: The async callback fires while Compile is running LoadCachedQnnContextFromBuffer on another thread. Both threads call AddQnnContextHandle concurrently, racing on context_map_ and contexts_. This results in heap corruption or double-free of QNN context handles.

summary: Generated image URL from OpenAI is stored permanently in DB but OpenAI-hosted image URLs expire (typically 1-2 hours), causing permanent broken images for previously processed magic diagrams.
failure_scenario: User takes a magic diagram photo → background worker calls OpenAI images.edit, gets back a temporary URL → URL stored in generated_image_url column → user views the file later that day or next day → broken image, permanent data loss because the generated image was never re-uploaded to R2.

summary: OpenAI images.edit endpoint is used for generating new diagrams from sketches, but images.edit is designed for inpainting/editing existing images (typically requires a mask); images.generate would be the correct endpoint for creating a new diagram from a prompt.
failure_scenario: User captures a sketch for magic diagram processing → backend calls openaiImageClient.images.edit with gpt-image-1 model → API either rejects the call (missing mask), returns a poorly edited original instead of a new diagram, or the model name 'gpt-image-1' is not recognized by OpenAI → processing fails with an API error.

summary: processType is never saved to the metadata object in saveFileLocally and never read back when constructing SharedFile in processSyncQueue, so any file saved locally loses its processType and defaults to standard-ocr when synced.
failure_scenario: A magic-diagram SharedFile (with processType='magic-diagram') is passed to saveFileLocally → metadata JSON stored without processType → device goes offline → later when online, processSyncQueue reads metadata, constructs SharedFile without processType → handleFileProcess uses default 'standard-ocr' → the sketch is OCR'd instead of being sent to magic diagram generation.

summary: prepareFile default MIME type construction generates non-standard MIME types like 'application/md' or 'application/heif' instead of proper types like 'text/markdown' or 'image/heif'; previously it fell back to 'application/octet-stream' which is at least unambiguous.
failure_scenario: A markdown file is shared without an explicit MIME type → prepareFile generates mimeType='application/md' → stored in DB as application/md rather than text/markdown → FileCard renders it as generic file instead of text, and server-side processSingleFileRecord fails to match it as text/plain or text/markdown in the else branch (line 334), treating it as unsupported.

summary: Missing R2 environment variables produce a console.error warning but execution continues; the r2Client is constructed with asserted non-null credentials (lines 32-33 using !) that may be undefined, causing confusing runtime errors on first R2 access instead of a clear startup failure.
failure_scenario: R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID or R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY is missing from environment → warning logged at startup → worker starts, picks up a pending file → first call to downloadFromR2 fails with an opaque AWS SDK error about missing credentials → file marked as error with an unhelpful message, and ALL subsequent files fail the same way.

summary: The pending files query has no ORDER BY clause, so files are processed in non-deterministic database order; combined with the .limit(10), older files can be starved indefinitely if new uploads keep arriving.
failure_scenario: 10 files are uploaded in quick succession → each cron run picks up 10 pending files in arbitrary order → if a file happens to always be outside the first 10 results, it never gets processed while newer files keep jumping ahead in the indeterminate ordering.

summary: needsProcessingTrigger is always true because uploadFile always returns status='pending' (never 'completed'), making the entire else-branch (lines 463-474) for direct text upload completion dead code; text files unnecessarily go through the trigger+poll flow.
failure_scenario: A text file is uploaded via the presigned URL flow → uploadFile returns status='pending' → needsProcessingTrigger evaluates to true (since status is never 'completed') → text file waits for background worker polling (~90 seconds) instead of being treated as immediately complete, adding unnecessary latency.

summary: The console.log that reported why a queued file failed processing (with the error message) was deleted; when a file errors during sync queue processing and is moved to the end of the queue, there is now no log indicating what went wrong.
failure_scenario: A queued sync file fails processing (e.g., network error, server 500) → the item is silently moved to the end of the queue → the failure is invisible in logs → developers cannot diagnose why files keep retrying without visible errors.

summary: processImageWithGPT4o creates a new OpenAI client instance via createOpenAI on every call; a module-level singleton already exists at line 15 (openaiImageClient), and this per-call instantiation is redundant.
failure_scenario: Background worker processes 10 image files in one run → processImageWithGPT4o is called 10 times → each call creates a new createOpenAI instance with the same API key → 10 unnecessary object allocations, though no functional bug.

summary: Content moderation logic (profanity word-list filtering) is duplicated between FileCard.tsx:runContentModeration (lines 12-37) and file-handler.ts:moderateContent (lines 39-61); the two implementations differ slightly in return shape and word lists.
failure_scenario: Maintenance burden: fixing a bug or adding a new flagged term requires updating two separate implementations; the two functions use different word lists ('vulgar'/'explicit'/'offensive'/'inappropriate' in FileCard vs 'explicit'/'inappropriate'/'offensive'/'banned' in file-handler), leading to inconsistent moderation results depending on which code path runs.

summary: The FilePreview component computes isPdf, isImage, isText (lines 42-46) and defines handleError (line 56) but none of these are used; renderPreview always renders an Image regardless of mimeType, and error handling is done inline in the onError callback.
failure_scenario: Maintenance burden: future developers see the computed isPdf/isText variables and assume the component handles multiple file types, but it only renders images; the handleError function exists but is never called; styles pdfView, genericContainer, fileNameText, mimeTypeText (lines 151-192) are defined but never referenced, increasing bundle size and confusion.

summary: processMagicDiagram uses a hardcoded token estimate of 5000 regardless of actual API usage; the OpenAI response may include actual token counts but they are not extracted.
failure_scenario: User's token usage is over-counted or under-counted for magic diagram generations → billing/rate-limiting based on token counts is inaccurate → user may be charged for more tokens than actually used, or may exceed limits without being throttled.

summary: Pydantic silently ignores underscore-prefixed fields in __init__, so _internal_config passed to TrainableModel(...) constructor is discarded and defaults to None
failure_scenario: User creates TrainableModel(name='x', project='y', base_model='Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct', _internal_config=InternalModelConfig(init_args=InitArgs(gpu_memory_utilization=0.75))) — pydantic's default extra='ignore' silently drops the unrecognized _internal_config kwarg. model._internal_config remains None. When _get_service later calls get_model_config(config=model._internal_config), it falls back to defaults (gpu_memory_utilization=0.79, lora_alpha=16, etc.) instead of the user's custom values. Affects examples/hn_title_generator/train.py:239, examples/2048/2048.ipynb:369, and examples/temporal-clue.ipynb:88.

summary: The any(isinstance(t, Trajectory) for t in trajectories) call consumes the first element of a generator iterator, causing TrajectoryGroup to miss it
failure_scenario: Call model.log(trajectory_generator, 'val') where trajectory_generator yields Trajectory objects. The any() call on line 107 consumes the first Trajectory from the generator (stopping at the first True). Then on line 109, TrajectoryGroup(cast(Iterable[Trajectory], trajectories)) receives the partially-consumed generator and silently skips the first trajectory, producing an incomplete log. Currently masked because gather_trajectory_groups returns a list, not a generator.

summary: Mutable default argument TrainConfig() is evaluated once at function definition, shared across all train() calls
failure_scenario: The parameter config: TrainConfig = TrainConfig() creates one TrainConfig(learning_rate=5e-6, beta=0.0) instance at module load time. All calls to model.train() without an explicit config argument share this same mutable pydantic model instance. If any caller mutates the default instance (e.g., model.train(trajectories) followed by code that inadvertently modifies the returned config's attributes), subsequent calls see the mutated values. The pydantic model is not frozen (no model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)).

summary: Field named 'config' on a pydantic BaseModel is confusingly close to pydantic's reserved 'model_config' class attribute
failure_scenario: A maintainer might confuse model_instance.config (the user's config field, type pydantic.BaseModel | None) with Model.model_config (pydantic's ConfigDict class attribute). No runtime error occurs because Python attribute resolution keeps them separate, but the naming makes code review and static analysis harder, especially when pydantic itself uses model_config for configuration.

summary: Concurrent calls to TrainableModel.register_for_training can race at await points, leaving inconsistent _api/_openai_client state
failure_scenario: Two asyncio coroutines call await model.register_for_training(api_a) and await model.register_for_training(api_b) concurrently. Coroutine A sets self._api = api_a and awaits at line 53. Coroutine B then sets self._api = api_b (overwriting). Both resume, each using their local api variable to create clients. The final self._api is api_b but self._openai_client could be from api_a or api_b depending on scheduling. The model is left in an inconsistent state where self._api points to one API but the cached client belongs to another.

summary: Stale docstring on register_for_training still describes old get_or_create_model behavior instead of current registration-only behavior
failure_scenario: The docstring says 'Retrieve an existing model or create a new one' but the method no longer creates or retrieves a model — it only calls os.makedirs() to create the output directory. A developer reading this docstring would be misled about the method's actual responsibility. The method signature also changed: it no longer takes name/project/base_model parameters, yet the docstring describes them.

summary: Struct fields p11module/p11cert guarded by #ifndef OPENSSL_NO_ENGINE but code accesses them with broader #if !defined(OPENSSL_NO_ENGINE) || OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER>=0x30000000L, causing compile error on OpenSSL 3.0+ without engine
failure_scenario: Build with -DOPENSSL_NO_ENGINE against OpenSSL 3.0+: struct GLOBAL_OPTIONS has no p11module/p11cert fields, but osslsigncode.c references them via the broader preprocessor guard → compile error

summary: read_pkcs7_certfile called with NULL certfile when PKCS#11 provider loads but certs fail silently and no -certs option given, causing BIO_new_file(NULL, ...) crash
failure_scenario: User runs: osslsigncode sign -pkcs11module /path/to/pkcs11.so -key 'pkcs11:token=t;object=key' -pkcs11cert 'pkcs11:token=t;object=cert' on OpenSSL 3.0. Provider loads successfully but cert URI fails. certfile is NULL, certs stack is empty → read_pkcs7_certfile(options) called → BIO_new_file(NULL, "rb") → segfault

summary: Validation allows -provider alone without -pkcs11module on OpenSSL 3.0+, but read_crypto_params only loads provider inside the p11module block, leading to crash on NULL certfile
failure_scenario: User runs: osslsigncode sign -provider /path/to/pkcs11prov.so -in file.exe -out signed.exe on OpenSSL 3.0+. Validation passes (provider is a valid sign parameter). In read_crypto_params, p11module is NULL so provider is never loaded; no key, no certs, certfile is NULL → read_pkcs7_certfile crashes

summary: sk_X509_new_null returns not checked for NULL; on OOM, subsequent sk_X509_push/sk_X509_num on NULL stack segfaults
failure_scenario: System under memory pressure → sk_X509_new_null() returns NULL for options->certs → later load_objects_from_store calls sk_X509_push(NULL, ...) or sk_X509_num(NULL) at line 4271 → segfault

summary: Infinite loop in load_objects_from_store when OSSL_STORE_load returns NULL due to non-EOF error (OSSL_STORE_eof returns 0 for errors, continue re-enters loop)
failure_scenario: Corrupt PKCS#12 file → OSSL_STORE_load returns NULL (error, not EOF) → OSSL_STORE_eof returns 0 → loop continues → OSSL_STORE_load returns NULL again → infinite loop, hang

summary: Resource leak: OSSL_STORE_INFO_get1_CERT/get1_CRL increments refcount but sk_X509_push return value unchecked; on push failure (OOM) the cert/CRL is leaked
failure_scenario: Low memory → sk_X509_push fails (returns 0) → cert already had refcount incremented by get1_CERT → object leaked (refcount never decremented). Same pattern at lines 4371 and 4178

summary: Missing NULL check for p7->d.sign before accessing p7->d.sign->cert in read_pkcs7_certfile; non-signed-data PKCS7 causes segfault
failure_scenario: User passes a PKCS7 EnvelopedData file as -certs → d2i_PKCS7_bio succeeds with non-NULL p7 → p7->d.sign is NULL (data is in p7->d.enveloped) → p7->d.sign->cert derefs NULL → segfault

summary: PVK key format support silently removed: comment claims PVK is supported but all PVK-specific code (find_pvk_key, read_pvk_key, b2i_PVK_bio, magic-byte detection) was deleted; OpenSSL STORE API does not support PVK format
failure_scenario: User with Microsoft PVK private key and .spc certificate file → load_objects_from_store fails to load the PVK key (unsupported format) → read_der_keyfile also fails → read_crypto_params returns 0 → signing fails with no actionable error message

summary: providers_cleanup calls UI_destroy_method on the UI method but does not reset the static ui_method pointer to NULL; if ui_osslsigncode is called again it returns a destroyed object
failure_scenario: providers_cleanup() called at exit (line 5215). If code is later refactored to clean up and re-initialize providers in the same process, ui_osslsigncode() returns a destroyed UI_METHOD → use-after-free or crash in subsequent OSSL_STORE_open

summary: OSSL_STORE_INFO_get1_PKEY overwrites *pkey without freeing previous value if store returns multiple keys
failure_scenario: PKCS#12 or other store containing two private keys → first key loaded via get1_PKEY and stored in *pkey → second key loaded via get1_PKEY and overwrites *pkey → first key's refcount never decremented → memory leak

summary: Outer `except Exception` in fetch_auth_token swallows all ApiServerException raises (non-200 status, missing token, JSON processing failure) and silently returns None instead
failure_scenario: Server returns HTTP 401 → `raise ApiServerException('Authentication failed: 401')` executes inside the outer try → caught by `except Exception as e:` on line 56 → logged → returns None. Callers of `agentops.init()` (including ~20 examples and the langchain integration) receive None instead of an exception, proceed with an uninitialized client, and all subsequent tracing calls silently no-op.

summary: _set_span_attributes replaced the dual guard `not attributes or not hasattr(span, 'set_attribute')` with only `span is None`, removing the hasattr safety check
failure_scenario: A mock span or proxy object that is not None but lacks a `set_attribute` method is passed via Session.end_session() or end_session() → line 178 `span.set_attribute(...)` raises `AttributeError`, bypassing the guarded paths and potentially crashing the caller's teardown logic.

summary: Return type annotation `-> AuthTokenResponse` is now inaccurate; fetch_auth_token returns None on every error path, violating the declared return type
failure_scenario: Static type checkers (mypy/pyright) report no issues with callers accessing `response['token']` after `fetch_auth_token()`, but at runtime `response` is None → `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` at any call site that follows the type annotation.

summary: Dummy session construction `Session(None, None); _current_session = dummy; return dummy` appears identically in both the try block (lines 141-143) and except block (lines 147-149), copy-paste duplication
failure_scenario: A future maintainer updates the dummy-session logic in one block but forgets the other → the two code paths diverge (e.g., one logs a warning and the other does not, or one sets _current_session and the other does not), producing different behavior depending on whether the initialization failed via return-None vs exception.

summary: Two adjacent `if session_or_status.span is not None:` blocks (lines 276, 278) test the same condition redundantly; the second block could use `else` or the two guarded calls could share a single `if`
failure_scenario: If a refactor adds early-return logic or extra mutations inside the first block, the span could be consumed/modified before the second block executes, causing _finalize_span and _flush_span_processors to silently skip while _set_span_attributes already ran — a half-finalized session. With a single guard this mistake would be structurally prevented.

summary: Modified Time value read from the wrong column: validity check uses index 9 (Last Modified) but data read uses index 8 (Icon), which is the pre-Tags column number that was not updated
failure_scenario: User imports a CSV with a Last Modified column mapped. The entry's modification time is parsed from the value in the Icon column (e.g., an integer 0-99 becomes a 1970 timestamp) instead of the actual timestamp column.

summary: Created Time value read from the wrong column: validity check uses index 10 (Created) but data read uses index 9 (Last Modified), which was not updated after the Tags column insertion
failure_scenario: User imports a CSV with a Created column mapped. The entry's creation time is parsed from the Last Modified column instead. The Created column value is silently ignored.

summary: Error message truncation label shows wrong skip count: appendStatusMsg no longer appends a trailing newline per message, so text.count('\n') returns one less than the number of messages, causing 'N more message(s) skipped' to display N-1
failure_scenario: CSV file has 4 malformed records producing 4 error messages. Two are displayed with the label '[1 more message(s) skipped]' but actually 2 are skipped. The singular/plural form is also wrong.

summary: testEmptyReparsing test removed, silently dropping coverage for the parse(nullptr) followed by reparse() code path
failure_scenario: A future refactoring that breaks the reparse-after-null behavior would not be caught by the test suite. The behavior is preserved currently but unguarded.

summary: request.data.dict() crashes for JSON POST because request.data returns a plain dict from json.loads(), not a QueryDict with a .dict() method
failure_scenario: A JSON POST request (Content-Type: application/json) triggers the dev middleware to call request_as_dict(). At line 140, request.data.dict() raises AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'dict', crashing the request-logging path.

summary: json.JSONDecodeError from request.data.get() bypasses the UnreadablePostError handler in the CSRF middleware, causing a 500 error instead of a 403
failure_scenario: A POST request with Content-Type: application/json and an invalid JSON body reaches a CSRF-protected view. request.data.get('_csrftoken', '') at line 367 triggers _load_data_and_files(), which calls json.loads(self.body) and raises json.JSONDecodeError on malformed JSON. The except UnreadablePostError at line 368 does not catch json.JSONDecodeError, so the exception propagates to _get_csrf_response which only catches RejectRequest, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of the expected 403 response.

summary: Stale comment in _load_data_and_files still references old attribute names 'self.POST' and 'self._post' which no longer exist after the rename
failure_scenario: No runtime failure, but the outdated comment at lines 380-383 ('self.POST, set self._post and self._file to prevent attempts to parse POST data again') misleads future maintainers about the actual attributes (self.data, self._data, self._files) that _mark_post_parse_error sets.

summary: Missing `await` on `testAsyncParams(bidRequests.rubicon)` — async assertions for rubicon's PAAPI navigator wrappers are a floating promise and may not complete before the test finishes
failure_scenario: If rubicon's `paapi.createAuctionNonce` or `paapi.getInterestGroupAdAuctionData` wrappers are broken (e.g., wrong args forwarded to navigator), the test passes anyway because the un-awaited promise's assertions are never guaranteed to execute before Mocha considers the test done. The sinon stubs in `testAsyncParams` could assert failure after the test already passed.

summary: Adding `'serverResponse'` to `ASYNC_SIGNALS` makes it replacified by a Promise in `makeDeferrals`, changing the behavior for any adapter that provides `serverResponse` in `buildPAAPIConfigs` — it was previously used as-is, now it gets async resolution
failure_scenario: An adapter that returns `{serverResponse: {data: 'value'}}` from `buildPAAPIConfigs` would previously get that value directly in the auction config. After this change, `serverResponse` is replaced by a Promise that resolves to `null` (unless a matching `interpretResponse` supplies a value). If no response-side config provides `serverResponse`, the adapter's value is silently dropped. No specific test was added to validate this new signal's behavior.

summary: Unused import `buildActivityParams` from `../../../src/activities/params.js` — imported in the diff but never referenced anywhere in the test file
failure_scenario: The import adds an unnecessary dependency on `src/activities/params.js`. If that module is removed or renamed, the test file will fail to parse even though it never uses the import. This is dead code introduced by the changeset.

summary: `.values(input)` passes a nested wrapper object `{ projectId, settings: {...} }` instead of flattened column values, causing the insert to only set projectId and drop the settings data on first insert
failure_scenario: User edits project commands in settings UI, saves → client calls upsert with `{projectId: "abc", settings: {projectId: "abc", runCommand: "yarn dev", ...}}` → Drizzle's `.values(input)` sees only `projectId` as a matching column, ignores the `settings` key entirely → first insert creates a row with `run_command='', build_command='', install_command=''` (all defaults) → `returning()` returns this broken row → on next page load, `restoreProjectSettings` fetches the broken row → user's saved commands are overwritten with empty strings

summary: `createCommit` sets `this.isSaving = true` then falls through the try block without any commit logic and without returning a result, causing the function to return `undefined` — all callers interpret `undefined` as a failure
failure_scenario: User clicks 'New backup' button → `createCommit()` runs → `isSaving` guard passes → `isSaving = true` → no actual commit creation happens → try block ends → finally sets `isSaving = false` → function returns `undefined` → caller checks `!res?.success` → `!undefined?.success` is `true` → caller logs error and shows failure toast 'Failed to create commit'

summary: Fallback chain duplicates `domainsManager.domains.preview?.url` twice instead of falling through to `domainsManager.domains.custom?.url`; custom domain URL is never used as a fallback
failure_scenario: Project has a published custom domain with no preview domain → `baseUrl` resolves to `project?.sandbox.url` (the sandbox URL) since both preview references are null → page metadata saves the sandbox URL instead of the user-visible custom domain → OpenGraph metadata points visitors to the sandbox URL instead of the published custom domain

summary: When `baseUrl` is `undefined`, `baseUrl?.startsWith('http')` returns `undefined` (falsy), constructing `"https://undefined"` which is truthy, so `new URL("https://undefined")` creates a URL with hostname "undefined"
failure_scenario: New project with no domains configured (no preview, no custom, no sandbox) → `baseUrl` is `undefined` → url becomes `"https://undefined"` → `new URL("https://undefined")` succeeds with hostname "undefined" → `metadataBase` saved as `new URL('https://undefined')` → generated code exports `metadataBase: new URL("https://undefined")` which is a corrupt metadata value

summary: Same URL-from-undefined pattern as site/index.tsx: when `baseUrl` is `undefined`, produces `new URL("https://undefined")`
failure_scenario: Same as site/index.tsx — corrupt `metadataBase` when no domain URL is available for a page's metadata

summary: `useEffect` resets `title` and `description` to `initialMetadata` values whenever `initialMetadata` reference changes, silently overwriting in-progress user edits regardless of the `isDirty` flag
failure_scenario: User types a new title into the metadata form → parent component re-renders, creating a new `initialMetadata` object reference (with the same values) → `useEffect` fires → `setTitle` and `setDescription` are called with the original values → user's unsaved edit is silently discarded → user sees their typed text replaced with the old value mid-typing

summary: `checkoutCommit` shows toast.success('Restored to backup!') and returns `true` after `createCommit` succeeds, but never actually checks out or restores any commit — the restore functionality is marked `// TODO: Implement`
failure_scenario: User selects a backup to restore → `checkoutCommit` is called → `createCommit` returns success (once fixed) → toast shows 'Restored to backup!' → method returns `true` → no actual checkout or file restoration occurs → user believes their project was restored but nothing changed

summary: `skipBuild: false` was removed from custom domain deployment options but remains in preview domain section — if the deploy service defaults `skipBuild` to `true`, custom domain deployments would skip the build step
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Publish to custom domain' with a hosting provider where `skipBuild` defaults to `true` → build step is skipped for custom domain deployment → stale previously-built files are deployed to the live custom domain → meanwhile preview domain deploys fresh content (since `skipBuild: false` is still present there) → production site runs old content while preview shows new content

summary: Function signature changed from model_uri to model_path and _download_artifact_from_uri call was removed, but all callers still pass URIs (file:// or runs:/), causing os.path.exists to fail on malformed paths
failure_scenario: Test test_log_model_with_code_paths calls _compare_logged_code_paths(__file__, model_uri, ...) where model_uri = mlflow.get_artifact_uri('model') returns a file://... URI. The function now does os.path.join('file:///path/to/model', 'MLmodel') which produces 'file:///path/to/model/MLmodel' -- a path that does not exist on disk.
